Peterson started the 2006 season off strong, rushing for an average of over 150 yards per game and scoring nine total touchdowns over five games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Peterson 2006 Game Log (Games 1–5) |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adrian-peterson-1/gamelog/2006/#25-29-sum:gamelog |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224054632/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adrian-peterson-1/gamelog/2006/#25-29-sum:gamelog |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Peterson's father, Nelson, was released from prison during the [[2006 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2006 college football season]] and was able to watch his son as a spectator for the first time on October 14,<ref name="Conversation"/> when Oklahoma played [[2006 Iowa State Cyclones football team|Iowa State]]. Oklahoma defeated Iowa State in that game; however, on the final drive for the Sooners, Peterson broke his [[collar bone]] when he dove into the end zone on a 53-yard touchdown run.<ref name="Return"/> During a press conference on October 18, Peterson said he was told by doctors to expect to be out for 4–6 weeks.<ref name="injury">{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Scott |date=October 18, 2006 |title=Peterson discusses injury |url=http://www.newsok.com/article/2957901 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061029133705/http://newsok.com/article/2957901 |archive-date=October 29, 2006 |access-date=October 19, 2006 |website=[[The Oklahoman]]}}</ref> At the time of the injury, Peterson needed only to gain 150 yards to pass [[Billy Sims]] as the University of Oklahoma's all-time leading rusher.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2006 |title=Stoops: Peterson Broke Collarbone |url=https://soonersports.com/news/2006/10/14/208383419 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071016155644/http://soonersports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/101406aaa.html |archive-date=October 16, 2007 |access-date=September 23, 2007 |website=SoonerSports.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He was unable to return for the rest of the Sooners' regular season and missed seven games. ==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
On January 15, 2007, Peterson declared that he would forego his senior year of college and enter the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref name="Sooners">{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2007 |title=Peterson to Enter 2007 NFL Draft |url=http://www.soonersports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011507aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071007165925/http://www.soonersports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011507aaa.html |archive-date=October 7, 2007 |access-date=August 21, 2007 |publisher=University of Oklahoma and CSTV}}</ref> Coming into the league, he was known as a tall, upright runner possessing a rare combination of speed, strength, agility, size, and vision, along with a highly aggressive running style.<ref name="VikingUpdate"/> His rare talent as both a great breakaway and power runner has often raised comparisons to past legends, including [[Eric Dickerson]], [[Walter Payton]], [[Gale Sayers]], [[O. J. Simpson]], [[Franco Harris]], and [[Jim Brown]].<ref name="Record">{{Cite web |last=Visser |first=Leslie |date=November 7, 2007 |title=Peterson rewriting the rookie record book 'All Day' long |url=http://www.sportsline.com/nfl/story/10458554 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071109234921/http://www.sportsline.com/nfl/story/10458554 |archive-date=November 9, 2007 |publisher=[[CBS Sportsline.com]]}}</ref> Concerns about his injuries suffered during college were noted by the media and potential NFL teams.<ref name="HomeRun">{{Cite web |last=Weisman |first=Larry |date=August 7, 2007 |title=Is Peterson a home run hitter for Vikings? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/vikings/2007-08-07-adrian-peterson_N.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081201185003/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/vikings/2007-08-07-adrian-peterson_N.htm |archive-date=December 1, 2008 |access-date=August 24, 2007 |website=USA Today}}</ref><ref name="Conversation"/><ref name="RunsAnger"/><ref name="Banks"/> He started 22 out of 31 games in his college career and had a dislocated shoulder his first year (although he did not miss any games), a high ankle sprain his sophomore year, and a broken collarbone his final year at Oklahoma.<ref name="HomeRun"/> His durability was a consideration for at least two teams in their draft analysis,<ref name="Banks">{{Cite web |last=Banks |first=Don |date=May 21, 2007 |title=Teams wary of Peterson's health |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/writers/don_banks/04/25/peterson/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070826010301/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/writers/don_banks/04/25/peterson/index.html |archive-date=August 26, 2007 |access-date=August 25, 2007 |website=CNN Sports Illustrated}}</ref> which impacted selection position. Prior to the 2007 NFL Draft, Peterson was compared by professional football [[Scout (sport)|scouts]] to Eric Dickerson.<ref name="WCCO">{{Cite web |last=Max |first=Mike |date=May 21, 2007 |title=Adrian Peterson Credits Family For Success |url=http://wcco.com/sports/local_story_141101828.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927004604/http://wcco.com/sports/local_story_141101828.html |archive-date=September 27, 2007 |access-date=August 25, 2007 |publisher=[[WCCO-TV]]}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
====2007 season====

{{see also|2007 Minnesota Vikings season}}
On April 28, 2007, Peterson was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the first round with the seventh overall pick of the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103015035/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |archive-date=November 3, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Peterson was the first running back selected and the first of three Oklahoma Sooners to be drafted in the 2007 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oklahoma Drafted Players/Alumni |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915221757/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/ |archive-date=September 15, 2019 |access-date=August 1, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> At a press conference during the draft, Peterson announced, "My collarbone, I would say it's 90% healed. A lot of teams know that, and I don't see it stopping me from being prepared for the season."<ref name="Draft">{{Cite web |last=Pedulla |first=Tom |date=April 29, 2007 |title=Vikings' Peterson confident he can contribute |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/vikings/2007-04-29-adrian-peterson_N.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070817134820/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/vikings/2007-04-29-adrian-peterson_N.htm |archive-date=August 17, 2007 |access-date=August 25, 2007 |website=USA Today}}</ref>

Peterson believed he was a player that a franchise could build around. In an interview with ''[[IGN]]'' following the NFL Draft, he said, "I'm a player who is coming in with the determination to turn a team around. I want to help my team get to the playoffs, win...and run wild. I want to bring people to the stands. I want people to come to the game to see what I can do next. Things like that can change the whole attitude of an organization. I want to win."<ref name="IGN">{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Jon |date=May 4, 2007 |title=Adrian Peterson Interview |url=http://sports.ign.com/articles/785/785800p1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070820180622/http://sports.ign.com/articles/785/785800p1.html |archive-date=August 20, 2007 |access-date=August 26, 2007 |publisher=IGN}}</ref> He later told the ''[[Star Tribune]]'' in an interview, "I want to be the best player to ever play this game."<ref name="Fire">{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=November 4, 2007 |title=At home, Vikings star can put his fire on ice |url=http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1526216.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071104160939/http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1526216.html |archive-date=November 4, 2007 |access-date=November 4, 2007 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> Nearly three months after being drafted, he was signed by the Vikings on July 29, 2007. His contract was worth [[United States dollar|$]]40.5 million over five years, with $17 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pasquarelli |first=Len |author-link=Len Pasquarelli |date=July 29, 2007 |title=Vikings agree to five-year deal with top pick Peterson |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2953541 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107055534/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=2953541 |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=July 29, 2007 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Peterson began his outstanding rookie year with high expectations for himself; he announced ambitious goals including being named [[National Football League Rookie of the Year Award|NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]] and rushing for over 1,300 yards during the course of the year. Just 11 weeks into his rookie season with the Vikings, Peterson was well on his way to Dickerson's record and considered one of the elite running backs in the NFL.<ref name="BestBacks">{{Cite web |last=Salisbury |first=Sean |date=November 7, 2007 |title=Is Adrian Peterson the best back in football? |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3095687 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071110142715/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3095687 |archive-date=November 10, 2007 |access-date=November 8, 2007 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On September 9, 2007, Peterson ran for 103 yards on 19 carries in his first NFL regular season game against the [[2007 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].<ref name="2007Wk1">{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2007 |title=National Football League Game Summary: Atlanta Falcons At Minnesota Vikings |url=http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/29201/MIN_Gamebook.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071129091951/http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/29201/MIN_Gamebook.pdf |archive-date=November 29, 2007 |access-date=September 23, 2007 |publisher=National Football League}}</ref> In addition to his rushing yardage, he scored his first professional football touchdown on a 60-yard pass reception from quarterback [[Tarvaris Jackson]].<ref name="2007Wk1"/> Over his first three regular season games, his 431 yards (271 rushing and 160 receiving) from [[Line of scrimmage|scrimmage]] are a team record.<ref name="Teammates">{{Cite web |last=Zulgad |first=Judd |date=September 25, 2007 |title=Teammates want to keep 'All Day' fresh for all season |url=http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1443725.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071016171643/http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1443725.html |archive-date=October 16, 2007 |access-date=September 26, 2007 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> For his performance in the three games, Peterson received the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month award for both September and October 2007.<ref name="RookieOfMonth">{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2007 |title=Peterson named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month for September |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=3048261 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107055553/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=3048261 |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=October 6, 2007 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name="2009MediaGuide">{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings 2009 Media Guide |url=https://res.cloudinary.com/nflclubs/image/upload/vikings/nbf7p0d1frujlo8donve.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210905215340/https://res.cloudinary.com/nflclubs/image/upload/vikings/nbf7p0d1frujlo8donve.pdf |archive-date=September 5, 2021 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=Minnesota Vikings}}</ref>

His breakout game as a professional came on October 14, 2007, against the [[2007 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], highlighted by a three-touchdown performance and a then-franchise record of 224 rushing yards on 20 carries.<ref name="TooMuch">{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=October 15, 2007 |title=Image of Vikings' bumbling offense fades on this day |url=http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1483851.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015125832/http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1483851.html |archive-date=October 15, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2007 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> Peterson established additional team records for a rookie during this game, which included the most 100-yard games rushing and the longest touchdown run from scrimmage.<ref name="dazzle">{{Cite web |last=Zulgad |first=Judd |date=October 14, 2007 |title=Peterson show dazzles Bears ... and Vikings |url=http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1484412.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015095259/http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1484412.html |archive-date=October 15, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2007 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> He also set an NFL rookie record with 361 all-purpose yards in a single game. His 607 rushing yards through the first five games of the season is second in NFL history to Eric Dickerson.<ref name="Impression">{{Cite web |last=Chadiha |first=Jeffri |author-link=Jeffri Chadiha |date=October 18, 2007 |title=Quick impression: Vikes' Peterson eyes record season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=chadiha_jeffri&id=3068586 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071020044117/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=chadiha_jeffri&id=3068586 |archive-date=October 20, 2007 |access-date=October 21, 2007 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> For his performance, he was named the Offensive Player of the Week for the first time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Week 6 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_6.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023830/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/week_6.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Following Peterson's record performance, [[Deion Sanders]], now an [[NFL Network]] analyst, said about him: "He has the vision of a [[Marshall Faulk]], the power of an [[Earl Campbell]], and the speed of an Eric Dickerson. Let's pray he has the endurance of an [[Emmitt Smith]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=October 18, 2007 |title=PLAYER OF THE WEEK: Rookie Peterson off to a sensational start for Vikings |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/2007-10-18-1869254474_x.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071021064619/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/2007-10-18-1869254474_x.htm |archive-date=October 21, 2007 |access-date=October 21, 2007 |website=USA Today |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He has also been compared to Walter Payton and [[Tony Dorsett]] by ''Star Tribune'' [[sports journalist]] Jim Souhan.<ref name="onekind">{{Cite web |last=Souhan |first=Jim |date=October 20, 2007 |title=Peterson is one of a kind |url=http://www.startribune.com/souhan/story/1496087.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071022030526/http://www.startribune.com/souhan/story/1496087.html |archive-date=October 22, 2007 |access-date=October 25, 2007 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref>

Three weeks later, on November 4, 2007, Peterson broke his own franchise record as well as the NFL single game rushing yard record (previously held by [[Jamal Lewis (American football)|Jamal Lewis]] since 2003) when he rushed for 296 yards on 30 carries and three rushing touchdowns against the [[2007 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] in a home game in [[Minneapolis]].<ref [[File:Adrian L. Peterson before 2008 Pro Bowl.JPEG|thumb|Peterson was named MVP of the [[2008 Pro Bowl]]]]
In honor of Peterson's record-breaking performance against the [[San Diego Chargers]], the jersey he wore that day was sent to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2007 |title=Peterson gives historic uniform to HOF |url=https://www.profootballhof.com/news/peterson-gives-historic-uniform-to-hof/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416172156/https://www.profootballhof.com/news/peterson-gives-historic-uniform-to-hof/ |archive-date=April 16, 2019 |access-date=August 16, 2019 |website=Pro Football Hall of Fame}}</ref> On November 11, 2007, just a week later, Peterson injured the [[Fibular collateral ligament|lateral collateral ligament]] in his right knee in a game against the [[2007 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]].<ref name="LCL">{{Cite news |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=November 12, 2007 |title=Vikings: Good news out of a bad collision |work=Star Tribune |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/11826756.html |url-status=dead |access-date=December 8, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071216043804/http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/11826756.html |archive-date=December 16, 2007}}</ref> The injury occurred in the third quarter of a 34–0 defeat at [[Lambeau Field]] on a low tackle by Packers [[cornerback]] [[Al Harris (cornerback)|Al Harris]].<ref name="LCL"/> Almost a month after the injury, Peterson returned to action on December 2, 2007, against the [[2007 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] scoring two touchdowns and rushing for 116 yards.<ref name="Lions">{{Cite news |last=Krawczynski |first=Jon |date=December 2, 2007 |title=Adrian's back as Vikings surge to big victory |work=Star Tribune |url=http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1586645.html |url-status=dead |access-date=December 2, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071204001433/http://www.startribune.com/vikings/story/1586645.html |archive-date=December 4, 2007}}</ref>

On December 18, he was named as the starting running back for the 2008 NFC Pro Bowl team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/probowl.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120624135926/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/probowl.htm |archive-date=June 24, 2012 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On January 2, he was named The [[Associated Press]] NFL Offensive [[Rookie of the Year (award)|Rookie of the Year]].<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite news |date=January 2, 2008 |title=Vikings' Peterson with runaway performance on field, and in voting |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3177185 |url-status=live |access-date=January 2, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080105025710/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3177185 |archive-date=January 5, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AP Offensive Rookie of the Year Winners |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/ap-offensive-rookie-of-the-year-award.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116080408/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/ap-offensive-rookie-of-the-year-award.htm |archive-date=November 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was named to the [[Pro Football Writers Association]] All-Rookie Team for the 2007 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2007.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023400/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2007.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On February 10, 2008, Peterson won the 2008 NFL [[Pro Bowl MVP]] award with 16 carries for 129 rushing yards along with two touchdowns. The 129 rushing yards was the second most in [[Pro Bowl]] history. He was the first rookie since Marshall Faulk in 1994 to win the Pro Bowl MVP award.<ref name="OwensPeterson">{{Cite web |last=Wilner |first=Barry |date=February 10, 2008 |title=Owens, Peterson Lead NFC Comeback |url=https://www.pottsmerc.com/2008/02/11/owens-peterson-lead-nfc-comeback/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429185749/https://www.pottsmerc.com/2008/02/11/owens-peterson-lead-nfc-comeback/ |archive-date=April 29, 2022 |access-date=February 11, 2008 |website=The Mercury}}</ref> Peterson and Faulk are currently the only NFL players to win both the NFL Pro Bowl MVP and Rookie of the Year awards in the same year. Peterson finished in second place in rushing yards (1,341) in the 2007 season behind [[LaDainian Tomlinson]], who finished with 1,474 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/leaders.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218210643/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/leaders.htm |archive-date=December 18, 2008 |access-date=October 17, 2008 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He also caught 19 passes for 268 yards and returned 16 kickoffs for 412, giving him 2,021 all-purpose yards (6th in the NFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Peterson Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01.htm |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |access-date=January 30, 2019 |archive-date=January 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190131181842/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2008 season====

{{see also|2008 Minnesota Vikings season}}

[[File:20090104 Adrian Peterson (28).JPG|thumb|Peterson in a 2008 NFC Wild Card game against the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]]]]
Peterson and the Vikings entered the 2008 season with high expectations and as he did during his rookie season, Peterson set high goals for himself including a 2,000-yard campaign and the NFL MVP award.<ref name="StarTrib">{{Cite web |last=Zulgad |first=Judd |date=May 16, 2008 |title=2,000 yards? MVP award? Peterson sets sights on the highest levels |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/18994284.html?location_refer=Vikings |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080517194450/http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/18994284.html?location_refer=Vikings |archive-date=May 17, 2008 |access-date=September 1, 2008 |website=[[Star Tribune]]}}</ref> Questions remained as to Peterson's durability and the ability of the Vikings offense to take the focus of opposing defenses off Peterson.<ref>{{cite web | title=Conference call: Vikings head coach Brad Childress | website=TennesseeTitans.com | date=September 24, 2008 | url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/conference-call-vikings-head-coach-brad-childress-443350 | access-date=January 2, 2026}}</ref>

Peterson had a phenomenal second season. He played in all 16 games, of which he started 15. He recorded ten games going over 100 rushing yards to go along with ten rushing touchdowns across the season. His Week 10 performance against the [[2008 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] earned him his third career Offensive Player of the Week nod.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Week 10 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/week_10.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023013/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/week_10.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Peterson finished [[List of NFL rushing champions|leading the league in rushing]] with 1,760 yards,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Peterson 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2008/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811182926/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2008/ |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=Brian |date=December 27, 2008 |title=Vikings' Adrian Peterson finishes season as NFL's top rusher with 1,760 yards (and nine fumbles) |url=https://www.twincities.com/2008/12/27/vikings-adrian-peterson-finishes-season-as-nfls-top-rusher-with-1760-yards-and-nine-fumbles/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211115214708/https://www.twincities.com/2008/12/27/vikings-adrian-peterson-finishes-season-as-nfls-top-rusher-with-1760-yards-and-nine-fumbles/ |archive-date=November 15, 2021 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |website=Twin Cities}}</ref> which marks the third-most yards in a sophomore season behind [[Eric Dickerson]]'s 2,105 yard season, and [[Chris Johnson (running back)|Chris Johnson's]] 2,006-yard season, which occurred the following season in 2009. In Peterson's first 30 games, he had 3,101 yards, which marks the third best start to a career for running backs behind Dickerson with 3,600 yards and [[Jim Brown]] with 3,144 yards. He became the fourth running back to lead the league in yards per game in his first two seasons along with Brown, [[Earl Campbell]], and Dickerson. In recognition of his 2008 season, he was named the recipient of the [[Bert Bell Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bert Bell Award (Player of the Year) Winners |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/bert-bell-award.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821031638/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/bert-bell-award.htm |archive-date=August 21, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On January 14, 2009, Peterson was named to his second AP [[All-Pro]] team in two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/allpro.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023905/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/allpro.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

The Vikings made the playoffs with a 10–6 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127084032/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/ |archive-date=January 27, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In his playoff debut, Peterson had 83 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in a 26–14 loss to the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in the [[2008–09 NFL playoffs#NFC: Philadelphia Eagles 26, Minnesota Vikings 14|Wild Card Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Philadelphia Eagles at Minnesota Vikings – January 4th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901040min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224193306/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200901040min.htm |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2009 season====
[[File:AP 2009.JPG|thumb|Peterson following a week 10 win over the Detroit Lions, which he ran for 133 yards and 2 touchdowns]]
{{see also|2009 Minnesota Vikings season}}

Prior to the start of the 2009 season, analysts on [[ESPN]] and [[Scout.com]] considered Peterson as one of the league's top running backs.<ref>{{cite web | title=Team Preview: Minnesota Vikings | website=ESPN.com | date=September 9, 2009 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/preview09/team?team=min | access-date=January 2, 2026}}</ref> However, the arrival of quarterback [[Brett Favre]], one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, coming out of retirement brought both expectation and speculation about Peterson's new role in the offense.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Mortensen |first1=Chris |author-link=Chris Mortensen |last2=Schefter |first2=Adam |author-link2=Adam Schefter |last3=Werder |first3=Ed |author-link3=Ed Werder |last4=Carter |first4=Cris |author-link4=Cris Carter |last5=Seifert |first5=Kevin |date=August 18, 2009 |title=Purple reign: Indecisive Favre signs with Vikings |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4406963 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110022121/http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4406963 |archive-date=January 10, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Head coach [[Brad Childress]], however, stated that he wanted to continue leaning on Peterson, giving him a large number of carries. Favre worked well into the offense through the first half of the season, re-establishing Peterson's ability with a passing attack. Peterson had 917 rushing yards through Week 10, while the Vikings had a record of 8–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Minnesota Vikings Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2009.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131200822/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2009.htm |archive-date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Peterson opened the season by rushing for 180 yards on 25 carries and three touchdowns against the [[2009 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], setting a new Vikings franchise record for rushing in the season opener.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Cleveland Browns – September 13th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200909130cle.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811222057/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200909130cle.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He again broke the hundred-yard barrier in Week 6 against the [[2009 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], with 143 yards and 22 carries. His next 100-yard effort came against the [[2009 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]], with 133 yards on 18 carries,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Minnesota Vikings – October 18th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200910180min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811222155/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200910180min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> and he was named the FedEx Ground Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 20, 2009 |title=Favre, Peterson Win Weekly NFL.com Awards |work=NFL.com |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Favre-Peterson-Win-Weekly-NFLcom-Awards/16bdb88f-2fdc-42a3-bb88-70fdb1e60b1d |url-status=dead |access-date=February 23, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224053317/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Favre-Peterson-Win-Weekly-NFLcom-Awards/16bdb88f-2fdc-42a3-bb88-70fdb1e60b1d |archive-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> Overall, he finished the season with 1,383 rushing yards and a league-high 18 rushing touchdowns to go along with a career-high 43 receptions for 436 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Peterson 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023639/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2009/ |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Rushing & Receiving |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/rushing.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224053000/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/rushing.htm |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In the playoffs, Peterson had 63 rushing yards and a 19-yard reception as Minnesota defeated the [[2009 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] by a score of 34–3 in the [[2009–10 NFL playoffs#NFC: Minnesota Vikings 34, Dallas Cowboys 3|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Dallas Cowboys at Minnesota Vikings – January 17th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001170min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811183348/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001170min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> However, they lost to the eventual [[Super Bowl XLIV]] champion [[2009 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] in the [[2009–10 NFL playoffs#NFC: New Orleans Saints 31, Minnesota Vikings 28 (OT)|NFC Championship]] in overtime by a score of 31–28. Peterson rushed for 122 yards and three touchdowns in the loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship – Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints – January 24th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001240nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811222543/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001240nor.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Peterson was voted to his third consecutive Pro Bowl on December 29. He was the starting running back for the NFC team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/probowl.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821031640/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/probowl.htm |archive-date=August 21, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> For the second consecutive season, he was named as a first-team All-Pro.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/allpro.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316084702/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/allpro.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2011 season====
{{see also|2011 Minnesota Vikings season}}
On September 10, 2011, the Vikings signed Peterson for $96 million over the course of seven seasons, making him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gates |first=Christopher |date=September 10, 2011 |title=Schefter: Peterson Contract Extension Worth $96 Million, $32 Million Guaranteed |url=https://minnesota.sbnation.com/minnesota-vikings/2011/9/10/2416895/adam-schefter-adrian-peterson-contract-extension |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801142925/https://minnesota.sbnation.com/minnesota-vikings/2011/9/10/2416895/adam-schefter-adrian-peterson-contract-extension |archive-date=August 1, 2019 |access-date=August 1, 2019 |website=SB Nation Minnesota}}</ref> Peterson reached the 6,000-yard milestone on September 18, 2011, in a loss to the [[2011 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Minnesota Vikings – September 18th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109180min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811215101/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109180min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On October 9, Peterson scored three touchdowns in the first quarter against the [[2011 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at Minnesota Vikings – October 9th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110090min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811215103/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110090min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> setting a new franchise record. He later earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for his performance during the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiederer |first=Dan |date=October 11, 2011 |title=Adrian Peterson named NFC Offensive Player of the Week |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/blogs/131555078.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013023601/http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/blogs/131555078.html |archive-date=October 13, 2011 |access-date=August 15, 2019 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Week 5 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/week_5.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316023828/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/week_5.htm |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>
In a Week 10 game against the [[2011 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]], Peterson suffered a high ankle sprain late in the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Yoder |first=Will |date=November 21, 2011 |title=Vikings Adrian Peterson Has High Ankle Sprain |url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2011/11/22/vikings-adrian-peterson-has-high-ankle-sprain |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117212531/https://www.si.com/si-wire/2011/11/22/vikings-adrian-peterson-has-high-ankle-sprain |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> He was later ruled out for their Week 11 game against the [[2011 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 27, 2011 |title=Vikings downgrade Peterson to out vs. Falcons |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7281473/adrian-peterson-minnesota-vikings-ruled-vs-atlanta-falcons |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224112959/http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7281473/adrian-peterson-minnesota-vikings-ruled-vs-atlanta-falcons |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

[[File:Adrian Peterson.jpg|thumb|Peterson in 2011]]
On December 24, Peterson was injured by safety [[DeJon Gomes]] and needed help off the field in a Week 16 game against the [[2011 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Langford |first=Richard |date=December 24, 2011 |title=Adrian Peterson Injury: Blow to Knee Will Likely End Frustrating Season for Star |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/996865-adrian-peterson-injury-blow-to-knee-will-likely-end-frustrating-season-for-star |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190816132001/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/996865-adrian-peterson-injury-blow-to-knee-will-likely-end-frustrating-season-for-star |archive-date=August 16, 2019 |access-date=August 16, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On December 26, he was placed on [[injured reserve]] having suffered a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burke |first=Chris |date=December 26, 2011 |title=Week 16 injuries: Adrian Peterson facing lengthy rehab |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/audibles/2011/12/26/week-16-injuries-adrian-peterson-facing-lengthy-rehab |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224112946/https://www.si.com/nfl/audibles/2011/12/26/week-16-injuries-adrian-peterson-facing-lengthy-rehab |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

In the 2011 season, Peterson had 208 carries for 970 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns to go along with 18 receptions for 139 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Peterson 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811182747/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PeteAd01/gamelog/2011 |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was ranked eighth by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2012]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2012-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211112163739/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2012-nfl-top-100.htm |archive-date=November 12, 2021 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2012 season: MVP season====

{{see also|2012 Minnesota Vikings season}}

====2016 season====

{{see also|2016 Minnesota Vikings season}}

Peterson started the 2016 season quietly with only 31 rushing yards on 19 carries in a 25–16 win over the [[2016 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Tennessee Titans – September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110oti.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106173140/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110oti.htm |archive-date=January 6, 2018 |access-date=February 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> With the Vikings playing the first ever regular season game at [[U.S. Bank Stadium]] in Week 2 against the [[2016 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', Peterson rushed for 19 yards until leaving the game with an apparent right knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings – September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811222448/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The next day, it was revealed that the right knee had a [[Meniscus tear|torn meniscus]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=September 19, 2016 |title=Adrian Peterson has torn meniscus. |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/zimmer-announces-adrian-peterson-has-torn-meniscus-0ap3000000705771 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920185426/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000705771/article/zimmer-announces-adrian-peterson-has-torn-meniscus |archive-date=September 20, 2016 |access-date=September 19, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=September 21, 2016 |title=Will this be Adrian Peterson's last stand in Minnesota? |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/will-this-be-adrian-peterson-s-last-stand-in-minnesota-0ap3000000707086 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160922141412/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000707086/article/will-this-be-adrian-petersons-last-stand-in-minnesota |archive-date=September 22, 2016 |access-date=September 21, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On September 22, Peterson underwent successful surgery to repair the meniscus. It was also revealed that the knee had a mild [[Fibular collateral ligament|LCL]] sprain, but it did not need surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=September 22, 2016 |title=Adrian Peterson undergoes successful knee surgery |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adrian-peterson-undergoes-successful-knee-surgery-0ap3000000706867 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923122512/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000706867/article/adrian-peterson-undergoes-successful-knee-surgery |archive-date=September 23, 2016 |access-date=September 22, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 23, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Vikings put Adrian Peterson on injured reserve |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/vikings-put-adrian-peterson-on-injured-reserve |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924101308/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/09/23/vikings-put-adrian-peterson-on-injured-reserve/ |archive-date=September 24, 2016 |access-date=January 2, 2026 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> On December 17, the Vikings activated Peterson to the active roster. He returned to action in Week 15 against the [[2016 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings – December 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811222303/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=August 11, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=December 17, 2016 |title=Vikings activate RB Adrian Peterson (knee) from IR |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adrian-peterson-will-start-for-minnesota-vikings-vs-colts-0ap3000000757929 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161219085416/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000757929/article/vikings-activate-rb-adrian-peterson-from-injured-reserve |archive-date=December 19, 2016 |access-date=December 17, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Despite only playing three games, Peterson was still ranked 98th by his peers on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2017]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106081444/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |archive-date=November 6, 2020 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On February 28, 2017, the Vikings announced that they would not exercise Peterson's 2017 option on his contract, making him a free agent at the start of the 2017 league year. Had the Vikings exercised the option, they would have had to pay him $18 million for the 2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2017 |title=Vikings Will Not Exercise 2017 Option on Adrian Peterson's Contract |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Will-Not-Exercise-2017-Option-on-Adrian-Petersons-Contract/3b48ded0-579e-4c29-8b01-154afe57c263?sf59216852=1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170301120109/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Will-Not-Exercise-2017-Option-on-Adrian-Petersons-Contract/3b48ded0-579e-4c29-8b01-154afe57c263?sf59216852=1 |archive-date=March 1, 2017 |access-date=March 1, 2017 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> Peterson's tenure with the Vikings ended with him leading the NFL in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns during that time period from the 2007 season to the 2016 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most Rushing Yards From 2007 To 2016 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-rushing-yards-from-2007-to-2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429151518/https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-rushing-yards-from-2007-to-2016 |archive-date=April 29, 2022 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=StatMuse}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===

{{see also|2017 New Orleans Saints season}}

On April 25, 2017, Peterson signed a two-year, $7 million contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]], which included a $2.5 million signing bonus.<ref name="Saints">{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2017 |title=Saints Agree to Terms with RB Adrian Peterson on a Two-Year Contract |url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/Saints-Agree-to-Terms-with-RB-Adrian-Peterson-on-a-Two-Year-Contract/ad8b607f-116c-4d0b-b397-a37ed2c596dc |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427002913/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/Saints-Agree-to-Terms-with-RB-Adrian-Peterson-on-a-Two-Year-Contract/ad8b607f-116c-4d0b-b397-a37ed2c596dc |archive-date=April 27, 2017 |access-date=July 23, 2019 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=April 25, 2017 |title=Adrian Peterson, Saints finalize two-year contract |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adrian-peterson-saints-finalize-two-year-contract-0ap3000000802102 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426052040/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000802102/article/adrian-peterson-saints-finalize-twoyear-contract |archive-date=April 26, 2017 |access-date=July 23, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Peterson played his first game with the Saints on September 11, 2017, against his former team, the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]]. [[File:Bills Defense.jpg|thumb|Peterson running against the [[2019 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] in 2019]]
On March 13, 2019, Peterson signed a two-year, $8 million contract to stay with the Washington Redskins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Redskins re-signing Adrian Peterson to two-year deal |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001022462/article/redskins-resigning-adrian-peterson-to-twoyear-deal |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190315035330/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001022462/article/redskins-resigning-adrian-peterson-to-twoyear-deal |archive-date=March 15, 2019 |access-date=August 16, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> After being a healthy scratch in Week 1, Peterson was slated to become the starter following a knee injury to starter [[Derrius Guice]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Chris |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Washington's Running Back Conflict Resolves Itself In Characteristically Grim, Destructive Fashion |url=https://deadspin.com/washingtons-running-back-conflict-resolves-itself-in-ch-1838085715 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190913204947/https://deadspin.com/washingtons-running-back-conflict-resolves-itself-in-ch-1838085715 |archive-date=September 13, 2019 |access-date=September 13, 2019 |website=deadspin.com}}</ref> He got the start in Week 2 against the [[2019 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]]. On December 15, against the [[2019 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]], Peterson passed [[Curtis Martin]] for fifth all-time in rushing yards, as well as becoming the tenth player in NFL history to reach 3,000 career rushing attempts and tied [[Walter Payton]] for fourth all-time in rushing touchdowns with 110.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stackpole |first=Kyle |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Adrian Peterson Passes Curtis Martin For Fifth On NFL's All-Time Rushing List |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/adrian-peterson-fifth-all-time-nfl-rushing-list-redskins-eagles |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714140249/https://www.redskins.com/news/adrian-peterson-fifth-all-time-nfl-rushing-list-redskins-eagles |archive-date=July 14, 2020 |access-date=December 20, 2019 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> Peterson finished the season with 211 carries for 898 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns while adding 17 receptions for 142 receiving yards. == Legal issues ==
On September 12, 2014, Peterson was indicted by a [[Montgomery County, Texas]], grand jury on charges of reckless or negligent injury to a child, after he had used a wooden implement to injure his 4-year-old son in [[Spring, Texas]], in May.<ref name="indicted">{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Ryan |date=September 12, 2014 |title=Report: Adrian Peterson indicted in child injury case in Texas |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24706732/report-adrian-peterson-indicted-in-child-injury-case-in-texas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140913011032/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24706732/report-adrian-peterson-indicted-in-child-injury-case-in-texas |archive-date=September 13, 2014 |access-date=September 12, 2014 |website=[[CBSSports.com]]}}</ref> The prosecution in the case alleged that Peterson used a tree branch to beat his son repeatedly on his back, buttocks, genitals, ankles, and legs. Peterson described the implement as a "[[Switch (corporal punishment)|switch]]",<ref name="indicted" /> a form of punishment that was used on Peterson in his own childhood.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peter |first=Josh |date=September 15, 2014 |title=Adrian Peterson's childhood friend shows tree where he says they picked out switches |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2014/09/adrian-peterson-childhood-friend-switch/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114161507/http://ftw.usatoday.com/2014/09/adrian-peterson-childhood-friend-switch |archive-date=January 14, 2015 |access-date=March 3, 2015 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Photos posted on ''[[TMZ.com]]'' showed his son's legs with slash-like wounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2014 |title=Adrian Peterson – Indicted for Child Abuse ... Doc Reported Injuries |url=http://www.tmz.com/2014/09/12/adrian-peterson-indicted-for-child-abuse/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140913032638/http://www.tmz.com/2014/09/12/adrian-peterson-indicted-for-child-abuse/ |archive-date=September 13, 2014 |access-date=September 12, 2014 |website=[[TMZ.com]]}}</ref> Peterson was subsequently deactivated for one game by the Vikings. Furthermore, he was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list for the remainder of the season.<ref name="beating-suspension-one-game">{{Cite web |last=Whitmer |first=Michael |date=September 12, 2014 |title=Adrian Peterson booked and released from jail |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/09/12/adrian-peterson-indicted-texas-grand-jury/gi9eXbtzoCTU8Zuh4FrLqK/story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140913013437/http://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/09/12/adrian-peterson-indicted-texas-grand-jury/gi9eXbtzoCTU8Zuh4FrLqK/story.html |archive-date=September 13, 2014 |access-date=September 13, 2014 |website=[[The Boston Globe]]}}</ref><ref name="Borzi" />

On November 4, 2014, Peterson pleaded [[no contest]] to the misdemeanor charge of recklessly assaulting his son. He avoided a jail sentence after reaching a plea agreement. Peterson was put on probation and also fined $4,000. He was also ordered to undergo 80 hours of community service.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2014 |title=NFL star Adrian Peterson admits reckless assault on son |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-29908856 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104212035/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-29908856 |archive-date=November 4, 2014 |access-date=November 4, 2014 |website=BBC News}}</ref> Peterson was suspended by the NFL. His 2014 season was over after arbitrator Shyam Das ruled in favor of the NFL on November 18, 2014, saying, "the league can keep Adrian Peterson on the commissioner's exempt list," effectively terminating any possibility the Minnesota Vikings running back would play again that season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2014 |title=Source: Peterson's season over after ruling |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11899414 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190731200801/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11899414 |archive-date=July 31, 2019 |access-date=July 31, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In December 2014, Harold Henderson, the NFL-appointed arbitrator for Peterson's appeal affirmed Peterson's unpaid suspension until at least spring 2015. However, the [[NFL Players Association]] said it was "considering immediate legal remedies" to the decision.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 13, 2014 |title=Adrian Peterson's appeal denied, suspension upheld |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/adrian-petersons-appeal-denied-suspension-upheld/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150111083803/http://www.foxnews.com/sports/2014/12/13/adrian-peterson-appeal-denied-suspension-upheld/ |archive-date=January 11, 2015 |access-date=December 31, 2014 |website=Fox News |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On August 4, 2016, [[ESPN]] reported that the NFL won an appeal in a case against Peterson, reversing a ruling which had overturned Peterson's suspension and fine.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 4, 2016 |title=NFL wins appeal in case against Adrian Peterson of Minnesota Vikings |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/17218215/nfl-wins-appeal-case-adrian-peterson-minnesota-vikings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806060621/http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/17218215/nfl-wins-appeal-case-adrian-peterson-minnesota-vikings |archive-date=August 6, 2016 |access-date=August 4, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In 2018, Peterson admitted that he was still using a belt to discipline his son.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keim |first=John |date=November 21, 2018 |title=Peterson says he still disciplines son 'with a belt' |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25342741 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190130220959/http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25342741 |archive-date=January 30, 2019 |access-date=January 30, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2018, Peterson was ordered to repay a Minnesota bank for defaulting on a 2016 loan. In 2018, DeAngelo Vehicle Sales LLC, a Pennsylvania loan company, sued Peterson after he defaulted on a 2016 loan and failed to make the full payment of $5.2 million by March 1, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maakaron |first=John |date=January 14, 2021 |title=Does Adrian Peterson Have Financial Issues? |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/adrian-peterson-defaults-on-loan |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130012758/https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/adrian-peterson-defaults-on-loan |archive-date=January 30, 2021 |access-date=February 3, 2021 |website=SI.com}}</ref> In 2019, Peterson reached a settlement agreement. '''Adrian Grady''' (born November 21, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive lineman]]. He was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in 2009. He played [[college football]] at [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]].

He was also a member of the [[New England Patriots]], [[St. Louis Rams]] and [[Hartford Colonials]].

==Early life==
Grady attended [[Coffee High School (Georgia)|Coffee High School]] in [[Douglas, Georgia]], where he played football as a defensive lineman and [[linebacker]]. He recorded 85 tackles as a sophomore defensive lineman before switching to linebacker as a junior; he missed the season with a leg injury. As a senior, he recorded 69 tackles and two sacks, earning second-team all-region honors.

==College career==
After graduating high school, Grady attended the [[University of Louisville]], where started two of the 12 games he played in as a true freshman in 2005. He played in eight games as a sophomore, starting two, picking up 16 tackles before suffering an injury. As a junior in 2007, Grady played in five games before suffering a season-ending injury. As a senior in 2008, he started 10 of 11 games, recording 41 tackles and two sacks.

==Professional career==

===Indianapolis Colts===
Grady was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] after going undrafted in the [[2009 NFL draft]]. He was waived by the Colts on September 5 during final cuts.

===New England Patriots (first stint)===
Grady was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New England Patriots]] on September 6, 2009. He was released by the Patriots on September 30.

===St. Louis Rams===
Grady was signed to the practice squad of the [[St. Louis Rams]] on October 7, 2009. He was released on October 12.

===New England Patriots (second stint)===
Grady was re-signed to the practice squad of the Patriots on November 17, 2009. He spent the remainder of the season on the practice squad and was re-signed to a future contract on January 12, 2010. He was waived by the Patriots on August 9, 2010.

'''Adrian Jarrell Clayborn''' (born July 6, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[University of Iowa]], and earned consensus [[All-American]] honors. He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the first round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. Clayborn also played for the [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[New England Patriots]]. With the Patriots, he won [[Super Bowl LIII]] over the [[Los Angeles Rams]]. Clayborn is one of 6 NFL players to record 6 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] in a game, doing so as a member of the Falcons in 2017.

==Early life==
Clayborn was born in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. At birth, he suffered from a condition known as [[Erb's Palsy]], something that is caused during birth by an injury to the nerves surrounding a child's shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=September 21, 2018 |title=Adrian Clayborn inspires by playing in NFL despite Erb's palsy |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4814990/adrian-clayborn-inspires-by-playing-in-nfl-despite-erbs-palsy |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709204705/https://www.espn.com/blog/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4814990/adrian-clayborn-inspires-by-playing-in-nfl-despite-erbs-palsy |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cox |first=Zack |date=March 21, 2018 |title=Adrian Clayborn's Erb's Palsy Limits Versatility But Not Productivity |url=https://nesn.com/2018/03/adrian-clayborns-erbs-palsy-limits-versatility-but-not-productivity/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=NESN.com |language=en-US |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709204736/https://nesn.com/2018/03/adrian-clayborns-erbs-palsy-limits-versatility-but-not-productivity/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Because his head and neck were pulled to the side as his shoulders passed through the birth canal, he suffered nerve damage resulting in the loss of some movement and weakness in his right arm.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morehouse |first=Marc |date=November 10, 2009 |title=Late bloomer Clayborn becoming dominant leader |url=http://thegazette.com/2009/11/06/late-bloomer-clayton-becoming-dominant-leader/ throughout his young life and eventually overcame the limitations caused by the disability.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 21, 2018 |title=New Patriots Defensive End Adrian Clayborn Hasn't Let Erb's Palsy News - Boston |language=en-US}}</ref>

When Adrian was 10, his older brother Anthony was shot and killed in northern St. Louis. He was survived by his seven children.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morehouse |first=Marc |date=August 10, 2010 |title=Spotlight on Adrian Clayborn: Close to it All |url=https://www.kcrg.com/sports/hawkeyes/Clayborn-Close-to-it-All-100147949.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314154427/http://www.kcrg.com/sports/hawkeyes/Clayborn-Close-to-it-All-100147949.html |archive-date=March 14, 2012 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |website=The Gazette}}</ref>

Clayborn attended high school at [[Webster Groves High School]], where he was a four-year [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[high school football|football]] and basketball.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 13, 2017 |title=Webster Groves High grad Adrian Clayborn has 6 sacks, Falcons romp past Cowboys 27-7 |url=http://www.ksdk.com/article/sports/nfl/webster-groves-high-grad-adrian-clayborn-has-6-sacks-falcons-romp-past-cowboys-27-7/63-491389071 |access-date=November 14, 2017 |website=KSDK |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708124014/https://www.ksdk.com/article/sports/nfl/webster-groves-high-grad-adrian-clayborn-has-6-sacks-falcons-romp-past-cowboys-27-7/63-491389071 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Clayborn was selected in the first round (20th overall) of the [[2011 NFL draft]] by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |access-date=February 26, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703032032/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Clayborn recorded his first sack in week 3 of the 2011 season against the [[2011 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]]. His sack on [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] also caused a fumble recovered by teammate [[Michael Bennett (defensive lineman, born 1985)|Michael Bennett]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - September 25th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109250tam.htm |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110225301/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109250tam.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the 2011 season with 7.5 sacks, 42 total tackles, and three forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708124013/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2012, Clayborn was placed on injured reserve after injuring his knee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucs' Adrian Clayborn out for season with knee injury |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bucs-adrian-clayborn-out-for-season-with-knee-injury-0ap1000000065853 |access-date=September 24, 2012 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=September 24, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120924215504/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000065853/article/bucs-adrian-clayborn-out-for-season-with-knee-injury?module=HP11_headline_stack |url-status=live }}</ref>  He played in three games on the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708062225/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2012/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the 2013 season, Clayborn had 5.5 sacks, 64 total tackles, one pass defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708182001/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Before the 2014 season, it was announced by new general manager [[Jason Licht]] that the Buccaneers would not be picking up the fifth year option on his rookie contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=April 23, 2014 |title=Bucs won't use fifth-year option on Adrian Clayborn |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bucs-wont-use-fifth-year-option-on-adrian-clayborn |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709184827/https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bucs-wont-use-fifth-year-option-on-adrian-clayborn |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also moved to the left side since the team signed [[Michael Johnson (defensive end)|Michael Johnson]] for the right side. He suffered yet another season-ending injury after playing in one game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708124014/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was placed him on IR and his future in Tampa in doubt since he would be an unrestricted free agent in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 12, 2014 |title=Adrian Clayborn heads to IR with biceps injury |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/adrian-clayborn-heads-to-ir-with-biceps-injury |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709184855/https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/adrian-clayborn-heads-to-ir-with-biceps-injury |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 17, 2018, Clayborn signed a two-year $10 million contract with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2018 |title=Patriots Sign Three Free Agents |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-three-free-agents-327361 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318072719/http://www.patriots.com/news/2018/03/17/patriots-sign-three-free-agents |archive-date=March 18, 2018 |access-date=March 18, 2018 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> In Clayborn's first season in New England, Clayborn recorded 11 tackles and 2.5 sacks in 14 games and one start.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122013707/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref> With Clayborn, the Patriots went on to win [[Super Bowl LIII]] 13–3 against the [[2018 Los Angeles Rams|Los Angeles Rams]] to give Clayborn his first championship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIII - Los Angeles Rams vs. New England Patriots - February 3rd, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201902030ram.htm |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204231138/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201902030ram.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 15, 2019, Clayborn was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cox |first=Zach |date=March 15, 2019 |title=Patriots Release Adrian Clayborn, Clear $4M In Salary Cap Space |url=https://nesn.com/2019/03/patriots-release-adrian-clayborn-clear-4m-in-salary-cap-space/ |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=NESN |archive-date=March 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190320122614/https://nesn.com/2019/03/patriots-release-adrian-clayborn-clear-4m-in-salary-cap-space/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Atlanta Falcons (second stint) ===
On April 9, 2019, Clayborn signed a one-year $4 million contract with the Falcons.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2019 |title=Falcons agree to terms with Adrian Clayborn on a one-year contract |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-agree-to-terms-with-adrian-clayborn-on-a-one-year-contract |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |access-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409163406/https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-agree-to-terms-with-adrian-clayborn-on-a-one-year-contract |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[2019 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]], Clayborn recorded his first sack of the season in the 24–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2019 |title=Jones scores late TD, leads Falcons past Eagles 24-20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128124 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=September 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190916162047/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128124 |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 10 against the [[2019 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], Clayborn had one sack in the 26–9 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints - November 10th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911100nor.htm |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709183356/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911100nor.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 11 against the [[2019 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]], Clayborn had two sacks in the 29–3 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Carolina Panthers - November 17th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911170car.htm |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 2, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221202222237/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911170car.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Clayborn played in 15 games with one start, recording 18 tackles, four sacks and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122013713/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Cleveland Browns ===
On April 9, 2020, Clayborn signed a two-year, $6 million contract with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=April 9, 2020 |title=Browns D-Line gets a pass-rushing boost with signing of veteran Adrian Clayborn |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-d-line-gets-a-pass-rushing-boost-with-signing-of-veteran-adrian-clayborn |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |archive-date=August 14, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814170339/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-d-line-gets-a-pass-rushing-boost-with-signing-of-veteran-adrian-clayborn |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=March 31, 2020 |title=Browns sign Adrian Clayborn |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/31/browns-sign-adrian-clayborn/ |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk |archive-date=September 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918014835/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/31/browns-sign-adrian-clayborn/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the season with 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble in 15 games and two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Clayborn 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708124019/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ClayAd00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Clayborn was released by the Browns on March 9, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2021 |title=Browns release DE Adrian Clayborn |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-release-de-adrian-clayborn |access-date=July 9, 2023 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708180736/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-release-de-adrian-clayborn |url-status=live }}</ref>
