(Harrisburg, Pennsylvania) | college = [[Temple Owls football|Temple]] (2008–2011) | undraftedyear = 2012 | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 1 | weight_lbs = 250 | pastteams = * [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] ({{NFL Year|2012}}) * [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ({{NFL Year|2013}})* * [[Denver Broncos]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}) * [[San Diego Chargers]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}) * [[Washington Redskins]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}) * [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] ({{NFL Year|2014}})* * [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] ({{CFL Year|2015}})* | highlights = * [[Mid-American Conference football individual awards|MAC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2009) * 3× First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] ([[2009 Mid-American Conference football season|2009]], [[2010 Mid-American Conference football season|2010]], [[2011 Mid-American Conference football season|2011]]) | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 3 | pfr = R/RobiAd01 }} '''Adrian Lynn Robinson Jr.''' (November 21, 1989 – May 16, 2015) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in [[2012 Pittsburgh Steelers season|2012]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Temple University]]. He also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Denver Broncos]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[Washington Redskins]]. ==Early life== Adrian Robinson was born on November 21, 1989, in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]]{{cite web|title=Adrian Robinson - 2011 Football|url=http://www.owlsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4687|publisher=Owls Football|accessdate=May 19, 2015}} to Adrian Robinson Sr, and Terry.{{cite news|last1=Bieler|first1=Des|title=Robinson committed suicide by hanging|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2015/05/18/reports-former-nfl-linebacker-adrian-robinson-committed-suicide-by-hanging/|newspaper=Washington Post|accessdate=May 19, 2015|date=May 18, 2015}} Robinson attended [[Harrisburg High School (Pennsylvania)|Harrisburg High School]], where he was named a three star prospect by scout.com. He graduated from Harrisburg High in 2008.{{cite web|last1=Veronikis|first1=Eric|title=Medical examiner: Harrisburg football star Adrian Robinson killed himself|url=https://www.pennlive.com/midstate/index.ssf/2015/05/medical_examiner_adrian_robins.html|website=Pennlive.com|publisher=The Patriet News|accessdate=May 19, 2015|date=May 18, 2015}} Robinson was selected to play in the Big 33 Football Classic during his senior year and voted the most valuable player in that game. He was also a two-time all state honoree at Harrisburg. Robinson received D-1 offers from Temple, Pittsburgh, and Connecticut. Robinson attended [[Temple University]] where he majored in communications.{{Cite web |date=May 17, 2015 |title=Tiger-Cats announce death of recent signed defensive lineman Adrian Robinson |url=http://www.kelownadailycourier.ca/sports/national_sports/article_9900fc84-30d8-5596-90fc-eac113183e22.html |access-date=May 19, 2015 |website=Kelowna Daily Courier}} ==College career== ===Temple University=== In 2008, Robinson played in all twelve games of the college season, including three starts at defensive end. In his sophomore season, Robinson was named the MAC Defensive Player of the Year. He also earned such accolades as 2009 first-team All-MAC honoree, first-team All-MAC by Phil Steele, 2009 MAC Defensive MVP by the Sporting News and ESPN.com's All-Non-Automatic Qualifying Team selection. He was first-team All-MAC again as a junior and senior. He finished his college career with a dominating performance in the 37–15 victory over Wyoming in the 2011 Gildan New Mexico Bowl. It was Temple's first bowl victory since 1979. ==Professional career== ===Pittsburgh Steelers=== On April 28, 2012, Robinson was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]]. ===Philadelphia Eagles=== On August 23, 2013, the Steelers traded Robinson to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] for [[running back]] [[Felix Jones]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/felix-jones-traded-to-pittsburgh-steelers-from-eagles-0ap1000000233090 |title=Felix Jones traded from Philadelphia Eagles to Steelers |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=August 23, 2013 |website=NFL.com |access-date=August 23, 2013}} He was released by the Eagles on August 30, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/26217/nfl/news/adrian-robinson |title=Adrian Robinson |publisher=kffl.com |accessdate=May 18, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518184042/http://www.kffl.com/player/26217/nfl/news/adrian-robinson |archivedate=May 18, 2015 }} ===Denver Broncos=== On September 1, 2013, the [[Denver Broncos]] claimed Robinson. He was waived by the Broncos on October 15, 2013. ===San Diego Chargers=== On November 12, 2013, the [[San Diego Chargers]] signed Robinson. He was released by the Chargers on December 7, 2013. ===Washington Redskins=== On December 24, 2013, the [[Washington Redskins]] signed Robinson.{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Revamp-Linebacker-Corps/f1ddfdda-a60b-408b-a16e-96faa8fedb6a|title=Redskins Revamp Linebacker Corps|date=December 24, 2013|first=Brian|last=Tinsman|accessdate=December 26, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227181135/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Revamp-Linebacker-Corps/f1ddfdda-a60b-408b-a16e-96faa8fedb6a|archive-date=December 27, 2013|url-status=dead}} He was waived on August 24, 2014.{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Announce-Initial-Roster-Cuts-Moves/a30a0afc-fceb-40c1-8ea2-47972cf4259c|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140825041946/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Announce-Initial-Roster-Cuts-Moves/a30a0afc-fceb-40c1-8ea2-47972cf4259c|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 25, 2014|title=Redskins Announce Initial Roster Cuts, Moves|date=August 24, 2014|first=Andrew|last=Walker|accessdate=August 24, 2014}} ===Tampa Bay Buccaneers=== Robinson was signed to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]' practice squad on September 10, 2014. He was released by the Buccaneers on September 23, 2014. ===Hamilton Tiger-Cats=== Robinson signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on April 27, 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12906938/ex-linebacker-adrian-robinson-dies-age-25 |title=Adrian Robinson, who recently signed with CFL's Tiger-Cats, dies |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 18, 2015 |access-date=May 18, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518183715/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/12906938/ex-linebacker-adrian-robinson-dies-age-25 |archive-date=May 18, 2015 }} ==Death== Robinson died on May 16, 2015.{{cite web|last1=Klis|first1=Mike|title=Former Broncos linebacker Adrian Robinson dies at 25|url=http://www.wthr.com/story/29087715/report-ex-nfl-linebacker-adrian-robinson-jr-dies-at-100|publisher=9news.com|accessdate=May 18, 2015}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} The medical examiner later ruled his death as a [[suicide by hanging]].{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_28140257/coroner-adrian-robinson-former-broncos-linebacker-died-suicide|title=Coroner: Adrian Robinson, former Broncos linebacker, died of suicide|work=denverpost.com|date=May 18, 2015 |accessdate=May 20, 2015}} Robinson is survived by his daughter, Avery Marie. On October 14, 2015, Robinson's family announced that a diagnosis of [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy]] (CTE) was confirmed through officials at the Concussion Legacy Foundation at Boston University.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13886586/autopsy-shows-ex-nfl-player-adrian-robinson-jr-killed-april-had-brain-injury|title=Adrian Robinson Jr. had brain disease CTE, autopsy shows|work=ESPN.com|date=October 14, 2015 |access-date=October 15, 2015}} He is one of at least 345 [[List of NFL players with chronic traumatic encephalopathy|NFL players to be diagnosed after death]] with this disease, which is caused by repeated hits to the head.{{cite news |title=The driving force behind Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) |website=Concussion Legacy Foundation |url=https://concussionfoundation.org/cte-resources/subconcussive-impacts |access-date=July 2, 2023 |archive-date=July 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702123543/https://concussionfoundation.org/cte-resources/subconcussive-impacts |url-status=dead }}{{cite news |author=Ken Belson and Benjamin Mueller |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/20/sports/football/cte-study-concussions-brain-tackle.html |title=Collective Force of Head Hits, Not Just the Number of Them, Increases Odds of C.T.E. '''Adrian D'Sean Tracy''' (born April 6, 1988) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the sixth round (184th overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. Tracy played [[college football]] at the [[College of William & Mary]].

==Professional career==

===New York Giants===
Tracy was signed to a multi-year deal with the Giants in June 2010, after being selected by them in the sixth round of the 2010 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2010/06/giants_sign_sixth-round_pick_a.html |title=Giants sign sixth-round pick Adrian Tracy |date=June 22, 2010 |first=Mike |last=Garafolo |work=The Star-Ledger }}</ref> In preseason, he suffered a dislocated elbow and was placed on IR for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Battista |first=Judy |author-link=Judy Battista |date=August 31, 2010 |title=Giants Lose Sorgi and Moss for Season |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/01/sports/football/01giants.html |work=New York Times}}</ref> He was waived by the Giants on September 3, 2011, but was re-signed to the practice squad the next day.

===Arizona Cardinals===
Tracy was signed to a reserve/future contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on January 9, 2014. The Cardinals released Tracy on August 30, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-To-53/552f8ee4-1e2a-4da1-b6a7-3e4f0a52e2d2 |title=Cardinals Cut To 53 |access-date=2014-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140901194443/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-To-53/552f8ee4-1e2a-4da1-b6a7-3e4f0a52e2d2 |archive-date=2014-09-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Tracy signed with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats on December 17, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2014/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 9, 2022}}</ref> He played in regular season games over five years for the Tiger-Cats, recording 131 defensive tackles, 21 sacks, five forced fumbles, and two interceptions. He became a free agent on February 11, 2020.

===Montreal Alouettes===
On February 13, 2020, Tracy signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2020/02/13/alouettes-add-muscle-defensive-line/|title=Alouettes add muscle to the defensive line|publisher=[[Montreal Alouettes]]|date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> However, the [[2020 CFL season]] was cancelled and he did not play in 2020. His contract expired on February 9, 2021, and he did not sign with a team in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2021/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 9, 2022}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On February 9, 2022, it was announced that Tracy had signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2022/02/09/argos-sign-dl-adrian-tracy/ |title=Argos sign DL Adrian Tracy |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=February 9, 2022}}</ref> However, he was released with the final training camp cuts on June 5, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2022/06/05/argos-transactions-june-5-2022/ |title=Argo transactions – June 5, 2022 |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=June 5, 2022}}</ref>

Tracy signed with Athletes Untapped as a private football coach on November 21, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Master Your Game: Football Coaching in Ashburn, Virginia with Adrian Tracy |url=https://athletesuntapped.com/blog/football-lessons-with-adrian-tracy/ |website=Athletes Untapped |publisher=Athletes Untapped |date=November 21, 2024 |access-date=September 8, 2025}}</ref>

'''Adrian Battles''' (born October 30, 1988) is a retired [[American football]] [[offensive guard]]. He played [[college football]] for [[Minnesota State University, Mankato]] from 2005 to 2009.

==College career==
Battles played [[college football]] from 2005 to 2009 as an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Minnesota State Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Battles at home in Viking camp: Spent his college career playing on the same practice fields|newspaper=[[Mankato Free Press]]|date=July 31, 2010|url=http://mankatofreepress.com/vikingscamp/x2064734415/Battles-at-home-in-Viking-camp}}</ref><ref name=MFP2>{{cite news|title=Battles Battling Away at Vikings Training Camp|publisher=Mav Blog|date=August 2, 2010|url=http://mavink.blogspot.com/2010/08/battles-battling-away-at-vikings.html}}</ref>    He was a four-year starter at Mankato, starting in 43 of 46 games while with the program.<ref name=MFP/>  According to Mark Craig of the ''[[Minneapolis Star-Tribune]]'', Battles "dominated the [[NCAA Division II]] ranks" as an offensive lineman for MNSU.<ref name=MC/>  Battles credited offensive line coach Mike Cunningham for treating him like a son and keeping him motivated through four years at MNSU.<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Mankato player at Super Bowl with Packers |newspaper=[[Aberdeen American News]] |date=February 4, 2011 |url=http://aberdeensports.net/inthehuddle/2011/02/04/former-mankato-player-at-super-bowl-with-packers/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327080102/http://aberdeensports.net/inthehuddle/2011/02/04/former-mankato-player-at-super-bowl-with-packers/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 27, 2012 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Minnesota Vikings===
In May 2010, Battles signed as a free agent to play professional football with the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He was moved by the Vikings from an offensive tackle to an offensive guard.<ref name=MFP2/><ref name=MFP>{{cite news|author=Chad Courrier|title=Vikings sign former Mav Battles: Former Minnesota State tackle to move to guard|newspaper=Mankato Free Press|date=May 4, 2010|url=http://mankatofreepress.com/sports/x1036628282/Vikings-sign-former-Mav-Battles}}</ref> He told reporters that the position change presented a challenge due to the differences in footwork and technique, but added, "When I get an opportunity, I have to make the most of it."<ref>{{cite news|title=Former MSU player Battles for a spot on the Vikings: Tackle-turned-guard feeling more comfortable with each practice|newspaper=Mankato Free Press|date=May 29, 2010|url=http://mankatofreepress.com/prosports/x1414119265/Former-MSU-player-Battles-for-a-spot-on-the-Vikings}}</ref>  Before playing in his first pre-season game in August 2010, Battles told a reporter, "I haven't even been to an NFL game. To actually play in the first NFL game I go to is awesome. I'm looking forward to it."<ref>{{cite news|author=Chad Courrier|title=Former Mav Battles for roster spot; ready for 1st game: Vikings guard has never attended an NFL game|newspaper=Mankato Free Press|date=August 13, 2010|url=http://mankatofreepress.com/vikingscamp/x334247211/Former-Mav-Battles-for-roster-spot-ready-for-1st-game}}</ref>  After completing the entire NFL preseason with the Vikings, Battles was released on September 5, 2010.<ref name=MC>{{cite news|title=Persistence paying off for former MSU Mankato offensive lineman|newspaper=[[Minneapolis Star-Tribune]]|date=February 1, 2011|url=http://www.startribune.com/featuredColumns/114984819.html}}</ref><ref name=BM/>

===Green Bay Packers===
In December 2010, he signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]]. He was a member of the Packers practice squad and became "an unofficial good-luck charm" for the Packers who went 7-0 after he joined the team (two regular season games and five postseason games) to become the first No. 6 seed from the NFC to play in the Super Bowl.<ref name=MC/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.packers.com/team/roster/Adrian-Battles/9c3ddf09-fdaa-42a5-a444-549a88acfab2|title=Adrian Battles|publisher=Green Bay Packers|access-date=February 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714081655/http://www.packers.com/team/roster/Adrian-Battles/9c3ddf09-fdaa-42a5-a444-549a88acfab2|archive-date=July 14, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Battles was part of the Packers' practice squad at [[Super Bowl XLV]]. With the team in [[Irving, Texas]], Battles told a reporter for the ''[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]'', "I was a Packer fan growing up. Just to be a part of this organization is great -- especially to be a part of the Super Bowl experience. A lot of guys don't get to experience this, even guys who have long careers. It's a blessing to be here and I'm thankful for it."<ref>{{cite news|author=Gary D'Amato|title=Milwaukee's Battles glad to be here|newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|date=February 2, 2011|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/115135689.html}}</ref>

At the media day before Super Bowl XLV, Battles showed up wearing a giant "[[cheesehead]]."  Photographs of the grinning, 6 foot, 3 inch, 315 pound cheesehead were published in multiple newspapers including a featured picture of the day in the United Kingdom's ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pictures of the day|newspaper=The Telegraph|date=February 2, 2011|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/picturegalleries/picturesoftheday/8298123/Pictures-of-the-day-2-February-2011.html?image=25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-02-01 |title=Photoblog: Say cheese |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/tag/_/name/adrian-battles |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Packers are set apart by small-town roots|newspaper=The Hamilton Spectator|date=February 2, 2011|url=http://www.thespec.com/sports/article/480531--packers-are-set-apart-by-small-town-roots}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Wall St alpha metric picks Packers in Super Bowl|publisher=Reuters|date=February 4, 2011|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/2011/02/04/us-nfl-superbowl-alpha-idUSTRE71352N20110204}}{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name=cheese/>  Battles told reporters, "I'm enjoying every minute of it."<ref name=cheese>{{cite news|title=Former Maverick happy to say cheese: Minnesota State standout joins Packers|newspaper=Mankato Free Press|date=February 3, 2011|url=http://mankatofreepress.com/sports/x1293239897/Chad-Courrier-Former-Maverick-happy-to-say-cheese}}</ref>

In August 2011, he joined the Packers for their visit to the [[White House]] after winning Super Bowl XLV and was prominently featured in photographs as he stood behind President [[Barack Obama]]. When his photograph was printed in newspapers across the country, friends of Battles joked that he "must have sneaked in there."<ref name=BM>{{cite news|author=Bob McGinn|title=Battles will always have a chief claim to fame|newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|date=August 15, 2011|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/packers/127805058.html}}</ref> Asked about his prominent placement, Battles told the ''[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]'', "I just call myself lucky for getting that spot. We went down in rows and I ended up right there in the front."<ref name=BM/>

On July 31, 2011, the second day of the Packers' 2011 training camp, Battles suffered an injury to his [[Achilles tendon]].<ref name=BM/> He was unable to return to the team after the injury and was waived/injured on August 30, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|author=Tom Silverman|title=Packers release Battles, Asiodu|newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|date=August 30, 2011|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/128710238.html}}</ref> After clearing waivers, he was placed on injured reserve and released with an injury settlement on September 2.

===Green Bay Blizzard===
Battles played for the [[Green Bay Blizzard]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] in 2014.

===Cleveland Gladiators===
Battles started the final game of the [[2015 Arena Football League season|2015 season]] for the [[Cleveland Gladiators]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/aflgld/mtt/adrian_battles_974183.html |title=Adrian Battles |publisher=arenafootball.com |access-date=November 9, 2015 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109195253/http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/aflgld/mtt/adrian_battles_974183.html |archive-date=November 9, 2015 }}</ref>

'''Adrian Moten''' (born April 22, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2011. He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]].

==Professional career==

===Indianapolis Colts===
On July 29, 2011, Moten was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an undrafted free agent. He was waived on November 26, 2011. He played in 10 games in the regular season and all 4 preseason games.

===Seattle Seahawks===
On November 28, 2011, Moten was claimed off waivers by the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. On May 15, 2012, he was released by the Seahawks.  He played in 2 regular season games with the Seahawks.

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On August 6, 2012, Moten was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. On August 31, 2012, Moten was released as one of the final cuts. On October 2, 2012, Moten was re-signed and then released on October 9, 2012.  He played in 1 regular season game and all 4 preseason games with the Eagles.

===Cleveland Browns===
On December 18, 2012, Moten was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]]. He was waived on August 3, 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-sign-Dominic-Alford-/08a687b8-65f0-435b-9d18-c31880937456 |title=Browns sign Dominic Alford |date=August 3, 2013 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |accessdate=August 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305010251/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-sign-Dominic-Alford-/08a687b8-65f0-435b-9d18-c31880937456 |archive-date=March 5, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On August 5, 2013, Moten was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Dave |last=Birkett |title=Detroit Lions waive WR Devin Thomas, sign CB Brandon King, claim LB Adrian Moten off waivers |url=http://www.freep.com/article/20130805/SPORTS01/308050109/detroit-lions-alex-elkins |work=Detroit Free Press |date=August 5, 2013}}</ref> On August 17, 2013, he was released by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/lions/index.ssf/2013/08/detroit_lions_sign_linebacker.html |title=Detroit Lions sign veteran OLB Rocky McIntosh |last=Rogers |first=Justin |date=August 17, 2013 |website=MLive.com |accessdate=August 18, 2013}}</ref>  He played in 3 preseason games.

===Saskatchewan Roughriders ===
Moten signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] on May 16, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.riderville.com/article/riders-add-three-more-to-defence |title=Riders Add Three More to Defence |access-date=2014-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714150607/http://www.riderville.com/article/riders-add-three-more-to-defence |archive-date=2014-07-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
Moten was signed to the [[Ottawa Redblacks]]' practice roster on August 26, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ottawaredblacks.com/roster/show/id/7095 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140830002916/http://www.ottawaredblacks.com/roster/show/id/7095 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 30, 2014 |title=Adrian Moten |publisher=ottawaredblacks.com |accessdate=August 29, 2014 }}</ref> He was released by the Redblacks on September 6, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/page/transactions |title=2014 Transactions |publisher=cfl.ca |accessdate=November 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205005714/http://www.cfl.ca/page/transactions |archivedate=December 5, 2014 }}</ref>

'''Adrian Charles Hamilton''' (born November 29, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Prairie View A&M Panthers football|Prairie View A&M Panthers]] and was signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2012. Hamilton was also a member of the [[Portland Thunder]] in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL).

==Early life==
Hamilton attended [[David W. Carter High School]], where he played both at [[linebacker]] and [[defensive end]].<ref>{{cite web | title=ESPN Profile | work= ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/15396 | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Scout.com">{{cite news|title=Adrian Hamilton profile|work=Scout.com|publisher=Fox Sports}}</ref>

In his last 2 years, he totaled 155 tackles, 12 sacks, 29 quarterback hurries, 9 forced fumbles and one fumble returned for a touchdown.

==College career==
Hamilton accepted a football scholarship from [[Oklahoma State University]] in 2006. As a freshman, he was suspended after failing to meet the NCAA academic requirements. The school also asked him to pay for his own tuition and "greyshirt" while sitting out the first semester, which he couldn't do.<ref>{{cite web | last=Wilson | first=Aaron | title=Ravens rookie linebacker Adrian Hamilton: ‘I’m hungry to get to the quarterback’ | website=Baltimore Sun | date=2012-09-02 | url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2012/09/02/ravens-rookie-linebacker-adrian-hamilton-im-hungry-to-get-to-the-quarterback/ | access-date=2025-10-08}}</ref>

In 2007, he [[Walk-on (sports)|walked on]] at [[Texas Tech University]]. As a sophomore, he played sparingly as a backup in 6 games, recording 4 tackles (one for loss).<ref name="AD" /> On November 17, in the season finale against No. 3 ranked [[Oklahoma]], he tallied 2 tackles as [[Texas Tech]] won 34–27.<ref>{{cite web | title= (3) Oklahoma 27, Texas Tech 34 Box Score | work= sports-reference.com | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2007-11-17-texas-tech.html |access-date= September 10, 2012}}</ref>

In August 2008, he was dismissed from the team by head coach Mike Leach for a team rules violation. In 2008, he enrolled at [[Dallas College|Dallas County Community College]] to improve his academic grades, although he didn't play football.<ref>{{cite news|title=DE dismissed from team|work=Lubbock Avalanche-Journal|date=August 14, 2008}}</ref><ref name="odds">{{cite web | title = Trying to beat the odds — again | work = ncaa.com | url = https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2012-03-02/trying-beat-odds-again | access-date = March 15, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130522013855/http://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2012-03-02/trying-beat-odds-again | archive-date = May 22, 2013 | url-status = dead | df = mdy-all }}</ref>

In 2010, he transferred to [[Football Championship Subdivision]] [[Prairie View A&M]]. As a junior, he was a backup [[defensive end]] behind [[Quinton Spears]] and Jarvis Wilson. He registered 27 tackles (8 for loss), 5½ sacks, eight tackles for loss and one blocked punt (returned for a touchdown).<ref>{{cite web | title = Prairie View DE Hamilton taking control of spotlight | work = chron.com | date = October 15, 2011 | url =https://www.chron.com/sports/article/Prairie-View-DE-Hamilton-taking-control-of-2219662.php| access-date = October 14, 2020}}</ref><ref name="AD" />

As a senior in 2011, he started 9 out of 11 games. Hamilton broke the FCS single season sack record held by former [[Indianapolis Colts]] [[Robert Mathis]] with 22, while leading the team with 81 tackles, 26.5 tackles for loss, 5 quarterback hurries and 6 forced fumbles.<ref name="AD">{{cite web|title=Adrian Hamilton Scouting report |work=draftcountdown.com |url=http://www.draftcountdown.com/ScoutingReports/OLB/Adrian-Hamilton.php |access-date=September 8, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720170037/http://www.draftcountdown.com/ScoutingReports/OLB/Adrian-Hamilton.php |archive-date=July 20, 2012 }}</ref> On December 6, he was announced as the [[Southwestern Athletic Conference]] (SWAC) co-Defensive Player of the Year along with [[Grambling State Tigers football|Grambling State]] linebacker Cliff Exama.<ref>{{cite web | title = 2011 All-SWAC Football Teams Announced | work = swac.org | url =https://swac.org/news/2011/12/6/205343356.aspx| date = December 6, 2011| access-date = October 14, 2020}}</ref> He also was named to the All-SWAC defensive first-team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lum, Hamilton Lead 2011 CSJ All-America Team |work=college-sports-journal.com |url=http://www.college-sports-journal.com/index.php/fcs-all-conference-teams/170-lum-hamilton-lead-2011-csj-all-america-team |access-date=September 8, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808041153/http://www.college-sports-journal.com/index.php/fcs-all-conference-teams/170-lum-hamilton-lead-2011-csj-all-america-team |archive-date= August 8, 2014 }}</ref> The [[Football Championship Subdivision]] also recognized Hamilton as Defensive Player of the Year in 2011.

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
Hamilton was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[2012 NFL draft]] on April 29.<ref>{{cite web | title = Undrafted free-agent deals for all 32 NFL teams  | work = nfl.com | url =https://www.nfl.com/news/undrafted-free-agent-deals-for-all-32-nfl-teams-09000d5d828bb384| access-date = April 30, 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Cowboys announce undrafted rookie free agents  | work =profootballtalk.nbcsports.com | date =April 30, 2012 | url =https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/04/30/cowboys-announce-undrafted-free-agents/| access-date = April 30, 2020 }}</ref> He was limited with knee and wrist injuries during training camp. On August 25, in a preseason game against the [[St. Louis Rams]], Hamilton had a sack on [[Kellen Clemens]]. On August 30, Hamilton was released.<ref>{{cite web | title = Source: Cowboys release OLB Adrian Hamilton  | work = espn.go.com | url =https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4696627/source-cowboys-release-olb-adrian-hamilton| date = August 30, 2020 | access-date = September 3, 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Cowboys Announce Release Of 23 Players, Roster Trimmed To 53  | work = dallascowboys.com | url =https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-announce-release-of-23-players-roster-trimmed-to-53-328756| date = August 31, 2012 | access-date = September 3, 2020 }}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On September 2, 2012, Hamilton signed with [[Baltimore Ravens]] to join the Practice squad.<ref>{{cite web  | title = Ravens Add Pass Rusher To Practice Squad  | work = baltimoreravens.com  | url = http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Reports-Ravens-Add-Pass-Rusher-To-Practice-Squad/22200aaf-31c5-4c01-aefd-d488b49fbf2f  | access-date = September 3, 2012  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120905010759/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Reports-Ravens-Add-Pass-Rusher-To-Practice-Squad/22200aaf-31c5-4c01-aefd-d488b49fbf2f  | archive-date = September 5, 2012  | url-status = dead  | df = mdy-all  }}</ref><ref>{{cite news| title = Cut By Cowboys, LB Hamilton Joins Ravens Practice Squad  | work = dallascowboys.com/ | date = September 3, 2012 }}</ref> On December 22, 2012, Hamilton was promoted to the active roster after the team placed [[Jameel McClain]] on Injured Reserve.<ref>{{cite web | title = Ravens put McClain on IR, elevate Hamilton  | work = profootballtalk.nbcsports.com | url =https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/12/22/ravens-put-mcclain-on-ir-elevate-hamilton/ | date = December 22, 2012 | access-date = September 3, 2020}}</ref> Hamilton played in the final two regular season games of the Ravens' [[Super Bowl XLVII]] championship season and made one tackle. He was declared inactive for the postseason.

On August 25, 2013, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].<ref>{{cite web | title= Ravens Place OLB Adrian Hamilton On Injured Reserve | work= baltimoreravens.com | url= http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Place-OLB-Adrian-Hamilton-On-Injured-Reserve/c1251a9a-b52c-4ded-8776-ffdd8d864687 | access-date= August 25, 2013 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130827135210/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Place-OLB-Adrian-Hamilton-On-Injured-Reserve/c1251a9a-b52c-4ded-8776-ffdd8d864687 | archive-date= August 27, 2013 | url-status= dead | df= mdy-all }}</ref> On June 17, 2014, he was waived.<ref>{{cite web | title=Ravens Waive WR Aaron Mellette, OLB Adrian Hamilton | work=baltimoreravens.com | url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Waive-WR-Aaron-Mellette-OLB-Adrian-Hamilton/80969d4b-42b1-4b2e-8424-87944e134ba7 | access-date=June 17, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140618200301/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Waive-WR-Aaron-Mellette-OLB-Adrian-Hamilton/80969d4b-42b1-4b2e-8424-87944e134ba7 | archive-date=June 18, 2014 | url-status=dead | df=mdy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Ravens cut Aaron Mellette, Adrian Hamilton | work= espn.com | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/baltimore-ravens/post/_/id/10629/ravens-cut-aaron-mellette-adrian-hamilton |date=June 17, 2014| access-date = September 3, 2020}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
On July 22, 2014, Hamilton signed with [[San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web | title= Linebacker Adrian Hamilton Joins Bolts | work= chargers.com | url= http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Linebacker-Adrian-Hamilton-Joins-Bolts/435ab5c6-883e-4169-84a4-7d48a46eb8df | access-date= July 22, 2014 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140725232705/http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Linebacker-Adrian-Hamilton-Joins-Bolts/435ab5c6-883e-4169-84a4-7d48a46eb8df | archive-date= July 25, 2014 | url-status= dead | df= mdy-all }}</ref> The Chargers released Hamilton on August 25.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Chargers-Trim-Roster-Waive-11-Players/57f5031c-ffb7-4573-bdcb-0a54b2c26612 |title=Chargers Trim Roster; Waive 11 Players |access-date=August 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140827203542/http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Chargers-Trim-Roster-Waive-11-Players/57f5031c-ffb7-4573-bdcb-0a54b2c26612 |archive-date=August 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

===Calgary Stampeders (CFL)===
On March 18, 2015, he was signed by the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.stampeders.com/2015/03/18/stamps-add-seven-players/ | title=Stamps Add Seven Players | date=March 18, 2015 | access-date=July 15, 2020}}</ref> He was released on June 14.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.stampeders.com/2015/06/14/stampeders-roster-moves-150614/ | title=Stampeders Roster Moves | date=June 14, 2015 | access-date=July 15, 2020}}</ref>

===Portland Thunder (AFL)===
On July 8, 2015, he signed with the [[Portland Thunder]] of the [[Arena Football League]]. He appeared in the last 5 games, making  12 tackles (2 for loss), 3 pass break ups, and one sack. He was placed on the Other League Exemption list, to allow him to sign a contract with the [[Ottawa RedBlacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].

===Ottawa RedBlacks (CFL)===
On September 8, 2015, he was signed to the practice roster of the [[Ottawa RedBlacks]] in the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/redblacks-make-flurry-of-roster-moves/n-5047693 | title=RedBlacks Make Flurry of Roster Moves | date=September 8, 2015 | access-date=July 15, 2020}}</ref> He was released on October 18.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2015/10/18/transactions-october-18-2015/ | title=Transactions: October 18, 2015 | date=October 18, 2015 | access-date=July 15, 2020}}</ref>

===Texas Revolution (CIF)===
In 2017, he was signed by the  [[Texas Revolution (indoor football)|Texas Revolution]] of the [[Champions Indoor Football]]. He was released on May 31.

'''Adewale Ojomo'''{{Audio|Adewale_Ojomu.wav|Listen}} (born November 11, 1988) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He signed with the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Miami]].

==Early life==
Ojomo attended [[Hialeah High School]] in Florida. He was rated as the No. 72 player in the state by the Orlando Sentinel.

==College career==
He played [[college football]] at the University of Miami. Ojomo finished college with 79 tackles, 9.5 sacks, 3 pass deflections, 2 forced fumbles.<ref name="AO">{{cite web | title=Adewale Ojomo College Statistics  | work= sports-reference.com | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adewale-ojomo-1.html }}</ref>

In his freshman season, Ojomo had 22 tackles, 3 sacks, a pass deflection and a forced fumble.<ref name="AO" />

In his junior season, he had 38 tackles, 5 sacks and a pass deflection.<ref name="AO" /> On September 2, 2010, in the season opener against Florida A&M in which Ojomo recorded 3 tackles and 2 sacks helping the [[Miami Hurricanes]] win 45-0.<ref>{{cite web | title=Florida A&M 0, (13) Miami (FL) 45 Box score  | work= sports-reference.com | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2010-09-02-miami-fl.html }}</ref>

In his senior season, Ojomo had 19 tackles, 1.5 sacks, a pass deflection and a forced fumble.<ref name="AO" />

==Professional career==

===New York Giants===
On May 1, 2012, Ojomo signed with the [[New York Giants]] as an [[Undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/26790/nfl/news/adewale-ojomo |title=Adewale Ojomo |work=kffl.com |access-date=May 1, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205002633/http://www.kffl.com/player/26790/nfl/news/adewale-ojomo |archive-date=December 5, 2014 }}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
He was signed to the Seahawks' practice squad on September 17, 2013.

===Buffalo Bills===
Ojomo was signed to the Bills' practice squad on September 24, 2013.

===Tennessee Titans===
On December 11, 2013, Ojomo signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] practice squad.<ref>[http://www.therepublic.com/view/story/86e712e105114d58b433ea905bd3ee2b/FBN--Titans-Moves Titans fill spot on practice squad by signing DE Adewale Ojomo] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214215455/http://www.therepublic.com/view/story/86e712e105114d58b433ea905bd3ee2b/FBN--Titans-Moves |date=2013-12-14 }}</ref> He was waived on April 7, 2014, two weeks after he was arrested for soliciting a prostitute in [[Miami]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Alper|first=Josh|title=Titans waive Adewale Ojomo after solicitation arrest|date=7 April 2014 |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/04/07/titans-waive-adewale-ojomo-after-solicitation-arrest/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|access-date=8 April 2014}}</ref>

===Los Angeles KISS===
Ojomo was assigned to the [[Los Angeles KISS]] of the [[Arena Football League]] on May 22, 2014.

===Dallas Cowboys===
Ojomo signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on August 1, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sabin |first1=Rainer |title=Dallas Cowboys to sign DEs Ken Boatright, Adewale Ojomo to replace WR L'Damian Washington, OT Darius Morris |url=http://cowboysblog.dallasnews.com/2014/08/dallas-cowboys-to-add-two-defensive-ends-in-wake-of-demarcus-lawrences-injury.html/ |website=DallasNews.com |publisher=Cowboys Blog |access-date=2 August 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140806223415/http://cowboysblog.dallasnews.com/2014/08/dallas-cowboys-to-add-two-defensive-ends-in-wake-of-demarcus-lawrences-injury.html/ |archive-date= 6 August 2014 }}</ref> The Cowboys waived Ojomo on August 26, 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/article-DavidHelman/Cowboys-Trim-Roster-To-75-Matt-Johnson-Waived-/a919dc13-f1b7-47e5-b0bc-ad7149621b66?campaign=social_20140826_30507006|title=Cowboys Trim Roster To 75; Matt Johnson Waived|date=2014-08-26|work=Dallas Cowboys|access-date=2018-02-22|language=en|archive-date=2014-08-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140827091214/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/article-DavidHelman/Cowboys-Trim-Roster-To-75-Matt-Johnson-Waived-/a919dc13-f1b7-47e5-b0bc-ad7149621b66?campaign=social_20140826_30507006|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Ojomo was signed by the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on September 17, 2014 and was assigned to the team's practice roster.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/cfl/justin-hickman-rejoins-tiger-cats-from-nfl-1.2769132|title=Justin Hickman rejoins Tiger-Cats from NFL {{!}} CBC Sports|work=CBC|access-date=2018-02-22|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/page/transactions |title=Transactions |publisher=cfl.ca |access-date=November 20, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205005714/http://www.cfl.ca/page/transactions |archive-date=December 5, 2014 }}</ref>

'''Adrian Hubbard''' (born February 27, 1992) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

==College career==
As a redshirt sophomore in 2012, Hubbard had seven [[quarterback sacks|sacks]], including one in the [[2013 BCS National Championship Game]]. He led Alabama in sacks (7), tackles for loss (11) and forced fumbles (3). Hubbard recorded a sack in each of Alabama's last three games (Auburn, Georgia and Notre Dame). His 7.0 sacks ranked sixth in the SEC this season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011113aac.html |title=Linebacker Adrian Hubbard to Return - ALABAMA CRIMSON TIDE - University of Alabama Official Athletic Site |website=www.rolltide.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130113042031/http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011113aac.html |archive-date=2013-01-13}}</ref> After his junior season in 2013, he entered the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scarborough |first=Alex |date=2014-01-09 |title=Dix, Kouandjio among 4 from Bama to NFL |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2014/story/_/id/10268085/ha-ha-clinton-dix-cyrus-kouandjio-alabama-crimson-tide-going-nfl-draft |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Adam John Thielen''' (born August 22, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for 13 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota State Mavericks football|Minnesota State Mavericks]] and signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]] in 2013, playing for them for 10 seasons. Thielen holds several NFL records, including eight straight games over 100+ yards receiving, and 74 receptions in the first half of a season.<ref name="bergman1">{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=October 28, 2018 |title=Adam Thielen records eighth straight 100-yard game |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adam-thielen-records-eighth-straight-100-yard-game-0ap3000000979955 |access-date=October 31, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Thielen also played in the NFL for the [[Carolina Panthers]] and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Detroit Lakes, Minnesota]], to Pete and Jayne Thielen, alongside his cousins, Adam grew up rooting for the Vikings and idolized [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] wide receivers [[Cris Carter]] and [[Randy Moss]], wearing their Vikings jerseys while practicing in his back yard as a child.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=Chris |date=December 23, 2017 |title='He always had a plan': The unlikely rise to NFL stardom for... |url=https://www.duluthnewstribune.com/sports/football/4378335-he-always-had-plan-unlikely-rise-nfl-stardom-detroit-lakes-adam-thielen |access-date=December 5, 2018 |website=Duluth News Tribune |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206001949/https://www.duluthnewstribune.com/sports/football/4378335-he-always-had-plan-unlikely-rise-nfl-stardom-detroit-lakes-adam-thielen |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=August 6, 2013 |title=Vikings WR Thielen on rise despite D2 background |url=https://www.startribune.com/vikings-wr-thielen-on-rise-despite-d2-background/218585341/ |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> He attended [[Detroit Lakes High School]], where he participated in four sports (football, basketball, baseball and golf).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mankle |first=Taylor |date=January 19, 2018 |title=Detroit Lakes High School shows love for Adam Thielen |url=http://www.wday.com/sports/football/4391046-detroit-lakes-high-school-shows-love-adam-thielen |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180706075817/http://www.wday.com/sports/football/4391046-detroit-lakes-high-school-shows-love-adam-thielen |archive-date=July 6, 2018 |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=WDAY}}</ref> In [[high school football|football]], he helped lead the Lakers to a 9–1 season and was an All-conference and All-state selection in his senior season. That same year, he also was a member of a Detroit Lakes [[golf]] team that won the 2008 2A Minnesota state championship.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Craig |first=Mark |date=August 20, 2016 |title=Wide receiver Adam Thielen isn't just a Vikings spare part |url=http://www.startribune.com/wide-receiver-adam-thielen-isn-t-just-a-vikings-spare-part/390813481/ |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref>

==College career==
After [[redshirted|redshirting]] the 2008 season at [[Minnesota State University, Mankato]], Thielen played in nine games and caught 21 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown as a freshman in 2009. As a sophomore in 2010, he started in all 11 games and was named Minnesota State's Offensive Player of the Year in addition to the All-[[Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference]] (NSIC) South Division second-team after he led the team with 41 receptions for 686 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Robert |date=February 9, 2015 |title=Detroit Lakes celebrates "Adam Thielen Day" |url=http://www.perhamfocus.com/news/3674755-detroit-lakes-celebrates-adam-thielen-day |access-date=October 31, 2018 |website=Perham Focus}}</ref> In 2011, he started all 12 games and was a second-team All-NSIC South Division selection for the second-straight season as he hauled in 62 passes for 715 yards and five touchdowns on offense and also handled kick return (three kicks for 77 yards and a score) and punt return duties (22 punts for 217 yards). During the 2012 season, Thielen became the main target for Minnesota State's passing attack and was again the team's starting kick and punt returner, helping the Mavericks to a 13–1 record, as they advanced to the [[NCAA]] Semi-finals. He led the Minnesota State receiving corps with 74 receptions for a total of 1,176 yards (15.9 avg) and eight touchdowns. For his efforts, Thielen was named to the NSIC South Division All-NSIC first-team, the [[Daktronics]] Super Region No. 3 second-team, and the Don Hansen Super Region second-team. Thielen finished near the top of several career receiving categories after his four years at Minnesota State including finishing second in receiving yards (2,802), second in receptions (198), and third in touchdown catches (20). As a Maverick, he notched five 100-yard receiving games, including a career-high of 167 against [[Southwest Minnesota State Mustangs|Southwest Minnesota State]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2012 |title=No. 10 MSU rallies past SMSU in double overtime thriller – |url=https://smsumustangs.com/news/2012/10/13/FB_1013120458.aspx?path=football |access-date=October 31, 2018 |website=SMSU Mustangs Athletics}}</ref>

Thielen did not receive an invitation to perform at the 2013 [[NFL Combine]], but he did attend a Regional Combine in Chicago in March, where he performed well enough to warrant an invitation to the Super Regional Combine held in [[Dallas, Texas]] in April.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dator |first=James |date=October 8, 2018 |title=How Adam Thielen went from a $500 D2 scholarship to record-setting NFL star |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2018/10/8/17950820/adam-thielen-vikings-d2-scholarship-roster |access-date=February 25, 2019 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> There, he showcased his athletic ability, completing the [[40-yard dash]] in 4.45 seconds and impressing in the [[three-cone drill]] with a time of 6.77 seconds, a mark that would have placed him in the top 20 at the NFL Combine.<ref name="Thielen">{{Cite web |date=August 7, 2013 |title=From prep to college to pro, receiver Adam Thielen stays in Minnesota in pursuit of NFL career |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/from-prep-to-college-to-pro-receiver-adam-thielen-stays-in-minnesota-in-pursuit-of-nfl-career/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Fox News |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (first stint)===
====2013====
After going undrafted in the [[2013 NFL draft]], Thielen attended a rookie tryout and evaluation session at Winter Park with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 11, 2013 |title=Detroit Lakes product gets shot with Vikings |url=https://www.inforum.com/sports/3048362-detroit-lakes-product-gets-shot-vikings |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=Inforum}}</ref> On May 6, 2013, the Vikings signed Thielen to a three-year, [[United States dollar|$]]1.48 million contract as an undrafted free agent.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Adam Thielen contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/adam-thielen-13071/ |access-date=November 25, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> On August 31, 2013, the Minnesota Vikings waived Thielen as part of their final roster cuts (along with 18 others), but he was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hasan |first=Arif |date=August 31, 2013 |title=Minnesota Vikings Release Final 53-Man Roster, Final Cuts |url=http://www.dailynorseman.com/2013/8/31/4681032/minnesota-vikings-release-final-53-man-roster-final-cuts |access-date=November 12, 2013 |website=SBNation |publisher=[[Vox Media, Inc.]]}}</ref> He saw some preseason action as a wide receiver and on special teams.

====2014====
[[File:Adam Thielen vikings.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Thielen with the Minnesota Vikings in 2014]]
After a strong preseason performance in both offense and special teams, Thielen earned a spot on the 53-man roster to start the 2014 campaign.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Robert |date=August 30, 2014 |title=Adam Thielen officially on Vikings roster |work=DL-Online |url=http://www.dl-online.com/sports/3336626-adam-thielen-officially-vikings-roster |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref>

Thielen made his NFL debut in the season opener in a road game against the [[St. Louis Rams]] on September 7.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at St. Louis Rams – September 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070ram.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 5, he caught his first NFL pass in the Vikings' 42–10 road loss against the [[Green Bay Packers]], finishing the game with four receptions for 57 yards that led the team in receiving.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay end zone.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 3, 2014 |title=Thielen Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week 2016 |website=KFAN}}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Thielen scored his first receiving touchdown on a 44-yard pass from quarterback [[Teddy Bridgewater]], after which he promptly gave the ball to his wife (then fiancée) Caitlin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=December 28, 2014 |title=Bridgewater, Vikings get by Bears 13–9 Reference]]}}</ref>

For the season, Thielen totaled eight catches for 137 yards (17.1 avg) and a touchdown on offense.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Also a special teams ace, Thielen was named to the All-Pro Special Teams Kick Return Unit and was named All-NFC North Special Team Player of the Year by [[Pro Football Focus]] (PFF) after he finished tied for second in the team in special teams tackles with 12 (9 of them solo).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/allpro.htm |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015====
In Week 4, Thielen hauled in a career-high six passes for 70 yards in a road game at the eventual [[Super Bowl 50|Super Bowl]] champions [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Denver Broncos – October 4th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510040den.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the regular season finale road game against the Packers on January 3, 2016, for the [[NFC North]] division, the Vikings executed a fake punt during the first drive of the game in which Thielen ran for 41 yards. He carried the ball another time for 26 yards, totaling 67 yards on two carries that tied for second in Vikings history for rushing yards in a game by a wide receiver with the effort. He also added a 16-yard catch as the Vikings ultimately clinched the NFC North title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers – January 3rd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601030gnb.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Thielen finished the season with 12 catches for 144 yards with a long of 30.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In 2015, Thielen was honored as the Vikings Special Teams Player of the Year. His seven special teams tackles tied for second on the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Robert |date=April 18, 2016 |title=Thielen named Vikings Special Teams player of the year |url=https://www.dl-online.com/sports/4012037-thielen-named-vikings-special-teams-player-year |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=Detroit Lakes Tribune}}</ref>

====2016====
With [[Stefon Diggs]] sidelined due to a groin injury, Thielen received the starting nod in his place for Week 5. Against the [[Houston Texans]], he broke 100 receiving yards in a game for the first time in his career as he finished the game with seven catches for 127 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Lindsey |date=October 9, 2016 |title=Adam Thielen's Career Day Sparks Vikings Offense |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Adam-Thielens-Career-Day-Sparks-Vikings-Offense/b4dc436d-ab8a-454a-ac5b-02096101080c |url-status=dead 11, 2016 |access-date=October 10, 2016 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> In the Vikings' loss to the [[Washington Redskins]] in Week 10, Thielen caught his second touchdown of the season on a 3-yard toss from [[Sam Bradford]] and also carried the ball once for 11 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2016 |title=Vikings' Adam Thielen: Touchdown reception in loss |url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/vikings-adam-thielen-touchdown-reception-in-loss/ |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=CBSSports}}</ref> Thielen had a career day on December 24, 2016, in a Week 16 loss to the Packers with a 202-yard, two-touchdown performance at [[Lambeau Field]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Lindsey |date=December 24, 2016 |title=Adam Thielen has Career Performance in Vikings Loss |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Adam-Thielen-has-Career-Performance-in-Vikings-Loss/2f9470cf-e5da-4d92-b058-f3d0e69f0abb |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 25, 2016 |access-date=December 25, 2016 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> His performance was just the fifth 200-yard receiving performance in Vikings history and the third that saw a Vikings receiver have at least 200 yards receiving and two touchdowns. He had the most receiving yards by a Viking since [[Percy Harvin]] in [[2011 Minnesota Vikings season|2011]]. Thielen needed only 40 yards receiving in the Week 17 Bears game to hit 1,000 yards on the season, and only once in the previous six games had he been held under 50 yards. However, he was targeted only once for a seven-yard gain to finish the season with 967 yards, giving the Vikings their first pair of Vikings receivers with 900 yards each since [[Randy Moss]] and [[Cris Carter]] accomplished the feat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Minnesota Vikings – January 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701010min.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Yotter |first=Tim |date=January 18, 2017 |title=Too many factors in Adam Thielen not getting 1,000 yards for Minnesota Vikings |url=http://www.scout.com/nfl/vikings/story/1746907-too-many-factors-in-thielen-not-getting-1-000 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215032934/http://www.scout.com/nfl/vikings/story/1746907-too-many-factors-in-thielen-not-getting-1-000 |archive-date=February 15, 2017 |access-date=February 14, 2017 |website=Scout.com}}</ref>

After having entered the 2016 season as an underdog, Thielen ended up leading the Vikings with 967 receiving yards, while also adding a career-high 69 catches and five touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Minnesota Vikings Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2016.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2016 |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> His 10.0 yards per target and 75.0% catch rate ranked in the top five players among NFL wide receivers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen Advanced Efficiency Stats and Metrics Profile |url=http://www.playerprofiler.com/nfl/adam-thielen |access-date=March 14, 2019 |website=PlayerProfiler.com}}</ref> Thielen dropped only two passes on 92 targets according to Sporting Charts, and [[Pro Football Focus]] ranked him as the 18th best receiver in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coller |first=Matthew |date=February 7, 2017 |title=Adam Thielen's status could throw a wrench in Vikings' free agency plans – 1500 ESPN Twin Cities |url=http://www.1500espn.com/vikings-2/2017/02/adam-thielens-status-throw-wrench-vikings-free-agency-plans/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215022122/http://www.1500espn.com/vikings-2/2017/02/adam-thielens-status-throw-wrench-vikings-free-agency-plans/ |archive-date=February 15, 2017 |access-date=February 14, 2017 |website=1500ESPN}}</ref> For his efforts, [[NFL.com]] named Thielen as their "Unsung Hero" for the Minnesota Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=January 27, 2017 |title=NFC unsung heroes: Giving credit where credit is due |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfc-unsung-heroes-giving-credit-where-credit-is-due-0ap3000000775667 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2017====
[[File:DeAngelo Hall, Adam Thielen (26599714459).jpg|thumb|225px|left|Thielen in a game against the Redskins in 2017]]
On March 15, 2017, Thielen signed a three-year contract extension with the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=March 15, 2017 |title=Vikings bring back Adam Thielen on three-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/vikings-bring-back-adam-thielen-on-three-year-deal-0ap3000000793289 |access-date=March 14, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On September 11, 2017, in the season opener against the [[New Orleans Saints]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Thielen started the season off strong with nine receptions for 157 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Minnesota Vikings – September 11th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709110min.htm |access-date=October 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> In Week 8, Thielen scored his first touchdown of the season against the [[Cleveland Browns]] at [[Twickenham Stadium]], [[London]] from quarterback [[Case Keenum]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Cleveland Browns – October 29th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710290cle.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> During Week 10 against the Redskins, Thielen finished with 166 receiving yards and a touchdown as the Vikings won 38–30. The following week against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Thielen finished the game with six catches for 123 yards, including a 65-yard touchdown reception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Minnesota Vikings – November 19th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711190min.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> During the Week 12 Thanksgiving matchup against division rival, [[Detroit Lions]], Thielen had eight receptions for 89 yards in the Vikings 30–23 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions – November 23rd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711230det.htm |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Thielen's output put him over the 1,000-yard mark for the season. ====2018====
Going into the 2018 season, Thielen had a new quarterback in [[Kirk Cousins]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Benjamin |first=Cody |date=August 5, 2018 |title=Adam Thielen says new Vikings QB Kirk Cousins has been 'phenomenal' entering 2018 |work=CBSSports.com |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/adam-thielen-says-new-vikings-qb-kirk-cousins-has-been-phenomenal-entering-2018/ |access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> He started off the season strong with six receptions for 102 receiving yards in a 24–16 victory over the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 9, 2018 |title=Cousins, Vikings hold on for 24–16 victory vs. 49ers |work=USA TODAY |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2018/09/09/cousins-vikings-hold-on-for-24-16-victory-vs-49ers/37766443/ |access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> He followed that up with a then-career high 12 receptions for 131 receiving yards and a touchdown in the 29–29 tie with the Packers.<ref>{{Cite news |others=RotoWire Staff |date=September 16, 2018 |title=Vikings' Adam Thielen: Leads team in receiving versus Packers |work=CBSSports.com |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/vikings-adam-thielen-leads-team-in-receiving-versus-packers/ |access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> In Week 3, in a 27–6 loss to the [[Buffalo Bills]], he recorded his third consecutive game with at least 100 receiving yards with a career-high 14 receptions for 105 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite news |others=RotoWire Staff |date=September 23, 2018 |title=Vikings' Adam Thielen: Catches 14 passes in loss to Bills |work=CBSSports.com |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/vikings-adam-thielen-catches-14-passes-in-loss-to-bills/ |access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> In Week 4, in a 38–31 loss to the Rams, he had eight receptions for 135 receiving yards and a touchdown. With this fourth consecutive game with at least 100 receiving yards to start the season, he joined [[Randy Moss]] and [[Isaac Bruce]] as the only players in the Super Bowl era to accomplish the feat.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Krammer |first=Andrew |date=September 29, 2018 |title=Adam Thielen, Kirk Cousins join rare company in loss to Rams |work=Star Tribune |url=http://www.startribune.com/adam-thielen-kirk-cousins-join-rare-company-in-loss-to-rams/494667321/ |access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> In Week 5, against the Eagles, Thielen recorded seven catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. He became the first player in the Super Bowl era to record five straight 100-yard receiving games to start a season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=October 7, 2018 |title=Adam Thielen sets NFL record with another 100-yard game |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/10/07/adam-thielen-sets-nfl-record-with-another-100-yard-game/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> In Week 6, against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], he had seven receptions for 123 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 14, 2018 |title=Murray, Vikings trample Cardinals on way to 27–17 victory |work=MPR News |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2018/10/14/murray-vikings-trample-cardinals-on-way-to-2717-victory |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref> In the following game, against the [[New York Jets]], he had nine receptions for 110 yards and a touchdown for this seventh consecutive game topping 100 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ratke |first=Kyle |date=October 21, 2018 |title=Another week, another 100-yard game for Adam Thielen |work=USA Today |url=https://vikingswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/21/another-week-another-100-yard-game-for-adam-thielen/ |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref> As of Week 8, he had 100 yards in each of the first eight games of the year, which is tied with [[Calvin Johnson]] for the record for most consecutive 100 yard games in a year. By doing so, he also broke the record for most consecutive 100 yard games to start a season in NFL history.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ratke |first=Kyle |date=October 29, 2018 |title=Adam Thielen continues to break records |url=https://vikingswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/29/adam-thielen-continues-to-break-records/ |access-date=October 29, 2018 |work=Vikings Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> In Week 9, against the Lions, the streak came to an end when he posted four receptions for 22 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown, which he managed to achieve for the sixth consecutive game.<ref name="x743">{{cite web | last=Busbee | first=Jay | title=Adam Thielen's 100-yard streak ends one game short of record | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=November 4, 2018 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/adam-thielens-100-yard-streak-ends-one-game-short-record-224709271.html | access-date=December 18, 2024}}</ref> In Week 12, against the Green Bay Packers, he recorded eight receptions for 125 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown in the 24–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomasson |first=Chris |date=November 26, 2018 |title=Vikings, Kirk Cousins take to the air to defeat Packers 24–17 |url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/11/25/vikings-kirk-cousins-take-to-the-air-defeat-packers-24-17/ |access-date=December 5, 2018 |website=Twin Cities}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2018 season with 113 receptions for 1,373 receiving yards and nine receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Adam Thielen 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=February 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was ranked #33 by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2019]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2019-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2021====
Thielen entered the 2021 season as a starting wide receiver alongside [[Justin Jefferson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart Archive |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/249/MIN |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=www.ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 1, he had nine catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns in a 27–24 loss to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Cincinnati Bengals – September 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109120cin.htm |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 6, he had a season-high 11 catches for 126 yards and a touchdown in a 34–28 victory over the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Carolina Panthers – October 17th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110170car.htm |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He suffered an ankle injury in Week 13 and missed the next two games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2021 |title=Vikings WR Adam Thielen injury update; plus, more NFL news from Week 13's Sunday games |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2021-nfl-season-notable-injuries-news-sunday-week-13-games |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He returned in Week 16, only to aggravate the injury, which required surgery. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 29, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Rob |date=December 29, 2021 |title=Vikings' Adam Thielen Placed on IR After Reported Surgery on Ankle Injury |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10022137-vikings-adam-thielen-placed-on-ir-after-reported-surgery-on-ankle-injury |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with 67 catches for 726 receiving yards and ten receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2022====
Thielen returned in 2022 as a starting wide receiver alongside Jefferson.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Minnesota Vikings Roster & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2022_roster.htm |access-date=May 31, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He started all 17 games, recording 70 catches for 716 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=November 13, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Following the 2022 season, the Vikings released Thielen on March 10, 2023, as a salary cap move.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=March 10, 2023 |title=Vikings Release Adam Thielen Ahead of 2023 Free Agency |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/adam-thielen-released-roster-cut-free-agency |access-date=March 10, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On March 19, 2023, Thielen signed a three-year $25 million contract with the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Callihan |first=Schuyler |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Breakdown of Adam Thielen's Contract with the Carolina Panthers |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/panthers/gm-report/breakdown-of-adam-thielens-contract-with-the-carolina-panthers |access-date=November 13, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> In a Week 3 loss to the Seahawks, he had 11 receptions for 145 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Seattle Seahawks – September 24th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309240sea.htm |access-date=November 13, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a Week 5 loss to the Lions, he had 11 receptions for 107 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Detroit Lions – October 8th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310080det.htm |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a Week 6 loss to the Dolphins, he had 11 receptions for 115 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Miami Dolphins – October 15th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310150mia.htm |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2023 season starting all 17 games and recording with 103 receptions for 1,014 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He recorded his first 100-reception and 1,000-yard season since 2018.

In Week 17 of the 2024 season, Thielen had five receptions for 110 yards and two touchdowns against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 29th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202412290tam.htm |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 season, Thielen appeared in ten games. He finished with 48 receptions for 615 yards and five touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (second stint)===
On August 27, 2025, the Panthers traded Thielen, a conditional 2026 seventh-round pick, and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 fourth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gantt|first=Darin|title=Panthers agree to trade Adam Thielen to the Vikings|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-agree-to-trade-adam-thielen-to-the-vikings-draft-picks|date=August 27, 2025|access-date=August 27, 2025|website=Panthers.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Young|first=Lindsey|title=Vikings Returning Adam Thielen to Minnesota in Trade with Carolina Panthers|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/adam-thielen-acquired-trade-carolina-panthers-wide-receiver-2025|website=Vikings.com|date=August 27, 2025|access-date=August 27, 2025}}</ref> After playing in a limited role throughout the 2025 season and recording eight catches for 69 yards in 11 games,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adam Thielen 2025 Game Log|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=December 1, 2025|language=en}}</ref> the Vikings granted Thielen's request to be waived on December 1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=December 1, 2025 |title=Vikings Waive Receiver Adam Thielen |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/adam-thielen-wide-receiver-waived-released-2025 |access-date=December 1, 2025 |website=Vikings.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On December 2, 2025, Thielen was claimed off waivers by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=December 2, 2025 |title=Steelers make multiple roster moves |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-multiple-roster-moves-x8951 |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He made five appearances (three starts) for Pittsburgh, recording 11 receptions for 117 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Thielen 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThieAd00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On January 14, 2026, Thielen announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=January 14, 2026 |title=Adam Thielen announces his retirement |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/adam-thielen-announces-his-retirement |access-date=January 14, 2026 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>
