'''Adrian Paul Hardy ''' (born August 16, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He was selected by the 49ers in the second round of the [[1993 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Northwestern State Demons football|Northwestern State Demons]].

==Early life==
Adrian Paul Hardy was born on August 16, 1970, in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He attended [[Redeemer High School]] in New Orleans.<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/h/hard02600.html | title=Adrian Hardy | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=20 December 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Hardy was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Northwestern State Demons football|Northwestern State Demons]] of [[Northwestern State University]] from 1989 to 1992.<ref name="Pfa"/> He earned first-team All-[[Southland Conference]] honors in 1991 and 1992 while also being named an [[All-American]] in 1992.<ref name="Bio"/> He blocked ten kicks during his college career.<ref name="Bio"/> Hardy played in the [[Hula Bowl]] after his senior season.<ref name="Bio"/> He was inducted into the school's N-Club Hall of Fame in 2014.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web | url=https://nsudemons.com/honors/n-club-hall-of-fame/adrian-hardy/241 | title=Adrian Hardy | publisher=nsudemons.com | accessdate=20 December 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Hardy was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the second round, with the 48th overall pick, of the [[1993 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HardAd20.htm | title=Adrian Hardy | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=20 December 2024}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on July 12.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in ten games for the 49ers during his rookie year in 1993.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in two games in 1994 before being waived on September 15, 1994.<ref name="PST">{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Adrian+Hardy&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=20 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="Pfr"/>

Hardy was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on September 16, 1994.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 14 games for the Bengals during the 1994 season, returning eight kicks for 185 yards and recovering one fumble.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was waived on August 27, 1995.<ref name="PST"/><ref name="transactions"/> He was re-signed by the Bengals on September 25 and appeared in ten games for them during the 1995 season.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/> Hardy was released on March 22, 1996.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/h/hard02600.html | title=Adrian Hardy NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=20 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Adarius Taylor''' (born ''' Adarius Glanton'''; September 21, 1990) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Cleveland Browns]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Eastern Arizona College]] and [[Florida Atlantic University]]. He also played for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life==
Taylor participated in football, track and basketball at [[Lake Gibson High School]] in [[Lakeland, Florida]].<ref name="A">{{cite web | url=http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adarius_glanton_802250.html | title=Adarius Glanton | publisher=fausports.com | access-date=October 20, 2014 | archive-date=September 21, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921122112/http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adarius_glanton_802250.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Taylor first enrolled at [[Iowa Western Community College]] before transferring to [[Eastern Arizona College]], where he played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Arizona College]] Gila Monsters.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://goreivers.com/sports/fball/2009-10/bios/glanton_adarius_gwsd | title=Adarius Glanton | publisher=[[Iowa Western Community College]] | accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref> He was named first-team All-Conference and All-Region as a sophomore, recording 85 tackles, 5.5 sacks, and two forced fumbles.<ref name="A"/> He later transferred to play for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic Owls]] from 2012 to 2013.<ref name="A"/>

===Carolina Panthers (first stint)===
====2014====
On May 10, 2014, the [[Carolina Panthers]] signed Taylor to a three-year, $1.53 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $16,000.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Adarius Taylor contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/tampa-bay-buccaneers/adarius-glanton-15704/ |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> Throughout training camp, Taylor competed for a roster spot against [[Anthony Morales]], [[Jason Williams (American football)|Jason Williams]], and [[Denicos Allen]]. On August 30, 2014, Taylor was waived as part of the Panthers' final roster cuts, but was signed to the team's practice squad on September 1, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/29986/nfl/news |title=Adarius Glanton |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=October 20, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204190538/http://www.kffl.com/player/29986/nfl/news |archive-date=December 4, 2014 }}</ref>

On October 19, 2014, Taylor made his professional regular season debut as the Panthers' lost 38–17 at the [[2014 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adariusglanton/2550565/gamelogs | title=Adarius Glanton | work=[[NFL.com]] | access-date=October 20, 2014}}</ref> On December 21, 2014, Taylor earned his first career start in place of [[A. J. Klein]] who sustained an ankle injury the previous week. Taylor finished the Panthers' 17–13 win against the [[2014 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] with a season-high six combined tackles.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Carolina Panthers: Adarius Glanton|url = http://www.panthers.com/team/roster/adarius-glanton/35365c3d-6447-455c-a9fb-15a622979393/|website = www.panthers.com|access-date = December 28, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151228182738/http://www.panthers.com/team/roster/adarius-glanton/35365c3d-6447-455c-a9fb-15a622979393/|archive-date = December 28, 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref> In Week 17, Taylor recorded five combined tackles and forced the first fumble of his career during a 34–3 win at the [[2014 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Panthers vs. Falcons - Game Recap - December 28, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554404|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 28, 2015}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in [[2014 NFL season|2014]] with 12 combined tackles (eight solo) in ten games and two starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Adarius Taylor (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adariustaylor/2550565/careerstats |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015====
Taylor entered training camp as a backup linebacker and competed for a roster spot against [[A. J. Klein|A.J. Klein]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carolina Huddle: Panthers roster projection |url=https://www.wcnc.com/mobile/article/sports/nfl/panthers/carolina-huddle-panthers-roster-projection/213128462 |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=Wcnc.com |date=August 4, 2015}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, the Carolina Panthers released Taylor as part of their final roster cuts and signed him to their practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/09/05/panthers-cut-jordan-todman-jason-trusnik-in-moves-to-53/ |title=Panthers cut Jordan Todman, Jason Trusnik in moves to 53 |publisher=profootballtalk.nbcsports.com |date=September 5, 2015 |access-date=September 6, 2015 |author=Gantt, Darin |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906051704/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/09/05/panthers-cut-jordan-todman-jason-trusnik-in-moves-to-53/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article34255032.html |title=Brenton Bersin, Damiere Byrd make Panthers' practice squad |publisher=charlotteobserver.com |date=September 6, 2015 |access-date=September 7, 2015 |author=Jones, Jonathan |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907154325/http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article34255032.html |archive-date=September 7, 2015 }}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
====2015====
On November 30, 2015, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] signed Taylor off the Panthers' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-LB-Adarius-Glanton-from-Panthers/125043b8-c669-4dc0-b561-5ea206e1647e |title=Bucs Sign LB Adarius Glanton from Panthers |publisher=buccaneers.com |date=November 30, 2015 |access-date=November 30, 2015 |author=Smith, Scott |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151201025804/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-LB-Adarius-Glanton-from-Panthers/125043b8-c669-4dc0-b561-5ea206e1647e |archive-date=December 1, 2015 }}</ref> Head coach [[Lovie Smith]] named Taylor the third middle linebacker on the depth chart, behind [[Kwon Alexander]] and [[Bruce Carter (American football)|Bruce Carter]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 12/01/2015 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/178/TB |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Taylor appeared in five games, primarily on special teams, and did not record a statistic during the [[2015 NFL season]].<ref name="career"/><ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Adarius Taylor (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adariustaylor/2550565/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2016====
On January 6, 2016, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers announced their decision to fire head coach [[Lovie Smith]] after they finished with a 9–7 record and did not qualify for the playoffs in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers fire Lovie Smith |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tampa-bay-buccaneers-fire-lovie-smith-0ap3000000618589 |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=January 6, 2016}}</ref> On January 15, 2016, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers officially promoted offensive coordinator [[Dirk Koetter]] to head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buccaneers announce promotion of Dirk Koetter to head coach |url=https://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2016/01/buccaneers_promote_dirk_koette.html |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=Nola.com |date=January 15, 2016}}</ref> During training camp in 2016, Taylor competed for a roster spot as a backup middle linebacker against [[Luke Rhodes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Big Night For Backup Bucs LBs Trying To Survive Cuts |url=https://www.pewterreport.com/big-night-backup-bucs-lbs-trying-survive-cuts/ |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=pewterreport.com |last=Horchy |first=Eric |date=August 26, 2016 |archive-date=October 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161027200411/http://www.pewterreport.com/big-night-backup-bucs-lbs-trying-survive-cuts/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On November 3, 2016, Taylor collected a season-high six solo tackles during the Buccaneers' 43–28 loss against the [[2016 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Adarius Taylor (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adariustaylor/2550565/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On January 1, 2017, against the Carolina Panthers, [[long snapper]] [[Andrew DePaola]] suffered a torn ACL late in the third quarter. Taylor then served as the long snapper for a successful extra point late in the fourth quarter to help the Buccaneers win by a score of 17–16.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/bucs-panthers-how-a-backup-long-snapper-with-a-broken-finger-helped-the/2308082/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904005850/http://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/bucs-panthers-how-a-backup-long-snapper-with-a-broken-finger-helped-the/2308082 | url-status=live | archive-date=September 4, 2017 | title=Bucs-Panthers: How backup long snapper with broken finger helped Bucs win | publisher=tampabay.com | date=January 1, 2017 | access-date=September 3, 2017 | author=Auman, Gerg}}</ref> He finished the [[2016 NFL season]] with 13 combined tackles (11 solo) in 16 games and zero starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2017====
On February 28, 2017, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers assigned a one-year, $690,000 tender to Taylor as a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs tender WR Adam Humphries, 3 others for 2017|url=http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/bucs/bucs-tender-wr-adam-humphries-3-others-for-2017/2314729|author=Auman, Greg|website=TampaBay.com|date=February 27, 2017|access-date=February 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307072626/http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/bucs/bucs-tender-wr-adam-humphries-3-others-for-2017/2314729|archive-date=March 7, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> On April 18, 2017, Taylor signed his one-year, $690,000 restricted free agent tender to remain with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Transactions: April 18, 2017 |url=https://landryfootball.com/nfl-notebook-april-18-2017/?print=print |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=LandryFootball.com| date=April 18, 2017 }}</ref> Throughout training camp, Taylor competed against [[Devante Bond]], [[Kendell Beckwith]], and [[Cameron Lynch]] to be the starting strongside linebacker after it was left vacant by the departure of [[Daryl Smith (linebacker)|Daryl Smith]].<ref>{{cite web |title=5 Potential Under-the-Radar X-Factors|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/5-potential-under-the-radar-x-factors-18932041 |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=Buccaneers.com |date=June 6, 2017}}</ref> Head coach Dirk Koetter named Taylor the backup middle linebacker, behind Kwon Alexander, to begin the regular season in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 10/01/2017 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/200/TB |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 3, Taylor collected a season-high eight combined tackles during a 34–17 loss at the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]]. On October 5, 2017, Taylor recorded seven combined tackles, forced a fumble, and made his first career sack during a 19–14 loss against the [[2017 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in Week 5. Taylor sacked Patriots' quarterback [[Tom Brady]] for a six-yard loss in the third quarter and forced a fumble by Brady that was recovered by teammate [[Will Clarke (American football)|Will Clarke]].<ref>{{cite web |title= New England Patriots at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - October 5th, 2017|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710050tam. |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 18, 2017, Taylor started in place of [[Lavonte David]] who was inactive due to a hamstring injury and made four combined tackles before being carted off the field during the third quarter of the Buccaneers' 24–21 loss against the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] in Week 15. Taylor sustained a broken [[tibia]] and [[fibula]] after colliding with teammate [[Robert Ayers]] as both attempted to sack Falcons' quarterback [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bucs' Adarius Glanton suffers broken left leg |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/21816686/adarius-glanton-tampa-bay-buccaneers-suffers-broken-left-leg-surgery |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |last=Laine |first=Jenna |date=December 19, 2017}}</ref> On December 20, 2017, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers officially placed Taylor on injured reserve. Taylor finished the [[2017 NFL season]] with 31 combined tackles (22 solo), one pass deflection, and one sack in 14 games and four starts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Standout Rookies Among Five Bucs Headed to IR|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Standout-Rookies-Among-Five-Bucs-Headed-to-IR/b5203974-8b43-4612-a385-24deb30cb4e4|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=December 20, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223235108/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Standout-Rookies-Among-Five-Bucs-Headed-to-IR/b5203974-8b43-4612-a385-24deb30cb4e4|archive-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref>

====2018====
During training camp, Taylor competed against [[Devante Bond]] to be the starting strongside linebacker. The role was left vacant after [[Kendell Beckwith]] sustained a broken ankle during a car accident.<ref>{{cite web |title=Taylor, Bond enter camp with a chance to start |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2018/7/24/17600458/taylor-bond-enter-tampa-bay-buccaneers-camp-with-a-chance-to-start |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=BucsNation.com |last=Marks |first=Kyle |date=July 24, 2018}}</ref> Head coach Dirk Koetter named Taylor the strongside linebacker to begin the regular season, alongside Lavonte David and middle linebacker Kwon Alexander.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 10/01/2018 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/212/TB |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 9, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles (four solo) during a 42–28 loss at the [[2018 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Adarius Taylor (2018) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adariustaylor/2550565/gamelogs?season=2018 |access-date=December 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On March 14, 2019, Taylor signed a two-year contract with the Cleveland Browns.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shook |first1=Nick |title=Browns add depth in linebacker Adarius Taylor |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-add-depth-in-linebacker-adarius-taylor |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=March 14, 2019}}</ref>

Taylor was released by the Browns on February 17, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns release 4 players |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-release-4-players |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=February 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers (second stint)===
On July 27, 2020, Taylor was signed by the Panthers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign Adarius Taylor, waive Austrian Robinson|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/adarius-taylor-signed-austrian-robinson-waived-carolina|author=Simmons, Myles|website=Panthers.com|date=July 27, 2020}}</ref> He played in nine games before being placed on injured reserve on November 11.<ref>{{cite news |author=Weaver, Tim |title=Panthers sign RB Reggie Bonnafon to active roster, place LB on IR |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/11/panthers-reggie-bonnafon-active-adarius-taylor-injured-reserve/ |website=USAToday.com |date=November 11, 2020 |access-date=December 17, 2020}}</ref> Taylor was activated off of injured reserve on December 12.<ref>{{cite news |author=Bryan, Will |title=Panthers activate linebacker Adarius Taylor from reserve/injured list |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-activate-linebacker-adarius-taylor-from-reserve-injured-list |website=Panthers.com |date=December 12, 2020 |access-date=December 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Calgary Stampeders===
On September 26, 2023, Taylor was signed to the practice roster of the [[Calgary Stampeders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stampeders.com/2023/09/26/stamps-add-five-to-expanded-practice-roster/ |title=Stamps Add Five To Expanded Practice Roster |publisher=[[Calgary Stampeders]] |date=September 26, 2023}}</ref> He was later promoted to the active roster and dressed in three games for the Stampeders during the season, recording five tackles on defense, three tackles on special teams, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://profootballarchives.com/players/t/tayl00155.html | title=ADARIUS TAYLOR | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=17 May 2025}}</ref> Taylor was released by the Stampeders on November 16.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/adarius-taylor-glantad01/transactions | title=Adarius Taylor | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=14 August 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Taylor had his last name changed to honor his father Basil George Taylor who died when Taylor was 16 years old. Before he changed his last name, it was Glanton, which is his mother's last name. Taylor's father was born in St. Catherine, Jamaica and immigrated to the US in 1979.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adarius Glanton Changes Last Name to Taylor|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/adarius-glanton-changes-last-name-to-taylor-20505850|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=April 3, 2018}}</ref>

In May 2025, Taylor was arrested and charged with negligent child abuse and solicitation of prostitution.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2025/05/16/ex-nfl-linebacker-among-255-arrested-in-polk-human-trafficking-sting-sheriff-says/ | title=Ex-NFL linebacker among 255 arrested in Polk human-trafficking sting | work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] | date=May 16, 2025 | accessdate=16 May 2025 | author=Morgan, Silas}}</ref>

'''Adrian Phillips''' (born March 28, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and joined the [[History of the San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]] as an undrafted free agent in 2014. During the 2018 season, he earned [[Pro Bowl]] and first-team [[All-Pro]] honors as a [[special teamer]]. Phillips joined the [[New England Patriots]] in 2020.

==Early life==
Phillips played [[high school football]] at [[Garland High School]] in [[Garland, Texas]]. Phillips was an all-state, all-area and two-time first-team all-district selection while playing offense and defense for the Owls. He was a member of [[ESPNU]]'s top 150 national prospects, ranked as the 14th-best athlete by ESPNU and 25th-best athlete by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. He recorded 72 receptions for 1,307 yards and 14 TDs, 1,111 rushing yards, 14 rushing TDs, 949 passing yards, five passing touchdowns, 87 tackles, a forced fumble, and three interceptions.<ref name="A">{{Cite web |title=ADRIAN PHILLIPS |url=http://www.texassports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4412 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907033448/http://www.texassports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4412 |archive-date=September 7, 2015 |access-date=November 3, 2014 |website=TexasSports.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Phillips played for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] from 2010 to 2013. He played in 50 games, starting 28. He was a 2013 honorable mention All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] coaches choice. Phillips had 206 career tackles and was a team captain in the 2013 season.<ref name="A" />

===San Diego / Los Angeles Chargers===
====2014 season====
On June 16, 2014, the [[San Diego Chargers]] signed Phillips after he went undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=June 16, 2014 |title=Chargers Sign DB Adrian Phillips; Waive D.J. Adams |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2014/06/16/chargers-sign-db-adrian-phillips-waive-dj-adams |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025131911/http://www.chargers.com/news/2014/06/16/chargers-sign-db-adrian-phillips-waive-dj-adams |archive-date=October 25, 2017 |access-date=May 28, 2017 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> On August 31, 2014, the San Diego Chargers waived Phillips. After clearing waivers, he was signed to their practice squad. On September 23, 2014, Phillips was waived from the Chargers' practice squad. On September 29, 2014, the San Diego Chargers' re-signed Phillips to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Diego Chargers Transactions (2014) |url=https://www.chargers.com/team/transactions/2014 |access-date=July 28, 2020 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> On October 1, 2014, Phillips was released from the Chargers' practice squad, but he was re-signed to the practice squad on October 7, 2014. On November 1, 2014, the San Diego Chargers promoted Phillips to the active roster. On November 2, 2014, Phillips made his professional regular season debut and recorded one tackle during a 37–0 loss at the [[Miami Dolphins]] in Week 9.<ref name="Z">{{Cite web |title=Adrian Phillips |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/30341/nfl/news |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204211927/http://www.kffl.com/player/30341/nfl/news |archive-date=December 4, 2014 |access-date=November 3, 2014 |website=kffl.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Phillips |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adrianphillips/2550842/gamelogs |access-date=November 3, 2014 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 3, 2014, the San Diego Chargers released Phillips, but re-signed him to their practice squad the following day.<ref name="Z" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Padaon, Ernie |date=November 4, 2014 |title=San Diego Chargers Re-Sign Adrian Phillips To Practice Squad |url=http://boltbeat.com/2014/11/04/san-diego-chargers-re-sign-adrian-phillips-practice-squad/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907033446/http://boltbeat.com/2014/11/04/san-diego-chargers-re-sign-adrian-phillips-practice-squad/ |archive-date=September 7, 2015 |access-date=November 4, 2014 |website=BoltBeat.com}}</ref> On November 29, 2014, the San Diego Chargers released Phillips and re-signed him to their practice squad on December 2, 2014.<ref name="Z" /> He finished his rookie campaign with one tackle and appeared in three games.

====2015 season====
Phillips entered training camp slated as a backup safety and competed for a roster spot against [[Gordon Hill (American football)|Gordon Hill]] and [[Johnny Lowdermilk]]. On September 5, 2015, the San Diego Chargers released Phillips, but subsequently signed him to their practice squad the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Fantasy Football Breaking News |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NFL&id=5419&line=316713&spln=1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905195326/http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NFL&id=5419&line=316713&spln=1 |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |access-date=September 5, 2015 |website=Rotoworld.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gehlken, Michael |date=September 6, 2015 |title=Chargers place nine on practice squad |url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/2015/sep/06/chargers-nfl-practice-squad-krasovic-javontee/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907032724/http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/2015/sep/06/chargers-nfl-practice-squad-krasovic-javontee/ |archive-date=September 7, 2015 |access-date=September 6, 2015 |website=SanDiegoUnionTribune.com}}</ref> On October 12, 2015, the San Diego Chargers released Phillips from their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=October 12, 2015 |title=Bolts Activate Antonio Gates, Waive Adrian Phillips |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2015/10/12/bolts-activate-antonio-gates-waive-adrian-phillips |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151013181532/http://www.chargers.com/news/2015/10/12/bolts-activate-antonio-gates-waive-adrian-phillips |archive-date=October 13, 2015 |access-date=October 13, 2015 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> On October 14, 2015, the Chargers re-signed him to their practice squad. On October 20, 2015, the San Diego Chargers signed him to their active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ADRIAN PHILLIPS |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/adrian-phillips-player-transactions |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021225223/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/adrian-phillips-player-transactions |archive-date=October 21, 2015 |access-date=October 21, 2015 |website=FoxSports.com}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Throughout training camp, Phillips competed for roster spot as a backup safety against [[Dexter McCoil]], [[Darrell Stuckey]], and Adrian MacDonald.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 28, 2016 |title=2016 Training Camp Preview: Safeties |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/2016-training-camp-preview-safeties-133796 |access-date=July 28, 2020 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Mike McCoy (American football coach)|Mike McCoy]] named Phillips the backup strong safety to begin the regular season, behind [[Jahleel Addae]].

Phillips was inactive as a healthy scratch for the first two games (Weeks 1–2). On October 2, 2016, Phillips recorded three combined tackles, a pass deflection, and made his first career interception during a 35–34 loss against the [[New Orleans Saints]]. Phillips intercepted a pass attempt by [[Drew Brees]], that was originally intended for wide receiver [[Michael Thomas (wide receiver, born 1993)|Michael Thomas]], during the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at San Diego Chargers – October 2nd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610020sdg.htm |access-date=July 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 10, Phillips recorded a season-high seven combined tackles (six solo) during a 31–24 loss against the Dolphins. He finished the [[2016 NFL season]] 38 combined tackles (25 solo), three pass deflections, and one interception in 14 games and five starts.

====2017 season====
On September 11, 2017, in the season opener against the [[Denver Broncos]] on ''Monday Night Football'', Phillips had an interception off of quarterback [[Trevor Siemian]] that helped set up a scoring drive for the Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers at Denver Broncos – September 11th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709110den.htm |access-date=October 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> He played in 15 games with four starts as the No. 3 safety behind [[Jahleel Addae]] and [[Tre Boston]].

====2018 season====
On March 14, 2018, Phillips re-signed with the Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Bolts Agree to New Contract with Adrian Phillips |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-agree-to-new-contract-with-adrian-phillips-164056 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He played in 16 games with seven starts, recording a career-high 94 combined tackles, nine passes defensed, one interception, and a forced fumble. He was named to his first Pro Bowl and was named first-team All-Pro, both as a special teamer.

====2019 season====
On March 15, 2019, Phillips re-signed with the Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne, Ricky |date=March 15, 2019 |title=He's Back! Bolts Agree to Terms with Pro Bowl and All-Pro S Adrian Phillips |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/he-s-back-bolts-agree-to-terms-with-pro-bowl-and-all-pro-s-adrian-phillips |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He entered the season as a starting safety following an injury to [[Derwin James]]. He suffered a broken arm in Week 2 and was placed on injured reserve on September 17, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Chargers Announce Pair of Signings |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-pair-of-signings |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> He was designated for return from injured reserve on November 14, 2019, and began practicing with the team again. He was activated on November 30.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 2019 |title=Chargers Activate Derwin James and Adrian Phillips |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-activate-derwin-james-and-adrian-phillips |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 21, 2020, the [[New England Patriots]] signed Phillips to a two-year, $6 million contract that includes $3 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $1.50 million.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dussault, Mike |date=March 19, 2020 |title=Report: Patriots sign safety Adrian Phillips |work=Patriots.com |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/report-patriots-sign-safety-adrian-phillips |access-date=March 22, 2020}}</ref>

Phillips made his debut with the Patriots in Week 1 against the Dolphins.  During the game, Phillips intercepted a pass thrown by [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] in the 21–11 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dolphins vs. Patriots – Box Score – September 13, 2020 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=401220131}}</ref>
In Week 15 against the Miami Dolphins, Phillips recorded his first career sack on [[Tua Tagovailoa]] during the 22–12 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins – December 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012200mia.htm |access-date=December 20, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 8 of the 2021 season, Phillips had three tackles and two interceptions, including a 26-yard pick-six, in a 27–24 win over his former team, the Chargers, earning AFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon, Grant |date=November 3, 2021 |title=Jets QB Mike White, 49ers WR Deebo Samuel among NFL Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jets-qb-mike-white-49ers-wr-deebo-samuel-among-nfl-players-of-the-week |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On January 1, 2022, Phillips signed a three-year contract extension with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss, Mike |date=January 1, 2022 |title=Source: New England Patriots, versatile safety Adrian Phillips agree to three-year extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32973381/source-new-england-patriots-key-safety-adrian-phillips-agree-three-year-extension |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was released on February 19, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2024-02-19 |title=Patriots Releasing DL Lawrence Guy & S Adrian Phillips |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/patriots-releasing-dl-lawrence-guy-s-adrian-phillips/ |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Adoree' K. Jackson''' (born September 18, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] and [[return specialist]]. He played [[college football]] for the  [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning the [[Jim Thorpe Award]] and the [[Jet Award]] during his junior season in 2016. He was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the first round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. Jackson spent four seasons with the Titans before signing with the Giants in 2021.

==Early life==
Jackson was born on September 18, 1995, in [[Belleville, Illinois]]. During his freshman year in high school, he attended [[Belleville East High School]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Klein |first=Gary |date=December 3, 2015 |title=USC's Adoree' Jackson never forgets the 618 area code |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/la-sp-usc-adoree-jackson-20151204-story.html |access-date=April 27, 2018 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> He moved to [[California]] prior to his sophomore year in high school.<ref name="latimes">{{Cite web |last=Sondheimer |first=Eric |date=August 21, 2013 |title=Serra's Adoree' Jackson aims to be unforgettable in every way |url=https://articles.latimes.com/2013/aug/21/sports/la-sp-0821-adoree-jackson-db-20130821 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130918075142/http://articles.latimes.com/2013/aug/21/sports/la-sp-0821-adoree-jackson-db-20130821 |archive-date=September 18, 2013 |access-date=February 11, 2015 |publisher=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Jackson attended [[Junípero Serra High School (Gardena, California)|Junípero Serra High School]] in [[Gardena, California]]. He played numerous positions including [[wide receiver]], [[running back]], [[defensive back]], and [[return specialist]]. Jackson was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a five-star recruit and was ranked as the number one athlete and sixth best player overall in his class.<ref name="yahoo">{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson – Yahoo! Sports |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Adoree'-Jackson-133916 |access-date=February 11, 2015 |publisher=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) to play [[college football]].<ref name="si">{{cite web |last=Ellis |first=Zac |date=February 5, 2014 |title=Five-star athlete Adoree' Jackson commits to USC over UCLA, Florida, LSU |url=https://www.si.com/college/2014/02/05/adoree-jackson-picks-usc-over-ucla-florida-lsu |access-date=April 29, 2026 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Jackson also played [[basketball]] and ran [[track and field]] in high school.<ref name="dailynews">{{Cite web |date=June 1, 2012 |title=Serra's Adoree' Jackson a contender for multiple state track titles |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20120601/serras-adoree-jackson-a-contender-for-multiple-state-track-titles |access-date=February 11, 2015 |website=Los Angeles Daily News}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Adoree' Jackson USC2015.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Jackson playing for USC in [[2015 USC Trojans football team|2015]].]] Jackson majored in communications with a real estate minor at USC.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson |url=http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Adoree'-Jackson/b378e61f-2f3b-47ab-a9e0-b85f78f76e4f |access-date=February 20, 2018 |website=Tennessee Titans}}</ref> Jackson played in 12 games as a [[true freshman]] in 2014. He played [[cornerback]], wide receiver, and return specialist. He was the [[Pac-12 Conference]] Freshman of the Year.<ref name="usctrojans">{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2014 |title=Adoree' Jackson Named Pac-12 Freshman Defensive Player Of Year |url=http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120214aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055950/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120214aaa.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=February 11, 2015 |website=USC Trojans Athletics}}</ref><ref name="foxsports">{{cite web |date=December 2, 2014 |title=USC's Jackson earns Pac-12 Freshman Defensive Player of the Year honors |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/uscs-jackson-earns-pac-12-freshman-defensive-player-of-the-year-honors |access-date=April 29, 2026 |publisher=FOX Sports}}</ref> In the [[2014 Holiday Bowl]], he had a 98-yard kickoff return [[touchdown]] and a 71-yard touchdown [[football catch|reception]] in USC's 45–42 win.<ref name="nfl">{{Cite web |title=USC's Adoree Jackson shines in Holiday Bowl win vs. Nebraska |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/usc-s-adoree-jackson-shines-in-holiday-bowl-win-vs-nebraska-0ap3000000449683|date=December 27, 2014 |access-date=January 31, 2022|website=nfl.com}}</ref> He finished his freshman season with 50 tackles, three receiving touchdowns, and two return touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree Jackson 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adoree-jackson-1/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Jackson was named a [[Freshman All-American]] by [[Football Writers Association of America]]<ref name="sportswriters">{{Cite web |title=FWAA > News > Freshman All-America Team |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2014/allamerica150114.html |access-date=February 11, 2015 |publisher=sportswriters.net}}</ref> and [[Pac-12 Conference football individual awards|Pac-12 Defensive Freshman of the Year]] by the Pac-12 coaches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2014/12/02/pac-12-football-all-conference-team-announced|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141203163205/http://pac-12.com/article/2014/12/02/pac-12-football-all-conference-team-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 3, 2014|title = Pac-12 football All-Conference team announced {{pipe}} Pac-12}}</ref>

In the 2015 season, Jackson finished with 27 receptions for 414 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns. In addition, he recorded two punt return touchdowns and one interception return for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree Jackson 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adoree-jackson-1/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Jackson placed fifth<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tfrrs.org/results/41405_2568045.html|title=TFRRS {{pipe}} NCAA Division I Outdoor Track & Field Championships Track & Field Meet Results}}</ref> in the long jump (almost 26 feet) and 4th in the 4×100 meters 2015 [[NCAA]] outdoor track and field championship earning two All-American awards. He also won the 2015 [[Pac-12 Conference]] Championship long jump.

On November 12, 2016, Jackson intercepted two passes from [[2016 Washington Huskies football team|Washington]]'s quarterback [[Jake Browning]], helping the Trojans win their fifth straight game and upset the fourth-ranked Huskies, who were undefeated at the time.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 13, 2016 |title=Sam Darnold leads USC to 26-13 upset of No. 4 Washington |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2016/11/12/sam-darnold-leads-usc-to-26-13-upset-of-no-4-washington/ |access-date=January 31, 2022 |website=The Denver Post|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On December 8, 2016, Jackson was awarded the 2016 [[Jim Thorpe Award]] as the nation's top defensive back.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson Wins 2016 Thorpe Award |url=https://usctrojans.com/news/2016/12/8/Adoree_amp_8217_Jackson_Wins_2016_Thorpe_Award |website=USC Athletics |access-date=January 31, 2022 |date=December 8, 2016}}</ref>

On January 16, 2017, Jackson announced he would forgo his senior season and enter the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Bonagura | first=Kyle | title=USC CB Adoree' Jackson says he will enter NFL draft | website=ESPN.com | date=January 16, 2017 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2017/story/_/id/18489163/jim-thorpe-award-winner-adoree-jackson-usc-trojans-enter-draft | access-date=April 29, 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On March 22, 2017, Jackson participated at USC's [[Pro Day]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jennifer Lee Chan |date=March 23, 2017 |title=All 32 NFL teams represented at USC Pro Day |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2017/3/23/15033338/usc-pro-day-recap-32-nfl-teams-represented-49ers-juju-smith-schuster |access-date=November 6, 2017 |website=ninersnation.com}}</ref> He ran positional drills and completed the three-cone drill, while also meeting with team representatives and scouts from all 32 NFL teams. Jackson was ranked the tenth best cornerback in the draft by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', ranked the seventh best cornerback by [[ESPN]], ranked the sixth best by NFLDraftScout.com, was ranked the fifth best cornerback by NFL analyst [[Mike Mayock]], and was ranked the second best cornerback by NFL analyst [[Bucky Brooks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chris Burke |date=April 24, 2017 |title=2017 NFL draft rankings: Top prospects by position |url=https://www.si.com/2017-nfl-draft-position-rankings |access-date=May 18, 2017 |website=si.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeff Legwold |date=April 22, 2017 |title=Ranking the 2017 Draft's Top 100 Players |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2017/story/_/id/19180310/ranking-top-100-prospects-available-2017-nfl-draft-espn-nfl-nation-reporter-jeff-legwold |access-date=May 18, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=*Adoree Jackson |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/pyrnotes.php?pyid=130700&draftyear=2017&genpos=CB |access-date=May 18, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Mike Mayock |date=April 12, 2017 |title=Mike Mayock's 2017 NFL Draft position rankings 3.0 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-mayock-s-2017-nfl-draft-position-rankings-3-0-0ap3000000799336 |access-date=January 31, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=[[Bucky Brooks]] |date=April 25, 2017 |title=Bucky Brooks' top 5 2017 NFL Draft prospects by position 3.0 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bucky-brooks-top-5-2017-nfl-draft-prospects-by-position-3-0-0ap3000000802450 |access-date=January 31, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

=== Tennessee Titans ===

====2017 season====
[[File:Adoree' Jackson in 2017.jpg|thumb|175px|Jackson in 2017]]
The [[Tennessee Titans]] selected Jackson in the first round (18th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=April 27, 2017 |title=Titans Select USC Defensive Back Adoree' Jackson 18th Overall |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-select-usc-defensive-back-adoree-jackson-18th-overall-18784302 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170428045709/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Select-USC-Defensive-Back-Adoree%E2%80%99-Jackson-18th-Overall/26025e43-39d2-428e-8ff5-5e58d75c7127 |archive-date=April 28, 2017 |access-date=January 31, 2022 |website=Tennessee Titans}}</ref>

On May 23, 2017, the Titans signed Jackson to a fully guaranteed four-year, $11.28 million contract that also includes a signing bonus of $6.34 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Adoree Jackson |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/tennessee-titans/adoree-jackson-21759/ |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref> He competed with [[Logan Ryan]], [[LeShaun Sims]], [[Brice McCain]], and [[Kalan Reed]] throughout training camp for the vacant starting cornerback positions after the departure of [[Jason McCourty]] and [[Perrish Cox]] during the off season. Head coach [[Mike Mularkey]] named him the starting cornerback, opposite Logan Ryan, and punt returner to begin the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans' depth chart: 09/01/2017 |url=http://www.Titans.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/TEN |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=ourlads.com}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans' depth chart |url=http://m.titansonline.com/team/depth-chart.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107222524/http://m.titansonline.com/team/depth-chart.html |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=Tennessee Titans}}</ref>

Jackson made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [[Oakland Raiders]]. He recorded four solo tackles, two pass deflections, and 40 return yards in a 16–26 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Tennessee Titans – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100oti.htm |access-date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson Hurdles Raiders Defenders |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/video/adoree-jackson-hurdles-raiders-defenders-19345777 |access-date=January 31, 2022 |website=Tennessee Titans}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Jackson recorded three solo tackles and returned two punts for 55 yards in a 37–16 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170jax.htm |access-date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> The following week, he collected five combined tackles, defended two passes, and returned five punts for a total of 51 yards in a 33–27 victory over the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Tennessee Titans - September 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709240oti.htm |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During Week 9, Jackson recorded eight combined tackles, deflected a pass, and had his first NFL carry for a 20-yard gain in a 23–20 win over the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref name="NFL">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player Stats: Adoree Jackson |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adoree'jackson/2558065/gamelogs |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref name="stats">{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Reference: Adoree Jackson stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00.htm |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], he had two tackles and two pass deflections along with 30 rushing yards as the Titans won by a score of 24–20. The following week, Jackson had 11 tackles, two pass deflections, and a forced fumble along with five rushing yards in a 40–17 road loss to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. In the regular-season finale against the Jaguars, he had five tackles, two pass deflections, and a forced fumble in a 15–10 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Adoree' Jackson Forces Fumble, Titans Recover |work=Tennessee Titans|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/video/adoree-jackson-forces-fumble-titans-recover-20171133 |access-date=January 31, 2022}}</ref>

Jackson finished his rookie season with 70 tackles, three forced fumbles, 17 pass deflections, 868 return yards, and 55 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Defense |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/defense.htm |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Titans finished second in the [[AFC South]] with a 9–7 record and made the playoffs as a Wild Card team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Regular Season Standings – National Football League |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/standings/_/season/2017 |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Titans Beat Jaguars, Punch Ticket to Playoffs |url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Beat-Jaguars-Punch-Ticket-to-Playoffs/5a96d12b-a9bc-4231-8bfa-baba96b4e1b6 |url-status=dead |access-date=January 7, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107175020/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Beat-Jaguars-Punch-Ticket-to-Playoffs/5a96d12b-a9bc-4231-8bfa-baba96b4e1b6 |archive-date=January 7, 2018}}</ref> In the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#AFC: Tennessee Titans 22, Kansas City Chiefs 21|Wild Card Round]] against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Jackson had four tackles and 61 return yards in the narrow 22–21 road victory. In the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 35, Tennessee Titans 14|Divisional Round]] against the [[New England Patriots]], he had three tackles and 83 return yards in the 35–14 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Tennessee Titans at New England Patriots – January 13th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801130nwe.htm |access-date=February 18, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2018 season====
During Week 2 against the [[Houston Texans]], Jackson recorded his first NFL interception by picking off [[Deshaun Watson]]. He finished the 20–17 victory with 6 tackles, two pass deflections, and an interception.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Froyd, Crissy |date=September 16, 2018 |title=Titans Highlights: Adoree' Jackson picks up first career interception |url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2018/09/16/titans-highlights-adoree-jackson-picks-up-first-career-interception/80936680007/ |access-date=November 3, 2018 |website=TitansWire.com}}</ref> Three weeks later, he recorded his second interception by picking off [[Josh Allen]] in the narrow 13–12 road loss. The Titans finished the 2018 season with a 9–7 record and barely missed out on the playoffs.

Jackson finished his second season with 73 tackles, 10 pass deflections, and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2019 season====
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=April 2024}}
In the season-opener against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Jackson recorded five tackles in a 43–13 win. He missed the final four games of the regular season with a foot injury, but returned and started all three playoff games before the Titans were eliminated in the AFC Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Tennessee Titans Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/oti/2019.htm |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2020 season====
On May 1, 2020, the Titans exercised the fifth-year option on Jackson's contract. He was placed on injured reserve on September 14, 2020, with a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=September 14, 2020 |title=Titans Promote CB Tye Smith to Roster, Place CB Adoree' Jackson on Injured Reserve in a Flurry of Roster Moves |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-promote-cb-tye-smith-to-roster-place-cb-adoree-jackson-on-injured-reserve |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 11, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=November 11, 2020 |title=Titans Activate CB Adoree' Jackson from Injured Reserve, But He Won't Play vs. Colts |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-activate-cb-adoree-jackson-from-injured-reserve-but-he-won-t-play-vs-colt |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

Jackson was released by the Titans on March 16, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=March 16, 2021 |title=Titans Release CB Adoree Jackson, RT Dennis Kelly |work=TennesseeTitans.com |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-cb-adoree-jackson-rt-dennis-kelly |access-date=March 16, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316195928/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-cb-adoree-jackson-rt-dennis-kelly |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 23, 2021, Jackson signed a three-year, $39 million contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raanan |first=Jordan |date=March 22, 2021 |title=Sources: Giants land CB Jackson with $39M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31115756/new-york-giants-spend-big-again-land-cb-adoree-jackson-3-year-39-million-deal-sources-say |access-date=March 23, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Eisen, Michael |date=March 23, 2021 |title=Giants sign CB Adoree' Jackson, former first-rounder |work=Giants.com |url=https://www.giants.com/news/adoree-jackson-reports-agree-to-terms-nfl-free-agency-tennessee-titans |access-date=March 23, 2021}}</ref> He finished the season with 62 tackles, eight passes defended, and one interception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 11 of the 2022 season in a loss against the [[Detroit Lions]], Jackson suffered an [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Giants rookie WR Wan'Dale Robinson suffered torn ACL vs. Lions |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/giants-rookie-wr-wan-dale-robinson-suffered-torn-acl-vs-lions |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 51 tackles, one forced fumble, two fumble recoveries, and seven passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 16 of the 2023 season against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Jackson recorded his first career Pick 6 on pass thrown by [[Jalen Hurts]] taking it 76 yards for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Citak |first=Matt |date=December 27, 2023 |title=Giants Now: Adoree' Jackson hits top speed of 20.92 mph on pick-6 |url=https://www.giants.com/news/adoree-jackson-interception-return-touchdown-philadelphia-eagles-next-gen-stats |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he appeared in 14 games. He finished with 63 tackles, one interception, eight passes defended, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Giants re-signed Jackson to a one year deal on September 1, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Citak |first=Matt |date=September 1, 2024 |title=Veteran cornerback Adoree' Jackson returns to Giants |url=https://www.giants.com/news/adoree-jackson-giants-re-sign-cornerback-usc-tennessee-titans-shane-bowen-free-agency-2024 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 28 total tackles (18 solo), five passes defended, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 13, 2025, Jackson signed a one-year, $5 million contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web | last1=Erby | first1=Glenn  | title=Eagles agree to deal with former Giants CB Adoree' Jackson | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-03-13 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/eagles-sign-former-first-round-211535543.html | access-date=2026-04-20}}</ref> He finished the 2025 season with 55 total tackles (40 solo), one interception, and 11 passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adoree' Jackson 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JackAd00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

([[Towson, Maryland]]) | college = [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] (2011–2014) | draftyear = 2015 | draftround = 5 | draftpick = 142 | pastteams = * [[Chicago Bears]] ({{NFL Year|2015}}–{{NFL Year|2018}}) * [[Green Bay Packers]] ({{NFL Year|2019}}–{{NFL Year|2022}}) * [[New York Jets]] ({{NFL Year|2023}}) * [[Houston Texans]] ({{NFL Year|2023}}) * [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] ({{NFL Year|2024}})* * [[San Francisco 49ers]] ({{NFL Year|2024}}) | status = | highlights = * [[PFWA All-Rookie Team]] ([[PFWA All-Rookie Team#2015|2015]]) | statweek = | statseason = | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 664 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 6.0 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue3 = 3 | statlabel4 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue4 = 5 | statlabel5 = [[Pass deflected|Pass deflections]] | statvalue5 = 49 | statlabel6 = [[Interceptions]] | statvalue6 = 10 | statlabel7 = [[Touchdown|Defensive touchdowns]] | statvalue7 = 1 | pfr = AmosAd00 }} '''Adrian Gerald Amos Jr.''' (born April 29, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the fifth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He has also played in the NFL for the [[Green Bay Packers]], [[New York Jets]], and [[Houston Texans]]. ==Early life== Amos attended [[Calvert Hall College High School]] in [[Towson, Maryland]]. He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a three-star recruit.{{Cite web |title=Adrian Amos, 2011 Safety, Penn State |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/adrian-amos-20136?view=pv |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=Rivals.com}} He originally committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Connecticut]].{{Cite news|title=Penn State's football program may be on the verge of landing Adrian Amos|url=http://blog.pennlive.com/patriotnewssports/2011/02/penn_states_football_program_m.html|last=Flounders|first=Bob|date=February 1, 2011|work=PennLive.com|access-date=February 5, 2018}} ==College career== Amos played at Penn State from 2011 to 2014. As a [[true freshman]], he played in all 13 games as a [[cornerback]] and on [[special teams]]. He recorded seven [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and an [[interception]]. As a sophomore in 2012, Amos started all 12 games and recorded 44 tackles and two interceptions. As a junior in 2013, Amos again started all 12 games, splitting time between cornerback and [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He finished the year with 50 tackles, one interception and 2.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]]. As a senior, he again started all 13 games, recording 42 tackles and three interceptions.{{Cite news|url=http://blog.pennlive.com/patriotnewssports/2012/04/penn_state_safety_adrian_amos.html|title=Penn State safety Adrian Amos making most of chances in short secondary|last=Pickel|first=Greg|date=April 21, 2012|work=PennLive.com|access-date=February 5, 2018}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-senior-bowl-adrian-amos-0124-20150123-story.html#page=1|title=After disciplined upbringing, former Calvert Hall defensive star Adrian Amos ready for the NFL|last=Wilson|first=Aaron|date=January 23, 2015|work=The Baltimore Sun|access-date=February 5, 2018}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-terps-penn-state-1031-20141030-story.html|title=Penn State's Adrian Amos leads trio of local contributors against Maryland|last=Zenitz|first=Matt|date=October 30, 2014|work=The Baltimore Sun|access-date=February 5, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== On November 10, 2014, the [[Senior Bowl]] announced that Amos had accepted their invitation to play in the [[2015 Senior Bowl]]. Prior to the Senior Bowl and [[NFL Combine]], Amos was projected to be a fourth or fifth round pick and was ranked as the sixth best free safety prospect by NFLDraftScout.com.{{Cite web |last=Zenitz |first=Matt |date=November 10, 2014 |title=Former Calvert Hall standout Adrian Amos accepts invitation to Senior Bowl |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/bal-former-calvert-hall-standout-adrian-amos-accepts-invitation-to-senior-bowl-20141110-story,amp.html |access-date=December 1, 2017 |website=Baltimore Sun}} On January 24, 2015, Amos attended the [[Senior Bowl]] and recorded two solo tackles to help the North defeat the South 34–13.{{Cite web |last=Poorman |first=Mike |date=January 25, 2015 |title=Smith & Amos Wow Woo from Penn State at Senior Bowl |url=http://www.statecollege.com/news/columns/smith-amos-wow-woo-from-penn-state-at-senior-bowl,1462562/ |access-date=December 1, 2017 |website=StateCollege.com |archive-date=December 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202052750/http://www.statecollege.com/news/columns/smith-amos-wow-woo-from-penn-state-at-senior-bowl,1462562/ |url-status=dead }} Amos attended the NFL combine and performed well, completing almost all of the combine drills, but chose to skip the [[bench press]]. His [[40-yard dash]] time of 4.39s ranked seventh among all safeties and his 4.03s time in the [[three-cone drill]] ranked second amongst his position.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=March 19, 2015 |title=Former Calvert Hall standout Adrian Amos runs 4.39 40-yard dash at Penn State pro day |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/bal-former-calvert-hall-standout-adrian-amos-runs-439-at-penn-state-pro-day-workout-20150319-story,amp.html |access-date=December 1, 2017 |website=Baltimore Sun}} He also finished in the top twenty among safeties at the combine in the 20-yard [[short shuttle]] and the 60-yard shuttle. On March 19, 2015, Amos opted to participate at Penn State's [[pro day]], along with [[Mike Hull (linebacker)|Mike Hull]], [[Donovan Smith]], [[Jesse James (tight end)|Jesse James]], [[Sam Ficken]], Miles Dieffenbach, [[Deion Barnes]], and three other teammates. He decided to perform the bench press, 40-yard dash, and positional drills for the team representatives and scouts from 19 NFL teams in attendance. He had an impressive performance overall and decreased his time in the 40-yard dash from 4.56s at the combine to 4.37s and 4.40s.{{Cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil |author-link=Gil Brandt |date=March 20, 2015 |title=Penn State safety boosts draft stock at pro day |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/penn-state-safety-boosts-draft-stock-at-pro-day-0ap3000000480380 |access-date=December 1, 2017 |website=NFL.com}} Amos attended private visits or workouts for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Amos was projected to be a second to fourth round pick by the majority of [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts. He was ranked the second best free safety prospect in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com and was ranked the 13th best safety by NFL analyst [[Charles Davis (defensive back)|Charles Davis]].{{cite web| On October 20, 2016, Amos recorded a season-high eight combined tackles in the Bears' 26–10 loss at the Packers. After starting 27 consecutive games to start his career, Amos missed a Week 13 matchup against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] with a foot injury.{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bears-adrian-amos-questionable-to-play/ |title=Bears' Adrian Amos: Questionable to play |date=December 2, 2016 |website=CBSSports |access-date=December 1, 2017}} Amos finished the season with 65 combined tackles (57 solo) and five pass deflections in 15 games and 14 starts.{{cite web| title=NFL Player Stats: Adrian Amos-2016| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adrianamos/2552385/gamelogs?season=2016| accessdate=December 1, 2017| publisher=National Football League}} [[Pro Football Focus]] gave him a grade of 80.6 for the 2016 season. On April 26, 2016, Amos, along with [[tight end]] [[Zach Miller (tight end, born 1984)|Zach Miller]], were awarded the [[Brian Piccolo Award]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/ct-zach-miller-adrian-amos-piccolo-awards-20160426-story.html|title=Bears honor Zach Miller, Adrian Amos with Brian Piccolo awards|last=Wiederer|first=Dan|date=April 26, 2016|website=Chicago Tribune|access-date=July 26, 2016}} Although the Chicago Bears finished 3–13, the defense finished seventh in passing defense and 15th in total defense. Amos failed to record an interception in his first two seasons and the Bears ranked 31st with only eight interceptions in 2016. ====2017==== During the Bears' training camp, Amos competed with [[Chris Prosinski]] and rookie [[Eddie Jackson (safety)|Eddie Jackson]] for his job as starting free safety. He was named the backup to Jackson to start the 2017 season.{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=September 10, 2017 |title=Eddie Jackson goes from fourth round to starting safety |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2017/09/eddie_jackson_goes_from_fourth.html |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=AL.com |language=en}} Amos played sparingly through the first three games and only logged 16 snaps on defense with no tackles.{{cite web | last=Wiltfong Jr.| first=Lester A. | title=Snap counts, stats and more: Chicago Bears vs Pittsburgh Steelers | website=Windy City Gridiron |publisher=SB Nation| date=2017-09-25 | url=https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2017/9/25/16358546/snap-counts-stats-and-more-chicago-bears-vs-pittsburgh-steelers-playing-time | access-date=2026-04-05}} Amos became the starting strong safety, opposite Eddie Jackson, for Week 4 after [[Quintin Demps]] suffered a fractured forearm the previous game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and was placed on injured reserve.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/ct-spt-bears-quintin-demps-returns-20171130-story,amp.html|title=Bears designate safety Quintin Demps to return from injured reserve|last=Biggs|first=Brad|date=November 30, 2017|website=Chicago Tribune|accessdate=December 1, 2017}} On September 28, 2017, Amos made his first start of the season and recorded eight combined tackles during a 45–13 loss at the Packers. '''Adolphus Fitzgerald Washington Jr.''' (born November 24, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the third round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Washington attended [[Roger Bacon High School]] in [[St. Bernard, Ohio]], as a freshman, before transferring to [[Robert A. Taft Information Technology High School]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]], for his final three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2014/09/25/buckeyes-adolphus-washington-starts-against-uc-bearcats/16215805/|title=OSU's Adolphus Washington of Taft prepares for Bearcats|date=September 25, 2014|work=Cincinnati.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/story/_/id/6905931/dwayne-stanford-ii-adolphus-washington-represent-taft-well|title=Dwayne Stanford II and Adolphus Washington represent Taft well|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> He had 90 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] and 23.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] as a senior and 107 tackles and 19 sacks as a junior. Washington was a five-star recruit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uga/football/recruiting/player-Adolphus-Washington-92432|title=Adolphus Washington|publisher=}}</ref> He committed to [[Ohio State University]] to play [[college football]]. Washington also played basketball in high school. As a senior, he averaged 23.1 [[points per game|points]] and 14.3 [[rebounds per game]] and was named the [[Gatorade]] Basketball Player of the Year for Ohio.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/high-school/player-of-the-year/post/_/id/7105/ohio-boys-hoop-poy-adolphus-washington|title=Ohio Boys Hoop POY: Adolphus Washington|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Washington was named a ''[[Parade Magazine]]'' All-American in both football and [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|basketball]].<ref>{{cite news|last=McLaughlin|first=Brian|title=Meet the 2012 PARADE All-America Football Team!|date=January 15, 2012|work=Parade|url=https://parade.com/89989/brianmclaughlin/football-team/|access-date=February 18, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=McLaughlin|first=Brian|title=Meet the 2012 PARADE All-America Basketball Team!|date=May 27, 2012|work=Parade|url=http://communitytable.com/89931/brianmclaughlin/basketball-team/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417110720/http://communitytable.com/89931/brianmclaughlin/basketball-team/|archive-date=April 17, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman in 2012, Washington played in 10 games. He recorded nine tackles and three sacks. As a sophomore in 2013, he played in 12 games with five starts and recorded 36 tackles and two sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/98187/washington-finds-a-home-on-osu-line|title=Adolphus Washington finds home on Ohio State Buckeyes defensive line – Big Ten Blog- ESPN|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> As a junior in 2014, he started all 14 games, recording 48 tackles and 4.5 sacks. During the [[2015 College Football Playoff National Championship]] against Oregon, he had three tackles and a sack. On December 9, 2015, Washington was cited for solicitation.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Goodbread|first1=Chase|title=Adolphus Washington cited for solicitation|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ohio-state-dt-adolphus-washington-cited-for-solicitation-0ap3000000598276|publisher=NFL|access-date=December 10, 2015}}</ref> As a result, he was suspended for the Fiesta Bowl.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Goodbread|first1=Chase|title=Adolphus Washington suspended for Fiesta Bowl|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000598988/article/adolphus-washington-suspended-for-fiesta-bowl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151214040234/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000598988/article/adolphus-washington-suspended-for-fiesta-bowl|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 14, 2015|publisher=NFL|access-date=December 11, 2015}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
Washington was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the third round, 80th overall, in the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2016 NFL Draft results: Adolphus Washington to Buffalo Bills at No. 80 overall|url=https://www.buffalorumblings.com/buffalo-bills-news/2016/4/29/11542478/2016-nfl-draft-results-adolphus-washington-buffalo-bills-round-3|author=Galliford, Brian|website=BuffaloRumblings.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=July 23, 2017}}</ref> He played in 15 games with 11 starts his rookie season, recording 21 tackles and 2.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adolphus Washington 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WashAd00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The following year in 2017, he started 10 games out of 15 played, recording 33 tackles and one sack.

After just one game in 2018, the Bills released him on September 10, 2018. Washington finished his time on the Bills with 3.5 sacks and 56 tackles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills sign DE Nate Orchard|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-de-nate-orchard|author=Brown, Chris|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=September 10, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On September 18, 2018, Washington was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys sign Adolphus Washington to practice squad, release Aziz Shittu|url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2018/9/18/17876482/roster-update-cowboys-sign-adolphus-washington-to-practice-squad-release-aziz-shittu|website=BloggingTheBoys.com|date=September 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On September 26, 2018, Washington was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] off the Cowboys' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals sign former Ohio State star Adolphus Washington from Cowboys' practice squad; Ryan Glasgow to IR|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2018/9/25/17901292/bengals-sign-former-ohio-state-star-adolphus-washington-from-cowboys-practice-squad|website=CincyJungle.com|date=September 26, 2018}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 23, 2018, after suffering a knee injury in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adolphus Washington becomes the third Bengals player to go on IR this week|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2018/11/23/18108795/adolphus-washington-becomes-third-bengals-player-to-go-on-ir-this-week|website=CincyJungle.com|date=November 23, 2018}}</ref> On April 23, 2019, the Bengals waived Washington.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-waive-adolphus-washington|title=Bengals Waive Adolphus Washington|website=Bengals.com|date=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On May 23, 2019, Washington was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Adolphus Washington signs with Dolphins|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/05/23/adolphus-washington-signs-with-dolphins/|author=Smith, Michael David|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=May 23, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Claim Five Players Off Waivers|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-claim-five-players-off-waivers-2019|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 1, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On July 9, 2017, Washington was arrested for a misdemeanor weapons charge in Sharonville, Ohio.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adolphus Washington arrested on weapons charge|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bills-dt-adolphus-washington-arrested-on-weapons-charge-0ap3000000819117|website=NFL.com|date=July 11, 2017}}</ref> On August 28, 2017, he was acquitted of weapons charges.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adolphus Washington acquitted of weapons charge|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adolphus-washington-acquitted-of-weapons-charge-0ap3000000836294|publisher=NFL|access-date=August 28, 2017}}</ref>

He transferred to the [[University of Miami]] for his senior year in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adrian Colbert Bio – University of Miami Hurricanes Official Athletic Site |url=http://www.hurricanesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211063749 |access-date=April 30, 2017 |website=Hurricanesports.com |archive-date=May 12, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512235650/http://www.hurricanesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211063749 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
