===San Francisco 49ers===
The [[San Francisco 49ers]] selected Colbert in the seventh round (229th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Colbert was the 31st [[cornerback]] drafted in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fann, Joe |date=April 29, 2017 |title=San Francisco 49ers Draft Miami S Adrian Colbert |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/San-Francisco-49ers-Draft-Miami-S-Adrian-Colbert/2ed7a0a5-2ba8-462f-a7b0-a078580108d7 |access-date=May 20, 2017 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

On May 4, 2017, the 49ers signed Colbert to a four-year, $2.48 million contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $84,786.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Adrian Colbert's contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/san-francisco-49ers/adrian-colbert-21971/ |access-date=September 9, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> He played in 14 games with six starts at free safety as a rookie, recording 37 tackles and five passes defensed.

Colbert entered the 2018 season as the starting free safety for the 49ers. He played in seven games with six starts before suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 7. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 22, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2018 |title=49ers place Adrian Colbert on IR, re-sign Tom Savage |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/22/49ers-place-adrian-colbert-on-ir-re-sign-tom-savage/ |website=Niners Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

Colbert was [[waived/injured]] during final roster cuts on August 31, 2019,<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 31, 2019 |title=49ers Announce 53-man Roster |work=49ers.com |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-53-man-roster |access-date=September 6, 2019}}</ref> and reverted to the team's injured reserve list the next day. He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 6.

===Seattle Seahawks===
On September 18, 2019, Colbert was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=September 18, 2019 |title=Seahawks Sign Free Safety Adrian Colbert & Tackle Elijah Nkansah To Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-free-safety-adrian-colbert-tackle-elijah-nkansah-to-practice-squad |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 26, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=September 26, 2019 |title=Seahawks Promote Safety Adrian Colbert From Practice Squad; Waive Defensive Tackle Bryan Mone |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-promote-safety-adrian-colbert-from-practice-squad-waive-defensive-tackl |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was waived on October 12, 2019, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=October 11, 2019 |title=Seahawks Promote Guard Jordan Roos & Tight End Jacob Hollister From Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-promote-guard-jordan-roos-tight-end-jacob-hollister-from-practice-squad |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 19, 2019, Colbert was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] off the Seahawks practice squad.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Crabbs, Kyle |date=November 20, 2019 |title=Miami Dolphins sign free safety Adrian Colbert |work=USAToday.com |url=https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2019/11/20/miami-dolphins-sign-free-safety-adrian-colbert/ |access-date=August 23, 2020}}</ref>

Colbert re-signed with the Dolphins on March 20, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt, Darin |date=March 19, 2020 |title=Dolphins bring back safety Adrian Colbert |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/19/dolphins-bring-back-safety-adrian-colbert/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> He was waived on August 16, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 16, 2020 |title=Dolphins Waive Two, Activate Brandin Bryant |work=MiamiDolphins.com |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-waive-two-activate-brandin-bryant |access-date=August 17, 2020 |archive-date=August 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200824052037/https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-waive-two-activate-brandin-bryant |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Colbert was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on August 22, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 21, 2020 |title=Chiefs sign Adrian Colbert |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/21/chiefs-sign-adrian-colbert/ |access-date=August 21, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Chiefs Roster Down to NFL-Mandated 53 |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-roster-down-to-nfl-mandated-53-x6671 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On September 6, 2020, Colbert was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen, Michael |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Giants claim 3 players as roster-building continues |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-roster-adrian-colbert-jackson-barton-damion-ratley |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 3, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Eisen, Michael |date=November 3, 2020 |title=Coach Joe Judge takes no solace in almost winning |work=Giants.com |url=https://www.giants.com/news/goals-clear-for-coach-judge-close-isn-t-good-enough |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> On December 19, 2020, Colbert was activated off of injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen, Michael |date=December 19, 2020 |title=Roster moves: Giants add two quarterbacks, three DBs to active roster |url=https://www.giants.com/news/roster-moves-giants-add-two-quarterbacks-three-db-s-to-active-roster |website=Giants.com |access-date=December 20, 2020 |archive-date=December 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201219210334/https://www.giants.com/news/roster-moves-giants-add-two-quarterbacks-three-db-s-to-active-roster |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On May 21, 2021, Colbert signed with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 21, 2021 |title=Patriots Sign S Adrian Colbert and RB Tyler Gaffney |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-s-adrian-colbert-and-rb-tyler-gaffney |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> On August 30, 2021, Colbert was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 31, 2021|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-53-man-roster-limit-acquire-ol-yasir-durant-|title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach 53-Man Roster Limit; Acquire OL Yasir Durant in a Trade with Kansas City}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On September 6, 2021, Colbert was signed by the [[New York Jets]] to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 6, 2021|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-sheldrick-redwine-rb-josh-adams|title=Jets Sign S Sheldrick Redwine, RB Josh Adams|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=November 30, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130131023/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-sheldrick-redwine-rb-josh-adams|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 20.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign S Adrian Colbert to Active Roster; Release OL Isaiah Williams|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-adrian-colbert-to-active-roster-release-ol-isaiah-williams|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 20, 2021}}</ref> On October 26, 2021, Colbert was released by the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign S Jarrod Wilson, Release S Adrian Colbert|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-jarrod-wilson-release-s-adrian-colbert|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 26, 2021}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On December 19, 2021, Colbert was signed to the [[Cleveland Browns]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns activate G Wyatt Teller, place DE Jadeveon Clowney on reserve/COVID-19 and make other roster moves|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-activate-g-wyatt-teller-place-de-jadeveon-clowney-on-reserve-covid-19-and|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=December 19, 2021}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster as a COVID-19 replacement player on December 24, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns activate 5 players from reserve/COVID-19 list, make other roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-activate-5-players-from-reserve-covid-19-list-make-other-roster-moves |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 24, 2021}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On August 9, 2022, Colbert signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Titans sign Adrian Colbert |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/08/09/titans-sign-adrian-colbert/amp/ |publisher=NBCSports.com |date=August 9, 2022 |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |access-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809192549/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/08/09/titans-sign-adrian-colbert/amp/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was released on August 29, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Trim Roster to 53 Players with 29 Roster Moves|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-trim-roster-to-53-players-with-29-roster-moves|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On November 29, 2022, Colbert was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears place Mooney, Jackson on IR, sign Thomas to active roster|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-place-mooney-jackson-on-ir-sign-thomas-to-active-roster|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=November 29, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 7 to 2023 reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-7-to-2023-reserve-future-contracts|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=January 9, 2023}}</ref> On August 21, 2023, Colbert was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 21, 2023 |title=Bears put S Adrian Colbert on injured reserve |work=[[NBC Sports]] |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bears-put-s-adrian-colbert-on-injured-reserve}}</ref> He was released with an injury settlement on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/adrian-colbert-reaches-injury-settlement/|title=
Adrian Colbert: Reaches injury settlement|website=CBS Sports|date=30 August 2023|accessdate=30 August 2023}}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on November 21, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wiltfong Jr. |first1=Lester A |title=Bears Make Practice Squad Moves |url=https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2023/11/21/23971697/chicago-bears-release-trace-mcsorley-practice-squad-adrian-colbert-roster-moves-michael-dwumfour |website=Windy City Gridiron |access-date=22 November 2023}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 10 to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-10-to-reserve-future-contracts-2024|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=January 8, 2024}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Colbert was released by the Bears.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears reach 53-man roster limit|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-reach-53-man-roster-limit-2024|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He was signed to the practice squad on November 20.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barbieri |first=Alyssa |date=November 20, 2024 |title=Bear Necessities: Chicago re-signs Adrian Colbert to boost secondary |url=https://bearswire-eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bears/2024/11/20/bear-necessities-chicago-re-signs-adrian-colbert-to-boost-secondary/76433624007/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |website=Bears Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 24 and became a free agent when the season was over.

Colbert is a cousin of NFL wide receiver [[Marquise Goodwin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gilbert |first=John |date=2019-11-19 |title=Dolphins swipe Seahawks practice squad player |url=https://www.fieldgulls.com/2019/11/19/20972659/miami-dolphins-swipe-seattle-seahawks-practice-squad-player-adrian-colbert-fs-gary-jennings-diggs |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Field Gulls |publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ade Aruna''' (born April 27, 1994) is a Nigerian former professional [[American football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]], and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]]. He has also been a member of the [[Oakland Raiders|Oakland]] / [[Las Vegas Raiders]] and [[BC Lions]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Nigeria]], Aruna moved to the [[United States]] during his high school years, initially to pursue a career in basketball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Okupa |first=Francis |date=April 23, 2018 |title=Nigeria dominates Africa's 2018 NFL draftee list |url=http://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/23292146/nigeria-dominates-africa-2018-nfl-draftee-list |access-date=May 7, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Minnesota Vikings===
Aruna was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round (218th overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gates |first=Christopher |date=April 28, 2018 |title=2018 NFL Draft: Minnesota Vikings select Ade Aruna |url=https://www.dailynorseman.com/2018/4/28/17295682/2018-nfl-draft-minnesota-vikings-ade-aruna-analysis-grades |accessdate=June 26, 2018 |website=Daily Norseman|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> On August 20, 2018, he was placed on [[injured reserve]] after suffering a knee injury in the preseason.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Release Forbath, Place Aruna on IR, Announce Other Moves|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-release-forbath-place-aruna-on-ir-announce-other-moves|author=Smith, Eric|website=Vikings.com|date=August 20, 2018}}</ref>

Aruna was waived/injured during final roster cuts on August 31, 2019,<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-2019-roster-cuts-53-man-roster|website=Vikings.com|date=August 31, 2019|accessdate=September 12, 2019}}</ref> and reverted to the team's injured reserve list the next day. He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 12.

===Oakland / Las Vegas Raiders===
On December 26, 2019, Aruna was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign DE Ade Aruna to practice squad|url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2019/12/26/21038449/oakland-raiders-sign-de-ade-aruna-to-practice-squad|work=Silver and Black Pride|publisher=SB Nation|date=December 26, 2019}}</ref> On December 30, 2019, Aruna was signed to a reserve/future contract. On July 27, 2020, he was waived with a [[non-football injury]] designation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders claim guard Jordan Roos|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-claim-guard-jordan-roos|website=Raiders.com|date=July 27, 2020}}</ref> He was re-signed on August 8, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Raiders re-sign defensive end Ade Aruna |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-re-sign-defensive-end-ade-aruna |website=Raiders.com |date=August 8, 2020 |accessdate=August 11, 2020}}</ref> Aruna was waived once again on August 25, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raiders sign defensive end Sharif Finch|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-defensive-end-sharif-finch|access-date=2020-08-25|website=Las Vegas Raiders|language=en-US}}</ref>

===BC Lions===
Aruna signed with the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on April 19, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Baker, Matt |title=Lions add three, including former Vikings draft pick Aruna |url=https://www.bclions.com/2021/04/19/lions-add-three-including-former-vikings-draft-pick-aruna/ |website=BCLions.com |date=April 19, 2021 |access-date=April 19, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on the suspended list on July 2, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 CFL Transactions |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/?season=2021 |website=CFL.ca |access-date=July 7, 2021}}</ref> He was released on February 14, 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/ade-aruna-arunaad01/transactions | title=Ade Aruna | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=January 23, 2024}}</ref>

'''Adonis K. Alexander''' (born November 7, 1996) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[St. Louis Battlehawks]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech Hokies]] and was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the sixth round of the 2018 [[NFL supplemental draft]].

==Early life and college==
Alexander attended [[Independence High School (Charlotte, North Carolina)|Independence High School]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]]. He then attended [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]], and was ruled academically ineligible for his final year, preventing him from entering the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paylor |first=Terez |date=July 10, 2018 |title=The Story of Adonis: This NFL supplemental draft candidate offers loads of intrigue |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/story-adonis-nfl-supplemental-draft-candidate-offers-loads-intrigue-031416081.html |access-date=July 13, 2018 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> However, he entered in to the 2018 [[NFL supplemental draft]].

==Professional career==
===Washington Redskins===
Alexander was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the sixth round of the 2018 supplemental draft.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Select Adonis Alexander In Sixth Round Of Supplemental Draft, Waive Sam Irwin-Hill|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-select-adonis-alexander-in-sixth-round-of-supplemental-draft-waive-sam-|website=Redskins.com|date=July 11, 2018}}</ref>

Alexander was waived by Washington on August 31, 2019, but was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-make-roster-moves-53-man-roster|title=Redskins Make Roster Moves|date=August 31, 2019|access-date=September 2, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|title=Redskins Sign Nine Players To Practice Squad|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-nine-players-to-practice-squad|date=September 1, 2019|access-date=September 2, 2019}}</ref> He was released on October 1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Waive WR Robert Davis, Release CB Adonis Alexander From Practice Squad|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-waive-wr-robert-davis-release-cb-adonis-alexander-from-practice-squad|website=Redskins.com|date=October 1, 2019}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On November 14, 2019, Alexander was signed to the [[Los Angeles Rams]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams sign second-year DB Adonis Alexander to practice squad|url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2019/11/14/nfl-rams-adonis-alexander-practice-squad/|work=The Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Rams on December 31.

Alexander was waived on September 4, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams waive 17 players ahead of 53-man roster deadline|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-waive-17-players-ahead-of-53-man-roster-deadline|website=TheRams.com|date=September 4, 2020}}</ref>

On January 4, 2021, Alexander signed a reserve/future contract with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-13-players-reserve-future-contracts|website=49ers.com|date=January 4, 2021|access-date=January 9, 2021|archive-date=October 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009001105/https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-13-players-reserve-future-contracts|url-status=dead}}</ref> Alexander was waived San Francisco on May 4.<ref>{{cite news |title=49ers Waive Three Players |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-waive-adonis-alexander-matt-cole-chris-edwards |website=49ers.com |date=May 4, 2021 |access-date=May 5, 2021 |archive-date=May 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519160318/https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-waive-adonis-alexander-matt-cole-chris-edwards |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Adam Trautman''' (born February 5, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Dayton Flyers football|Dayton Flyers]] and was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the third round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. Prior to the 2023 season, he was traded to the Broncos, reuniting with former Saints head coach [[Sean Payton]].

==Early life==
Trautman grew up in [[Williamsburg, Michigan]] and attended [[Elk Rapids High School]], where he played basketball and [[high school football|football]] and was an All-County selection in both sports.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Meet the Prospect: Dayton's Adam Trautman transitions from small-town QB to NFL TE prospect |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1203208/2019/09/12/meet-the-prospect-daytons-adam-trautman-transitions-from-small-town-qb-to-nfl-te-prospect/ |access-date=January 28, 2020 |website=The Athletic}}</ref> Trautman set every major school passing record and was named the [[Lake Michigan Conference (Michigan)|Lake Michigan Conference]] Player of the Year as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartsock |first=Mike |date=September 22, 2017 |title=Ex-QB Trautman thriving at tight end for Dayton Flyers |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/trautman-thriving-tight-end-for-dayton-flyers/WiFx04azWQfGTgbS58posN/ |access-date=January 28, 2020 |website=[[Dayton Daily News]]}}</ref>

==College career==

web |last=Schofield |first=Mark |date=January 21, 2020 |title=Schofield's Senior Bowl Day 1 notes: Dayton TE Adam Trautman's competitiveness, athleticism stand out |url=https://madison.com/sports/football/schofield-s-senior-bowl-day-notes-dayton-te-adam-trautman/article_07a1c207-4fc0-5a1e-b285-0290494c85a7.html |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |archive-date=January 29, 2020 |url-status=dead }}</ref> As a redshirt freshman, he caught 24 passes for 238 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dobrowolski |first=Chris |date=November 2, 2017 |title=Trautman thriving at Dayton as team's top receiver |url=http://www.antrimreview.net/content/trautman-thriving-dayton-team%E2%80%99s-top-receiver |access-date=January 28, 2020 |website=The Review}}</ref> He had 43 receptions for 537 yards and five touchdowns and was named second-team All-[[Pioneer Football League]] in his sophomore season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edholm |first=Eric |date=January 22, 2020 |title=Small-school tight end who never caught a pass before 2016 is now an NFL draft prospect Sports}}</ref> As a junior, Trautman led the team with 41 receptions, 604 yards and nine touchdowns and was again named second-team All-PFL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Rhiannon |date=January Senior, he was named the PFL Offensive Player of the Year and first-team All-PFL after catching 70 passes for 916 yards and 14 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartman |first=Marcus |date=January 21, 2020 |title=Dayton's Trautman ready to measure himself against best at Senior Bowl ===New Orleans Saints===
[[File:Adam Trautman (51583671965) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Trautman with the [[New Orleans Saints]] in 2021]]
Trautman was drafted by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the third round with the 105th overall pick of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was the first Dayton football player to be drafted since Bill Westbeld in [[1977 NFL draft|1977]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |date=April 24, 2020 |title=Adam Trautman first Dayton Flyers player drafted in 43 years |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/adam-trautman-first-dayton-flyers-player-drafted-years/HWCY0ZseJCBUsTc30pH1KN/ |access-date=April 25, 2020 |website=[[Dayton Daily News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dayton Drafted Players/Alumni |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/dayton/drafted.htm |access-date=May 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Trautman made his NFL debut on September 13, 2020, in the season opener against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], becoming the first Dayton player to appear in an NFL game in 45 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archdeacon |first=Tom |date=September 20, 2020 |title='Pancake' block highlights debut for Trautman |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-pancake-block-highlights-debut-for-trautman/OPLPX7GA55GGDN3I5AEFDS462U/ |access-date=September 21, 2020 |website=[[Dayton Daily News]]}}</ref> He caught a 17-yard pass from [[Drew Brees]] for his first career reception on September 21, 2020, on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' in a 34–24 loss to the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |date=September 21, 2020 |title=Dayton's Trautman makes first NFL catch |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/daytons-trautman-makes-first-nfl-catch/VSH5HWDQIFAVHKPNZ5QB6IDS3M/ |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=[[Dayton Daily News]]}}</ref> In Week 9, against the Buccaneers, he had three receptions for 39 yards and his first professional touchdown reception in the 38–3 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – November 8th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011080tam.htm |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a humorous incident, the Buccaneers were unable to find a picture of Trautman to use on their scoring display, and instead used a picture of then-Rams quarterback [[Jared Goff]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-12|title=Bucs Used Jared Goff's Picture For Saints' Rookie Adam Trautman After He Scored 1st Career TD (VIDEO)|url=http://www.totalprosports.com/2020/11/12/bucs-used-jared-goffs-picture-for-saints-rookie-adam-trautman-after-he-scored-1st-career-td-video/|access-date=2021-06-23|website=Total Pro Sports|language=en|archive-date=June 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628220204/https://www.totalprosports.com/2020/11/12/bucs-used-jared-goffs-picture-for-saints-rookie-adam-trautman-after-he-scored-1st-career-td-video/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with 15 receptions on 16 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown and was rated the best rookie tight end by [[Pro Football Focus]], who also rated him the best run-blocking tight end in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-all-rookie-team-chargers-justin-herbert-qb-vikings-justin-jefferson-washington-chase-young|title=PFF's 2020 NFL All-Rookie Team: Chargers' Justin Herbert starts at QB, Vikings' Justin Jefferson earns WR1 spot|first=Ben|last=Linsey|website=[[Pro Football Focus]]|date=January 4, 2021|access-date=November 27, 2021}}</ref> 
Trautman entered the 2021 season as the starting tight end for the Saints after the team released [[Jared Cook]] in the offseason.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_d3944510-d539-11eb-b2ef-c38e3f9c8f03.html|title=How Adam Trautman prepared himself for the lead role in the Saints tight end room|first=Luke|last=Johnson|website=[[NOLA.com]]|date=June 1, 2021|access-date=November 27, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 23, 2021.<ref name="u231">{{cite web | last=Sigler | first=John | title=Saints re-sign Kevin White and Ken Crawley, send two others to injured reserve | website=Saints Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2021-11-23 | url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/lists/saints-sign-kevin-white-ken-crawley-nfl-roster-moves/ | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> He was activated on December 18.<ref name="b058">{{cite web | last=Rose | first=Bob | title=Saints Activate TE Adam Trautman, Place TE Garrett Griffin on IR | website=SI.com | date=2021-12-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/saints-activate-adam-trautman-garrett-griffin-ir | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> In the 2021 season, he finished with 27 receptions for 263 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Trautman 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TrauAd00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he finished with 18 receptions for 207 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Trautman 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TrauAd00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On April 29, 2023, Trautman was traded from the Saints, along with the 257th pick of the [[2023 NFL draft]], to the [[Denver Broncos]] in exchange for the 195th pick of the draft.<ref name="a471">{{cite web | last=DiLalla | first=Aric | title=Broncos acquire TE Adam Trautman, seventh-round pick from Saints for sixth-round selection | website=Denver Broncos | date=2023-04-29 | url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-acquire-te-adam-trautman-seventh-round-pick-from-saints-for-sixth-round- | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> He was the Broncos starting tight end throughout the season, playing all 17 games with 12 starts while recording 22 catches for 204 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Trautman 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TrauAd00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-06 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2024, Trautman signed a two-year contract extension with the Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=March 13, 2024 |title=Broncos re-sign TE Adam Trautman to 2-year contract |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-re-sign-te-adam-trautman-to-2-year-contract |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

On March 8, 2026, the Broncos signed Trautman to a three-year, $17 million extension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomasson |first=Chris |date=2026-03-08 |title=Broncos to re-sign LB Justin Strnad, TE Adam Trautman to 3-year deals |url=https://www.denvergazette.com/2026/03/08/broncos-to-re-sign-lb-justin-strnad-te-adam-trautman-to-3-year-deals/ |access-date=2026-03-08 |website=Denver Gazette |language=}}</ref>

'''Adrian Killins Jr.''' (born January 2, 1998) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCF Knights football|UCF Knights]]. He played for the NFL's [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[Arlington Renegades]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]].

==Early life==
Killins was born and grew up in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]] and attended [[Mainland High School]], where he played [[high school football|football]] and ran track. Killins was a two-time state champion in the 200 meters and was the runner-up in the 100 meters as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crepea |first=James |date=December 29, 2017 |title=How fast is UCF running back Adrian Killins Jr.? |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2017/12/how_fast_is_ucf_running_back_a.html |access-date=October 5, 2020 |website=[[AL.com]] |publisher=[[The Oregonian]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Killins was a member of the [[UCF Knights football|UCF Knights]] for four seasons. He was named second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) after his junior season when he rushed 147 times for 715 yards and eight touchdowns and had 19 receptions for 377 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murschel |first=Matt |date=April 3, 2019 |title=UCF running back Adrian Killins pushes to build on his success during his senior season |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-spring-football-0404-story.html |access-date=October 4, 2020 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref> As a senior, Killins rushed for 629 yards and seven touchdowns and caught eight passes for 120 yards and one touchdown and was again named second-team All-AAC.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beede |first=Jason |date=February 21, 2020 |title=NFL Network analyst surprised by no combine invite for Killins |url=https://247sports.com/college/central-florida/Article/Daniel-Jeremiah-NFL-Network-analyst-UCF-football-Adrian-Killins-surprised-about-no-invite-144110007/ |access-date=October 4, 2020 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref> Killins finished his collegiate career with 2,459 rushing yards and 25 rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Chris |date=April 25, 2020 |title=UCF star Adrian Killins enters NFL draft with chip on his shoulder |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-adrian-killins-nfl-draft-20200425-3qxzdam3nbh63afu4nxdblxsgy-story.html |access-date=October 4, 2020 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref>

'''Adonai Enlil''' "'''AD'''" '''Mitchell''' (born October 8, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played college football for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] and [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] before being selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the second round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Mitchell was born on October 8, 2002, in [[Missouri City, Texas]]. He attended Cane Ridge High School in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], a neighborhood of [[Nashville]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vitale |first=Joe |date=April 26, 2021 |title=Did Georgia find its next star WR in freshman Adonai Mitchell? |url=https://ugawire.usatoday.com/2021/04/26/did-georgia-find-its-next-star-wr-in-freshman-adonai-mitchell/ |access-date=29 September 2021 |website=UGA Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> During his high school career, he had 53 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 795 yards, 8 receiving [[touchdowns]], 373 [[rushing yards]], and 9 rushing touchdowns on 68 attempts.<ref name="Adonai Mitchell's Football Stats">{{cite web |title=Adonai Mitchell's Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/adonai-mitchell/zIiRXGM4Eea-8KA2nzwbTA/football/stats.htm |website=Max Preps |publisher=Max Preps |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref>

Mitchell was named the 2019 Tennessean Region 5-6A Athlete of the Year<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=December 11, 2019 |title=Tennessee high school football: Nashville area all-region teams |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/11/tennessee-high-school-football-2019-nashville-area-all-region-teams/4390890002/ |access-date=29 September 2021 |website=Tennessean |publisher=The Tennessean}}</ref> following a season which saw him record 28 receptions for 417 yards and 5 touchdowns in addition to 203 rushing yards and 4 touchdowns on 45 carries,<ref name="Adonai Mitchell's Football Stats"/> leading his team to a 9–4 overall record and a 6-0 league record. Before the start of the 2020 high school season, he was named to the MaxPreps Preseason Tennessee All-State Second Team Offense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poff |first=Zack |date=August 18, 2020 |title=Preseason Tennessee All-State high school football team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/JSjtrvxxQ0-NamWeZ4Z00g/preseason-tennessee-all-state-high-school-football-team.htm |access-date=29 September 2021 |website=Max Preps |publisher=Max Preps}}</ref>

Prior to his time at Cane Ridge High School, Mitchell attended [[Ridge Point High School]] in [[Missouri City, Texas]], where he had 25 receptions totaling 378 yards and 3 touchdowns in addition to 170 rushing yards and 5 touchdowns on 23 carries.<ref name="Adonai Mitchell's Football Stats"/> Following the season, he was named to the UIL Class 6A District 20 All-District Second Team Offense.<ref name="Adonai Mitchell">{{cite web |title=Adonai Mitchell |url=https://georgiadogs.com/sports/football/roster/adonai-mitchell/5506 |website=Georgia Bulldogs Football |publisher=University of Georgia |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref>

== College career ==
=== Georgia ===
Mitchell, a three-star recruit,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adonai Mitchell, Georgia Bulldogs, Wide Receiver|url=https://247sports.com/player/adonai-mitchell-46085140/|url-status=live|access-date=|website=247Sports|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201210091219/https://247sports.com/Player/Adonai-Mitchell-46085140/ |archive-date=2020-12-10 }}</ref> enrolled at the [[University of Georgia]] in January 2021<ref name="Adonai Mitchell"/> after flipping his commitment from [[Ole Miss football|Ole Miss]] from July 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/12/georgia-football-recruiting-adonai-mitchell-commitment-ole-miss-decommit/5424432002/|website=[[The Tennessean]]|date=July 12, 2020|title=Adonai Mitchell commits to Georgia after originally picking Ole Miss|author=Kreager, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{Cite came following his recruitment by top-ranked football programs such as [[Auburn football|Auburn]], [[Missouri football|Missouri]], [[West virginia football|West Virginia]], and [[Boston College football|Boston College]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adonai Mitchell |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/240451/adonai-mitchell |website=ESPN |publisher=ESPN |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref> In the Georgia Bulldogs' spring game in April 2021, he caught 7 of his 13 targets for 105 yards and 1 touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thombs |first=Palmer |date=April 17, 2021 |title=Adonai Mitchell caps off strong spring with impressive G-Day |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia/Article/Georgia-Football-Adonai-Mitchell-caps-off-strong-spring-with-impressive-G-Day-164320894/ |access-date=30 September 2021 |website=Dawgs 247 |publisher=247 Sports}}</ref> During week three of the 2021 Georgia Bulldogs season, Mitchell was named SEC Freshman of the Week following a performance that saw him record four receptions for 77 yards and one touchdown vs [[South Carolina football|South Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeBary |first=Matt |date=September 20, 2021 |title=Georgia's Nolan Smith and Adonai Mitchell Earn SEC Football Weekly Honors |url=https://dawgpost.com/s/3614/georgias-nolan-smith-and-adonai-mitchell-earn-sec-football-weekly-honors |access-date=29 September 2021 |website=Dawg Post}}</ref>

He was a key part of the [[2022 College Football Playoff National Championship|2022 College Football National Championship]] victory at the end of the 2021 season, catching the go-ahead 40-yard touchdown pass from [[Stetson Bennett]] with 8 minutes remaining. During the celebration of the victory, Mitchell was interviewed by CBS Atlanta affiliate, WGCL, where he recounted the catch, "It was amazing to answer that call when it came, be that answer that the team to come through."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gagnon |first1=Emily |title=CBS 46 Atlanta |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=bOmTK_eu_Jg&feature=youtu.be |publisher=CBS 46 Atlanta |access-date=17 January 2022}}</ref> Mitchell finished the season as the Bulldogs' third-ranked receiver, totaling 29 receptions for 426 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Georgia Bulldogs Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/georgia/2021.html |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Mitchell's sophomore [[2022 Georgia Bulldogs football team|2022 season]] was hampered by injury — specifically an ankle hurt during the Bulldogs' week 2 game against [[2022 Samford Bulldogs football team|Samford]].<ref name="Hill">{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Jordan D. |date=December 4, 2022 |title=Georgia football: Kirby Smart discusses AD Mitchell’s return from injury |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia/Article/Georgia-football-Kirby-Smart-discusses-AD-Mitchells-return-from-injury-199563532/ |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref> The injury lingered throughout the season<ref name="Hill" /> and he only saw action in 6 games, catching just 9 balls for 134 yards and 3 touchdowns — numbers that would be, by far, the worst of his college career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adonai Mitchell College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adonai-mitchell-1.html |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He missed six games with the injury before making it back for the SEC title game against [[2020 LSU Tigers football team|LSU]].<ref name="Hill" /> In that game, he slipped and fell on a potential touchdown route late in the first quarter, but later managed to make his mark in the box score when he rolled out to his right on a trick two-point conversion pass, zipping a spiral to teammate [[Darnell Washington]] for the score.<ref name="Hill" />

===Texas===
Mitchell transferred to [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Erin |date=January 20, 2023 |title=Former Georgia Wide Receiver Adonai Mitchell to Transfer to Texas |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10062467-former-georgia-wide-receiver-adonai-mitchell-to-transfer-to-texas |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> He had 55 receptions for 845 yards and 11 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adonai Mitchell 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adonai-mitchell-1/gamelog/2023 |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Mitchell was selected in the second round, 52nd overall, by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2024-04-27 |title=Adonai Mitchell goes to Colts at No. 52 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/adonai-mitchell-goes-to-colts-at-no-52 |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Indianapolis received the pick in a trade with the [[Carolina Panthers]] for the 46th overall pick ([[Jonathon Brooks (American football)|Jonathon Brooks]]), the Colts in exchange receiving two fifth-round picks (No. 142: [[Anthony Gould (American football)|Anthony Gould]]) (No. 155: the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] selected [[Jeremiah Trotter Jr.]]) as well.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colts trade back with Carolina Panthers in Round 2 of 2024 NFL Draft |url=https://www.colts.com/news/2024-nfl-draft-trade-back-carolina-panthers-second-round-picks-fifth-round |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=www.colts.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Mitchell began the [[2024 NFL season|2024 season]] as a starter for the Colts, on the field for the first snap in four of his first seven contests. During that period, he was targeted 27 times but made just 10 catches for 109 total yards — drawing some attention at one point for dropping the ball in an apparent aversion to forthcoming contact.<ref name="a903">{{cite web | last=Erickson | first=Joel A. | title=Colts: Texas native Adonai Mitchell excited for chance to play at NRG | website=IndyStar | date=2024-10-24 | url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2024/10/24/colts-texas-native-adonai-mitchell-excited-for-chance-to-play-at-nrg/75813732007/#:~:text=Mitchell%20had%20to%20make%20it,that%20I've%20never%20felt. | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref> He was subsequently eased from the starting lineup with the return from injury of second-year player [[Josh Downs]], who suffered a sprained ankle during training camp. Colts receivers coach [[Reggie Wayne]] expressed complete confidence in Mitchell, attributing his miscues to normal rookie jitters.<ref name=Firm>Jake Arthur, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0i4ExzAiqiE Indianapolis Colts' Reggie Wayne Stands Firm in Defense of AD Mitchell: 'Just Keep Watching'], Locked on Colts, via YouTube.com, Oct. 10, 2024.</ref> "Just keep watching," Wayne urged.<ref name=Firm /> Mitchell ended the season with seven starts, 23 receptions, and 312 receiving yards.

In Week 4 of the [[2025 NFL season|2025 season]] against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Mitchell fumbled the ball at the end zone during his celebration, leading to a touchback instead of a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |last2=Simmons |first2= |last3= |last4= |first4= |date=September 28, 2025 |title=Adonai Mitchell loses TD from fumbled celebration out of the end zone |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/adonai-mitchell-loses-td-from-fumbled-celebration-out-of-the-end-zone |access-date=September 29, 2025 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He played a total eight games during the season before being traded.

===New York Jets===
On November 4, 2025, the Colts traded Mitchell along with two first round picks ([[2026 NFL draft|2026]] (No. 16) and [[2027 NFL draft|2027]]) to the [[New York Jets]] in exchange for cornerback [[Sauce Gardner]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets-Colts Trade {{!}} Green & White Acquire WR Adonai Mitchell & Two First-Round Picks for CB Sauce Gardner|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-colts-trade-two-first-round-picks-sauce-gardner-ad-mitchell-11-04-2025|accessdate=November 4, 2025|work=NewYorkJets.com|language=en-US|date=November 4, 2025|first=Susanna|last=Weir}}</ref>

On November 30, Mitchell recorded his first career touchdown on a 52-yard reception from quarterback [[Tyrod Taylor]] in the Jets' 27–24 win over the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Can't-Miss Play: Adonai Mitchell's first career TD catch comes on 52-yard launch from Taylor|url=https://www.nfl.com/videos/can-t-miss-play-adonai-mitchell-s-first-career-td-catch-comes-on-52-yard-launch-from-taylor|website=NFL.com|access-date=2025-11-30|language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Adetomiwa Adebawore''' ({{respell|add|E|TOMMY|wah add|E|BAR|eh}}; born March 4, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern Wildcats]] and was selected by the Colts in the fourth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Adebawore was born on March 4, 2001, in [[Kansas City, Missouri]], and attended [[North Kansas City High School]].<ref name="BeastProfile">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2023 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410190932/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 10, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=249}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ricks |first=Dhomonique |date=November 8, 2017 |title=This North KC junior and son of African royalty knows the value of hard work in the classroom, on the field and in life |url=https://fox4kc.com/news/education/this-north-kc-junior-and-son-of-african-royalty-knows-the-value-of-hard-work-in-the-classroom-on-the-field-and-in-life/ |access-date=November 17, 2022 |website=[[WDAF-TV|FOX4KC.com]]}}</ref> He was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Northwestern over offers from Washington State, Navy, and Tulane.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rich |first=Davis |date=April 17, 2018 |title=2019 defensive end Adetomiwa Adebawore commits to Northwestern |url=https://www.insidenu.com/2018/4/17/17247914/2019-defensive-end-adetomiwa-adebawore-commits-northwestern-wildcats-football-pat-fitzgerald |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=InsideNU.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Adebawore played in eight games during his freshman season at Northwestern, recording six tackles and one sack.<ref name=MG24>Hayden Clark, et al., (eds.), ''2024 Media Guide.'' Indianapolis, IN: Indianapolis Colts, Inc., 2024; unpaginated [p. 58].</ref> He became a starter for the Wildcats during his sophomore season and finished the year with 17 tackles, six tackles for loss, and two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carroll |first=Gabriela |date=November 12, 2021 |title=Football: Adetomiwa Adebawore shines for Northwestern's defense in 2021 |url=https://dailynorthwestern.com/2021/11/12/sports/football-adetomiwa-adebawore-shines-for-northwesterns-defense-in-2021/ |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=[[The Daily Northwestern]]}}</ref> Adebawore was named honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] as a junior after leading the team with 4.5 sacks and 8.5 tackles for loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dowling |first=Ignacio |date=July 28, 2022 |title=Northwestern football's most important players No. 4: Adetomiwa Adebawore |url=https://www.insidenu.com/2022/7/28/23281377/northwestern-footballs-most-important-players-no-4-adetomiwa-adebawore |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=InsideNU.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref> He was named third team All-Big Ten as a senior after recording 38 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Devin |date=February 2, 2023 |title=Senior Bowl practice: D-lineman Adetomiwa Adebawore excels, as does defensive back Darius Rush |url=https://www.inquirer.com/eagles/senior-bowl-day-3-adetomiwa-adebawore-darius-rush-20230202.html |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]}}</ref> Adebawore played in the [[2023 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinnan |first=Cory |date=February 2, 2023 |title=Reese's Senior Bowl notes and standouts from day-two |url=https://brownswire.usatoday.com/lists/browns-senior-bowl-adetomiwa-adebawore-day-two/ |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=Browns Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

'''Adisa Akil Isaac''' (born October 4, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]].

==Early life==
Isaac was born on October 4, 2001, in [[Brooklyn, New York]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/adisaisaac|title=NFL Draft Profile: Adisa Isaac, EDGE, Penn State Nittany Lions|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 29, 2022|access-date=August 23, 2023}}</ref> He attended [[Canarsie High School]] in [[Canarsie, Brooklyn]], where he played [[defensive end]] and recorded 210 tackles and 39 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moyer |first=Josh |date=November 20, 2019 |title=Why Penn State teammates already think true freshman DE Adisa Isaac is a future first-round pick |url=https://www.centredaily.com/sports/college/penn-state-university/psu-football/article237595459.html |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=Centre Daily}}</ref> He committed to [[Penn State University]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wogenrich  |first=Mark |date=2018-12-17 |title=Adisa Isaac, New York's top-ranked player, commits to Penn State |url=https://www.mcall.com/2018/12/17/adisa-isaac-new-yorks-top-ranked-player-commits-to-penn-state/ |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=The Morning Call |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pickel  |first=Greg |date=2018-12-19 |title=Adisa Isaac, one of four Penn State top-100 signees, comes with powerful pass rush |url=https://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/2018/12/adisa-isaac-one-of-four-expected-penn-state-top-100-signees-comes-with-powerful-pass-rush.html |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=PennLive.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Penn State in 2019 he played in 11 games and had 14 tackles and 1.5 sacks. As a sophomore in 2020, he had 1.5 sacks and 13 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Elton  |date=2022-09-14 |title=Penn State football | Isaac growing into role on Nittany Lions' defensive line |url=https://www.tribdem.com/sports/penn-state-football-isaac-growing-into-role-on-nittany-lions-defensive-line/article_24523561-3128-5482-baba-aa29ec0f4bde.html |access-date=2024-05-27 |website=The Tribune-Democrat |language=en}}</ref> After missing 2021 due to injury, Isaac started all 13 games in 2022, recording 28 tackles and four sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wick |first=Nolan |date=2023-01-09 |title=Defensive End Adisa Isaac Returning To Penn State For Fifth Season |url=https://onwardstate.com/2023/01/08/defensive-end-adisa-isaac-returning-to-penn-state-for-fifth-season/ |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=Onward State |language=en-US}}</ref> He returned to Penn State in 2023, rather than enter the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wick |first=Nolan |date=2023-01-09 |title=Defensive End Adisa Isaac Returning to Penn State for 2023 Season |url=https://www.statecollege.com/articles/penn-state-football/defensive-end-adisa-isaac-returning-to-penn-state-for-2023-season/ |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=StateCollege.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Adedayo Odeleye''' (born October 17, 1997)<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2023-07-27 |language=en |title=Adedayo Odeleye Biography |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/bio/_/id/5066095/adedayo-odeleye}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> is a Nigerian-British [[American football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He has previously played for the [[Berlin Thunder (ELF)|Berlin Thunder]] of the [[European League of Football]] (ELF).

== Early life ==
Odeleye was born in [[Lagos]], Nigeria and his family moved to the United Kingdom when he was nine.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Sidhu |first=Deepi |date=May 4, 2022 |title=Texans add DL Adedayo Odeleye through NFL International Player Program {{!}} Daily Brew |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-add-dl-adedayo-odeleye-through-nfl-international-player-program-daily-bre |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=HoustonTexans.com |language=en-US}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> 

==College career==
He played his first football games for [[Loughborough University]] in 2017.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |access-date=2022-05-09 |language=en |title=Adedayo Odeleye {{!}} {{!}} European League of Football |url=https://europeanleague.football/player/adedayo-odeleye |archive-date=2022-05-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220509141827/https://europeanleague.football/player/adedayo-odeleye |url-status=dead }}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":1" /> He was also active in [[Rugby football|rugby]].<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2022-05-09 |language=en |title=Texans awarded Adedayo Odeleye in NFL International Pathway program |url=https://sportstalk790.iheart.com/content/2022-05-03-texans-awarded-adedayo-odeleye-in-nfl-international-pathway-program/}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In March 2021, he was accepted into the NFL [[International Player Pathway Program]] (IPPP), but ultimately was not signed for the NFL.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2022-05-09 |date=2022-01-19 |language=en-US |title=NFL International Player Pathway spotlight: Adedayo Odeleye, DL, The UK |url=https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/nfl-international-player-pathway-spotlight-adedayo-odeleye-dl-the-uk/}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

===Berlin Thunder===
In the [[2021 European League of Football season|2021 season]], he played for the [[Berlin Thunder (ELF)|Berlin Thunder]] in the [[European League of Football]]. With 34 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] (14 for a loss), seven [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and a recovered [[Turnover (gridiron football)|fumble]] in eight games, he was selected to the ELF All Star Team.<ref name=":0"/>

===Houston Texans===
Odeleye was invited back to the NFL IPPP in 2022 and was ultimately signed by the [[Houston Texans]] for the [[2022 Houston Texans season|2022 season]].<ref>{{cite web |access-date=2022-05-09 |title="Es werden weitere Spieler folgen" |url=https://www.football-aktuell.de/cgi-bin/news.pl?artikel=16516743238028}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":1" /> He was waived on August 31, 2022, but signed to the practice squad the next day. On January 10, 2023, he signed a reserve/future contract. He was waived on August 29, 2023, but signed to the practice squad the next day. On January 29, 2024, Odeleye's contract expired with the team and was waived.

===Baltimore Ravens===
On August 30, 2024, Odeleye was signed to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign International Player to Practice Squad|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/baltimore-ravens-transaction-adedayo-odeleye-international-player-signing-practice-squad-2024|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 30, 2024}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 21, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-reserve-future-contracts-2025|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=January 21, 2025}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Odeleye was waived by the Ravens as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mink |first1=Ryan |title=5 Takeaways From Ravens Roster Cuts |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-roster-cuts-53-takeaways-2025 |website=baltimoreravens.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 27, 2025, Odeleye signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walker |first1=Patrik |title=2025 Cowboys Roster: Holden, Grier fill out practice squad |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2025-cowboys-roster-holden-others-head-to-practice-squad |website=DallasCowboys.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 6, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Holden, Childress lead group of early Cowboys 2026 signings|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/holden-childress-lead-group-of-early-cowboys-2026-signings|author=Walker, Patrik|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=January 6, 2026}}</ref>
